findings.proposed_fix: Add keepalive_idle and statement_cache_size to PgOptions (named defaults) and evict least-recently-used statements instead of clearing everything.

findings.excerpt:
/// When the connection was last handed back; used to validate stale ones.
last_used: std::time::Instant,   // written at pool.rs:148, never read anywhere
findings.problem: The field and its comment promise validation of stale pooled connections, but last_used is only ever assigned. Pool::get checks nothing but is_closed(), so connections silently dropped by a firewall are detected only on first use (partly masked by the retry loop in PgBackend::begin). The comment describes a feature that does not exist.
findings.proposed_fix: Either implement it (when an idle connection's last_used exceeds a configurable idle_validate_after, run a cheap `SELECT 1` before handing it out, discarding it on failure) or delete the field and the comment. Test by terminating idle backends (as idle_pooled_connections_that_died_are_replaced_transparently does) and asserting zero failed first uses.

findings.excerpt: const CACHE_CAP: usize = 8192;   // ... if cache.len() >= CACHE_CAP { cache.clear(); }
findings.problem: The decoded-changeset cache is bounded by a fixed count (not bytes) that an operator cannot tune, and on overflow it drops the whole cache at once (thrashing on any history walk longer than 8192 changesets). Memory per entry is unbounded because changeset size varies with ops/message limits.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the capacity a constructor argument (StoreHistory::with_capacity, wired to a server/engine config key) and evict LRU entries, optionally bounding by estimated bytes.

findings.excerpt: line.chars().take(200).collect()
findings.problem: The persisted summary length (200 chars) is a bare literal baked into stored index rows; changing it later silently produces inconsistent summaries between old and new rows unless a reindex runs, and it is not named or documented.
findings.proposed_fix: Introduce `pub const SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS: usize = 200;` documented on ChangesetInfo::summary, and make `ag reindex` rebuild summaries when it changes (or take the value from Limits).

findings.excerpt: crate::Credentials::new(env("AG_TEST_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID", "test"), env("AG_TEST_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", "test"));   // plus bucket default "ag-test" and region "us-east-1"; lib.rs:26 `pub mod testing;`
findings.problem: Test-support code with default credentials 'test'/'test', bucket 'ag-test' and panicking asserts is an unconditional `pub mod testing` of the production crate, so it is compiled into every release build of ag-storage and exported to all dependents, although the whole workspace only uses it from tests/ directories (grep of src/ outside ag-storage finds no use).
findings.proposed_fix: Gate the module with `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "testing"))]` and enable the `testing` feature only from dev-dependencies of the crates that need it; drop the credential defaults and require the AG_TEST_S3_* variables (the scripts export them).

findings.problem: A no-op ObjectLock, documented as test-only, is a public, re-exported (lib.rs:31) implementation that any caller can hand to S3ObjectStore::open, silently reintroducing the GC lost-object race. Its only user is the regression test tests/s3.rs that demonstrates the race. ManualClock (clock.rs:25) and MemoryObjectStore::corrupt_for_test (object_store.rs:150) are similar test doubles in the public production API.
findings.proposed_fix: Move NoLock (and ManualClock, corrupt_for_test) behind the `testing` feature / #[doc(hidden)] so production code cannot select them; keep the race-reproduction test using the feature.

findings.problem: Test hooks and destructive test helpers (overwrite any object with arbitrary bytes, delete the whole prefix) live on the production S3ObjectStore, and every put/delete_if_older_than takes an extra mutex and calls the hook. A test seam in the hot path of the storage engine, plus `purge_for_test` which deletes every object under the prefix, is public API of the shipped crate.
findings.proposed_fix: Compile hook/purge/corrupt helpers only under cfg(any(test, feature = "testing")) (the call sites become `#[cfg(...)] self.fire(..)`), so release builds contain neither the seam nor the destructive helpers.

findings.problem: Arbitrary-SQL execution on the transaction handle (able to rewrite the audit chain, streams, etc.), a hand-maintained table whitelist that already misses tables (meta, changeset_parents, changeset_paths, intent_objects, policies, counters, task_deps, agent_runs), and an irreversible DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE are public, always-compiled API whose stated purpose is simulating tampering in tests.
findings.proposed_fix: Put raw_execute/raw_query/exists/count_rows/drop_schema behind the `testing` feature; for decommissioning provide a deliberate, audited admin function instead of doc(hidden) pub.

findings.excerpt: Self { objects: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()), limits: Limits::default(), clock }
findings.problem: MemoryObjectStore cannot be given limits (blob-size limit is the default), unlike FsObjectStore/S3ObjectStore, so an embedded repository using it (Repository::ephemeral) silently ignores configured Limits.
findings.proposed_fix: Add MemoryObjectStore::with_limits(clock, limits) and use it from Repository::ephemeral.

findings.problem: When the conditional UPDATE matches no row, the error reports `actual` as the same number as `expected`, a made-up value (the real stored version is not read), producing a self-contradictory 'expected version N, found N' message exactly in the race case the CAS exists for.
findings.proposed_fix: Re-read the stream row and report its real version (or NotFound if it vanished). Cover with a test that bypasses the write lock (two raw connections) to force the UPDATE-affected-0 path.

findings.problem: The doc says 'Delivered events' but the query has no `dispatched_at IS NOT NULL` filter, so it returns pending and failed events too; callers relying on 'history' for replay get undelivered events mixed in.
findings.proposed_fix: Either add the filter (and a second method for all events) or correct the doc and rename to outbox_recent; assert in outbox_is_at_least_once that a pending event is not returned as delivered.

findings.excerpt:
/// Records a failed delivery attempt (the event stays pending).
pub fn outbox_fail(&self, id: u64, error: &str) -> Result<(), MetaError> {   [consumer: ag-integrate/src/derive.rs:46-47 `// Notification-only topics have no in-process consumer. _ => Ok(()),` then outbox_ack]
findings.problem: The outbox is advertised as at-least-once delivery, but a failed event stays pending forever: no max attempts, no backoff, no dead-letter state, and outbox_pending orders by id with a LIMIT, so `limit` permanently failing events at the head block every later event (head-of-line blocking). On the success side the only consumer acknowledges unknown/notification topics without delivering them anywhere, marking them 'dispatched'. Both ends look like delivery but are not.
findings.proposed_fix: Add next_attempt_at + max_attempts (dead-letter state, surfaced by `ag doctor`/metrics) to the outbox table via migration 0003 for both backends, make outbox_pending skip events whose next_attempt_at is in the future, and make real consumers (SSE/webhook dispatch) ack only on actual delivery. Test with a poisoned event followed by healthy ones.

findings.problem: Several mutators ignore the affected-row count and return Ok(()) when nothing matched (ack/fail of an unknown outbox id, replacing the payload of a non-existent intent, staging an object for an intent that does not exist), unlike their siblings (run_finish, lease_release, workspace_update ...) which return NotFound. A wrong id is silently a successful no-op, hiding logic errors and, for intent_add_object, leaving GC protection records that protect nothing.
findings.proposed_fix: Check the execute() row count and return MetaError::NotFound for 0 rows (and verify the intent exists in intent_add_object); add negative tests.

findings.excerpt: state           TEXT NOT NULL,   -- intents.state; same for proposals.state (137), reviews.decision (149), attestations.result (161), agent_runs.status (206), tasks.state (216), queue.state (265); postgres/0001_init.sql:86,146,158,170,215,225,274. Contrast jobs: 0002_jobs.sql:12 CHECK (state IN (...))
findings.problem: Every state machine except jobs is an unconstrained TEXT column, and the Rust API takes free strings (proposal_set_state(&str) records.rs:254, run_finish(&str) agents.rs:314, queue_finish(&str) agents.rs:565, task_update(.., state: Option<&str>) agents.rs:363, review_add(decision: &str), attestation result). Valid values exist only in doc comments, so a typo or a malicious/buggy caller can persist an invalid state that later parsing (IntentState::from_str) rejects as 'metadata corruption'. The enumerations are enforced nowhere at the storage layer.
findings.proposed_fix: Add migration 0003 (both backends) with CHECK constraints for each enumeration (SQLite needs table rebuilds; PostgreSQL ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT), replace the &str parameters with enums (ProposalState, RunStatus, TaskState, QueueState, Decision, AttestationResult) and test that invalid values are rejected on both real backends.

findings.excerpt: WHERE i.state NOT IN ('published','integrated','rejected','failed','aborted') OR i.updated_at >= ?1
findings.problem: The list of terminal intent states is duplicated as a SQL literal instead of derived from IntentState::is_terminal; adding or reclassifying a state updates one place and silently breaks GC protection of staged objects in the other.
findings.proposed_fix: Generate the SQL list from IntentState::ALL.filter(is_terminal) (as intents_in_states already does for its list) and add a test that the generated list equals the enum's terminal set.

findings.problem: Every error (connection lost, Retriable, decode failure, hash mismatch) is converted to None without a log line or counter. A broken or corrupt cache and a dead database look identical to a cold cache, so the system silently degrades to full replay and operators have no signal; `ag verify` is the only detector.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the miss semantics but count and log non-NotFound errors (a metric `derived_tree_cache_errors_total` and a warn-level log), and have `ag doctor`/verify report cached trees that fail verification.

findings.excerpt:
//! * [`Meta`] is the strongly consistent metadata store (SQLite in WAL mode
//!   with `synchronous=FULL`): the changeset index, streams, ...
findings.problem: The crate-level documentation describes the metadata store as SQLite only, although PostgreSQL is a first-class backend (meta/mod.rs:1, ADR-0004) and the same paragraph's guarantees (WAL, synchronous=FULL) do not apply to it.
findings.proposed_fix: Reword: 'SQLite (WAL, synchronous=FULL) or PostgreSQL (advisory-lock-serialized writers, REPEATABLE READ readers)' and link to docs/operations/postgres-and-s3.md.

findings.problem: For SQLite a Meta owns one Connection behind a Mutex, and read() holds that mutex for the whole read transaction, so within one Meta handle readers serialize with each other and with writers; the statement that readers are not serialized is only true across handles/processes. The server compensates with a pool of reopened handles (ag-server/src/repos.rs:181), which is not mentioned in the storage docs.
findings.proposed_fix: Document the per-handle behaviour (and the need for one handle per concurrent reader, as RepoPool does), or open a small read-only connection pool inside Meta for SQLite so concurrent reads really are not serialized; add a test with a long reader and a concurrent reader on one handle.

findings.excerpt: let size = xml::first_text(c, "Size").and_then(|s| s.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(0);
findings.problem: A missing or unparseable <Size> in a ListObjectsV2 entry becomes size 0 silently, whereas a missing LastModified in the very same loop is a hard error. ObjectInfo.size feeds inventory/verify output and quota accounting, so a malformed listing is reported as empty objects.
findings.proposed_fix: Treat a missing or non-numeric Size like LastModified: return StoreError::Remote('list: no usable Size for <key>').

findings.excerpt: fn job_by_key(&self, key: &str) -> Result<Option<JobRow>, MetaError> {   [consumer: ag-server/src/api/jobs.rs:133 `tx.job_list(None, 1000)?.into_iter().find(|j| j.dedupe_key.as_deref() == Some(&key))`]
findings.problem: The dedupe lookup is private, so the server emulates it by scanning the newest 1000 jobs. Once a validation job is older than the 1000 newest, the scan misses it, the enqueue path falls through to job_enqueue (which does dedupe in storage) but also emits the 'enqueued' metric and a second job.enqueue audit event for work that was not enqueued.
findings.proposed_fix: Make it `pub fn job_by_dedupe_key` (indexed by the UNIQUE dedupe_key) and use it in ag-server instead of the capped scan; add a server test with >1000 jobs asserting no duplicate audit event.

findings.problem: Without the environment variables the real-backend tests print a notice and report PASS (about 30 tests), so a plain `cargo test` shows green for tests that exercised nothing. CI protects itself with AG_REQUIRE_BACKENDS=1 but local runs and any CI job that forgets the flag silently lose the PostgreSQL/S3/TLS/object-lock coverage.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the harness start the real servers itself when the variables are unset (spawn the throwaway postgres cluster and MinIO from the test binary, as scripts/pg-test.sh and s3-test.sh do) or mark these tests #[ignore] with a reason so they show as ignored rather than passed; default AG_REQUIRE_BACKENDS to on in CI via the workflow-level env.

findings.excerpt: scope: serde_json::from_str(&scope_json).unwrap_or_default(),
findings.problem: A credential whose stored scope_json cannot be parsed silently gets the default CredentialScope, which Scope::from_wire/Scope::permits treat as UNRESTRICTED (empty repos/streams/operations = any). A damaged row or schema drift therefore widens a narrowly scoped agent credential to everything its subject's roles allow. Fail-open swallowed error in the authentication path.
findings.proposed_fix: Make row_to_credential return rusqlite::Error::FromSqlConversionFailure on a parse error so Authenticator::authenticate fails closed (log the credential id, answer unauthenticated/internal). Add CHECK (json_valid(scope_json)) to the credentials table. Add an integration test that corrupts scope_json in a real control.db and asserts the token is rejected, never accepted unrestricted.

findings.excerpt: quota: serde_json::from_str(&quota).unwrap_or_default(),
findings.problem: An unparsable quota_json silently becomes the default Quota, i.e. every limit 0 = unlimited (object bytes, streams, open proposals, per-repo rate limit). A corrupt row disables all quota enforcement for that repository without any signal.
findings.proposed_fix: Propagate the parse error (FromSqlConversionFailure) and refuse to serve the repository with a logged internal error; add CHECK (json_valid(quota_json)); test with a corrupted row.

findings.excerpt: control.add_object_bytes(&name, size as i64)?;
findings.problem: The repository object quota (quota.max_total_object_bytes) is checked and accounted ONLY in App::store_object (the object upload path). add_object_bytes has no other caller. Blobs and changesets written through virtual workspaces (api/workspaces.rs:112 workspace_modify with inline VirtualContent::Bytes), and everything else that writes through the engine, are neither counted nor limited, so a writer can exceed the quota arbitrarily with repeated /workspaces/{name}/changes calls (8 MiB per request, unlimited requests). Docs advertise repository quotas as done (docs/architecture/adr-traceability.md:89). object_bytes is also never reconciled except by a manual non-dry-run GC (admin.rs:146).
findings.proposed_fix: Enforce the quota where bytes actually enter the repository: account and check in workspace_modify/modify_workspace (and any other writer) or, better, in a quota-aware wrapper around the repository's ObjectStore so every put is counted. Add periodic reconciliation (set_object_bytes from objects().list()) instead of GC-only. Verify with a real-server test that uploads through the workspace API past max_total_object_bytes and expects quota_exceeded.

findings.excerpt: max_object_bytes: 0,
findings.problem: Quota.max_object_bytes (proto field 2, accepted by PATCH /v1/repos/{owner}/{rname} and stored/returned) is never enforced anywhere: objects.rs:41 and http.rs:402 use only the global cfg.limits.max_object_bytes. default_quota also hardcodes max_object_bytes/max_streams/requests_per_second/burst to 0 and config.rs only offers defaults for max_open_proposals and max_total_object_bytes, so operators cannot set a default for the other quota fields.
findings.proposed_fix: Enforce the per-repo max_object_bytes in ObjectSink::push and store_object (use min(global, repo quota)); add [limits] defaults for max_object_bytes, max_streams, requests_per_second and burst and use them in default_quota; test through the real HTTP server.

findings.excerpt: if max_streams > 0 && repo.meta().read(|tx| tx.list_streams())?.len() as u32 >= max_streams {
findings.problem: Quota checks are check-then-act and not atomic: max_streams (here), max_open_proposals (proposals.rs:27-28, which also loads up to 100_000 rows to count) and the object quota (objects.rs:88-111, where used bytes are read outside the write and before authorization) all race under concurrent requests, so quotas can be exceeded. Documented as 'approximate' only for object_bytes.
findings.proposed_fix: Perform the count and the insert in one metadata transaction (or a SQL-level conditional insert) so the quota is enforced atomically; for object bytes use an atomic reserve (UPDATE ... SET object_bytes = object_bytes + ?2 WHERE object_bytes + ?2 <= max) before writing and roll back on failure.

findings.excerpt: WHERE (?1 IS NULL OR subject = ?1) AND (?2 IS NULL OR repo = ?2) ORDER BY subject, repo, role LIMIT 5000",
findings.problem: all_bindings() (the source of every authorization decision) calls roles(None, None), which silently truncates at 5000 rows ordered by subject. The comment says 'Bindings are few' but nothing enforces it: bindings beyond the 5000th (late subjects alphabetically) are silently ignored, so those users are denied or get not_found with no error. Same pattern: credentials() LIMIT 1000 (line 248) silently truncates list_credentials and the may_manage_credential scan; all_bindings (line 324) also silently drops rows with an unknown role via filter_map.
findings.proposed_fix: Give all_bindings its own unlimited query (or fail loudly when more rows than a documented, configurable cap exist) and log/skip-with-warning on unknown roles; paginate credentials/roles listings with page tokens instead of a hidden LIMIT. Test with 6000 bindings against a real control.db.

findings.excerpt: || (!inner.is_empty() && inner.raw().iter().all(|p| outer.matches(p) || outer.raw().contains(p)))
findings.problem: Scope::contains decides whether a delegated credential's pattern is a subset of its minter's by matching the inner pattern's SOURCE TEXT as a literal string against the outer glob. That is not glob inclusion and is unsound: outer repos=['acme/*b*'] 'contains' inner ['acme/[ab]*'] because the literal text 'acme/[ab]*' matches 'acme/*b*', yet the inner pattern also matches 'acme/alpha', which the outer does not. A narrowly scoped token can therefore mint a wider one, breaking the 'a credential can never exceed its minter' guarantee (docs/protocol/agwp-v1.md). The same literal-pattern-as-repo-name trick is used for CredentialsMint/CredentialsRevoke checks in api/admin.rs:200 and :259.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with a real containment check: restrict scope patterns to a decidable grammar (literal segments with a single trailing '*' or a bare '*') validated at mint time, and implement prefix/segment containment on that grammar; reject character classes, '?', '{}' in scopes and bindings. For admin checks, verify the minter's role pattern contains the requested pattern with the same function. Add property tests comparing against brute-force enumeration over a name universe.

findings.excerpt: Glob::new(pattern).map(|g| g.compile_matcher().is_match(value)).unwrap_or(false)
findings.problem: An invalid glob in a stored role binding silently never matches. Bindings are not validated on creation: api/admin.rs:335-337 (grant_role) only checks the role and that subject is non-empty, and main.rs:213-214 (admin grant) validates nothing, so typos create permanently inert bindings that look granted in list_roles. The glob is also recompiled for every binding on every request.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate subject and repo patterns (Patterns::new / Glob::new plus subject shape user:/agent:/service:/group:) in Control::grant_role and the API, return invalid_argument; cache compiled matchers inside the bindings cache.

findings.excerpt: let mut cfg = ServerConfig::default();
findings.problem: The offline `ag-server admin` command builds its App from ServerConfig::default() and has no --config flag, so it ignores the real configuration. `admin create-repo` therefore always creates SQLite+filesystem repositories even when the server is configured with [repos.storage] PostgreSQL/S3 (the shipped compose setup), producing repositories the server would later open with the wrong backend/layout; it also ignores repos.default_stream and the limits.* quota defaults (main.rs:245 passes v1::Quota::default()), and the auth ttl caps.
findings.proposed_fix: Add --config/AG_SERVER_CONFIG to `admin` and load the same ServerConfig as `serve`; use the repository defaults (default_quota, default_stream, storage template) in create-repo. Verify against the compose PostgreSQL/MinIO stack that `admin create-repo` yields a repo in its own schema/prefix.

findings.excerpt: expires_at_ms: now + i64::from(ttl) * 1000,
findings.problem: `admin mint` accepts any u32 ttl (default 3600, up to ~136 years) and never applies auth.max_ttl_secs / auth.max_agent_ttl_secs that the API enforces (api/admin.rs:217-224), contradicting the docs ('always expiring', agents <= 1 h). Combined with the default-config issue above the caps cannot even be read.
findings.proposed_fix: Load the config in admin and apply the same per-kind max TTL as App::mint_credential (share one function).

findings.excerpt:
meta_backend: "sqlite".into(),
        object_backend: "fs".into(),
        durability: String::new(),
        stream_count: 0,
        changeset_count: 0,
findings.problem: row_to_wire fills canned values: backend names 'sqlite'/'fs' and zero stream/changeset counts and empty durability. create_repo and every entry of list_repos return these as if true, even for repositories on PostgreSQL/S3 (only describe_repo overwrites them at lines 124-128). Clients (Web UI repo list, SDKs) see wrong backends and 0 streams/changesets.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive meta_backend/object_backend from the effective storage template (cfg.repos.storage / the repo's stored config) in row_to_wire, and either compute counts for listings or make the fields optional/omitted when not computed (do not emit 0). Test with a Postgres/S3 repo in tests/storage_backends.rs asserting list and create report the real backends.

findings.excerpt: pub public_url: Option<String>,
findings.problem: Documented as 'Externally visible base URL (for links in responses and OIDC redirects)' but it is never read anywhere in the repository (only declared and defaulted); no response contains links and there are no OIDC redirects (the server validates bearer tokens only). A dead configuration knob advertising features that do not exist; openapi.json also hardcodes servers [{"url":"/"}] (routes.rs:263).
findings.proposed_fix: Either remove the field (deny_unknown_fields will then reject stale configs) or implement it: use it for the OpenAPI servers entry, absolute links and the OIDC redirect login flow planned in the web product, and validate it as an absolute http(s) URL.

findings.excerpt: const MAX_MESSAGE: usize = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
findings.problem: gRPC decode/encode size is a fixed 16 MiB, unrelated to the configurable limits.max_request_bytes (default 8 MiB) that the HTTP transport honours (http.rs:100) and that Negotiate advertises (session.rs:41). Lowering max_request_bytes does not restrict gRPC; raising it above 16 MiB has no effect on gRPC while clients are told otherwise.
findings.proposed_fix: Pass cfg.limits.max_request_bytes (and chunk-size aware limits for ObjectService) into router() and use it for max_decoding/encoding_message_size; test that a gRPC request above the configured limit gets too_large.

findings.excerpt:
max_changeset_ops: 100_000,
                max_changesets_per_publication: 10_000,
findings.problem: Negotiate advertises engine limits as duplicated literals instead of reading them from the engine (ag_types::Limits::default() has the same numbers today, so they can silently drift). The engine limits themselves are not configurable by an operator: ag-integrate/src/repo.rs:140 uses Limits::default() for every repository, so max_ops, max_dag_depth, max_tree_entries, max_blob_size etc. cannot be tuned from [limits].
findings.proposed_fix: Add the engine Limits to the server config ([limits.engine]) and pass them into Repository::open; build the Negotiate limits from that same value (single source of truth) and add a test that the advertised and enforced values agree.

findings.excerpt: if Authorizer::roles(p, std::slice::from_ref(b), &b.repo.replace('*', "x")).contains(&b.role) {
findings.problem: whoami computes the caller's roles by replacing '*' in each binding's repo pattern with the literal 'x' and testing that fake repository name. This is wrong for patterns with '?', character classes or alternation (a binding like 'acme/{web,api}' or 'acme/[ab]' never matches its own substituted text), so the reported role list silently omits roles the caller really holds, and it can include roles that only apply to a different name.
findings.proposed_fix: Report bindings that apply to the principal by matching on the SUBJECT only (subject_ok in Authorizer::roles) and return the repo pattern as stored; do not synthesize a repository name.

findings.excerpt: .unwrap_or(Outcome::Invalid { reason: format!("operation is {} and has no result yet", i.state) });
findings.problem: For an integrate operation without a (parsable) stored result, GetOperation fabricates an IntegrationOutcome with status 'invalid' and a prose reason. A pending/in-flight operation or a result that fails to deserialize (error swallowed by .ok() on line 302) is reported to clients as a terminal 'invalid' outcome rather than as pending/unknown, which breaks the documented 'ask for the outcome after deadline_exceeded' protocol.
findings.proposed_fix: Return outcome: None with the operation state ('pending'/'applying') when there is no result, and an internal error (logged with request id) when a stored result fails to parse; add a test that polls an operation mid-flight.

findings.excerpt: Ok((tx.audit_after(after_seq, limit.saturating_mul(4).max(limit))?, latest))
findings.problem: Topic-filtered event reads fetch only 4*limit raw audit rows and then filter. subscribe() (lines 137-140: 'else if batch.latest_seq > st.cursor { st.cursor = batch.latest_seq; }') treats an empty filtered window as 'only filtered-out events arrived' and jumps the cursor to the latest sequence, permanently skipping matching events that lie beyond the 1024-row window (e.g. a burst of >1024 non-matching audit entries followed by a matching one). replay() returns a short/empty page that clients read as 'no more events'. This violates the documented 'loses nothing' resume guarantee.
findings.proposed_fix: Push the topic filter into the audit query (WHERE action matches) or loop until `limit` matching events are found or the log is exhausted, and only advance the cursor to the last row actually examined. Add a test with >1024 non-matching entries between matching events through a real server.

findings.excerpt: let existing = tx.job_list(None, 1000)?.into_iter().find(|j| j.dedupe_key.as_deref() == Some(&key));
findings.problem: Job de-duplication looks for an existing job only among the 1000 most recent jobs, and existing_validation_jobs (line 167) only among 500. Once a repository has more jobs than that, duplicates are silently enqueued and 'pending' validations are not reported. Also rebuild_job_index uses repos("","",100_000) and count_queued_jobs caps at 1000 per repository (the /metrics gauge is a hint, per metrics.rs:34).
findings.proposed_fix: Look the job up by dedupe_key with an indexed query (job_by_dedupe_key) instead of scanning a limited list; paginate rebuild_job_index; count queued jobs with COUNT(*).

findings.excerpt: match tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || control.kv_get("ready-probe")).await {
findings.problem: /readyz only reads a sentinel key from the local SQLite control database. It does not check the configured PostgreSQL metadata or S3 object backends and keeps answering 'ready' after shutdown begins, although docs (deployment.md) tell operators to 'watch /readyz' and Kubernetes uses it for traffic routing. /healthz (line 39) is an unconditional 'ok' (acceptable for liveness only).
findings.proposed_fix: Readiness should ping the storage backends of a configured template (SELECT 1 on PostgreSQL, HEAD bucket on S3) with a short timeout and return 503 once app.begin_shutdown() has been called; integration-test against the compose PostgreSQL/MinIO.

findings.excerpt: h2.graceful_shutdown(Some(std::time::Duration::from_secs(20)));
findings.problem: The TLS path hardcodes a 20 s graceful-shutdown deadline while the plaintext path (axum::serve ... with_graceful_shutdown, line 213) waits indefinitely; neither is configurable and k8s terminationGracePeriod cannot be matched to it.
findings.proposed_fix: Add server.shutdown_grace_secs (default documented) and apply the same deadline to both listeners.

findings.excerpt: app.cfg.server.cors_origins.iter().filter_map(|o| HeaderValue::from_str(o).ok()).collect();
findings.problem: Invalid CORS origins are silently dropped; if every entry is invalid the layer allows nothing and browser clients fail with no diagnostic. ServerConfig::validate does not check cors_origins. Allowed methods/headers and max_age(600) are fixed.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate cors_origins in ServerConfig::validate (absolute origin, no path, or '*' explicitly) and fail startup on a bad entry; optionally make max_age configurable.

findings.excerpt: if let Some(expected) = std::env::var(&app.cfg.metrics.token_env).ok().filter(|t| !t.is_empty()) {
findings.problem: Borderline (documented): when the token variable is unset or empty, /metrics is served without authentication on any address; main.rs:172-181 only logs a warning for non-loopback binds. The shipped container configs listen on 0.0.0.0, so forgetting the secret fails open.
findings.proposed_fix: Add metrics.require_token (default true when the listener is non-loopback) so the server refuses to start or disables /metrics unless a token is set or the operator explicitly opts out.

findings.excerpt: let tls = axum_server::tls_rustls::RustlsConfig::from_pem_file(cert, key).await?;
findings.problem: TLS material is loaded once at startup: certificates cannot be rotated without a restart (renewal every 60-90 days), and there is no way to set a minimum TLS version or require client certificates (mTLS).
findings.proposed_fix: Reload with RustlsConfig::reload_from_pem_file on SIGHUP or file change, add server.tls_client_ca / tls_min_version options, and test rotation with rcgen certificates against the real listener.

findings.excerpt: let ttl = if req.ttl_secs == 0 { max.min(if is_agent { 3600 } else { 24 * 3600 }) } else { req.ttl_secs };
findings.problem: Default lifetimes of minted credentials (1 h for agents, 24 h otherwise) are magic numbers with no configuration key (only the maxima are configurable); the description cap take(200) at line 236 is also a bare literal.
findings.proposed_fix: Add auth.default_agent_ttl_secs and auth.default_ttl_secs (validated <= the maxima) and a named constant for the description limit.

findings.problem: Empty branch that evaluates a condition and does nothing; dead code that reads like a missing check. The same file has a redundant branch in list_credentials (line 283: `if out.is_empty() && subject != "*" && subject != me { return Ok(...out) }` followed by an identical Ok(...)) whose comment claims special privacy handling that does not exist.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete both branches (or implement the intended check) and add tests proving self-minting only narrows and that listing another subject's credentials reveals nothing.

findings.excerpt: //! Each caller (credential, falling back to identity) has a token bucket;
findings.problem: The doc says the bucket falls back to identity, but App::rate_limit (app.rs:320) always keys on 'cred:{credential_id}'. For OIDC tokens the id is the per-token jti, so one user minting/refreshing tokens gets a fresh full bucket each time (limit bypass) and the bucket map grows; for the bootstrap token everyone shares one bucket. Unauthenticated/failed-auth traffic is never rate limited (limiting runs after authentication), and the pre-auth /v1/capabilities route bypasses dispatch entirely (no limiting or shedding).
findings.proposed_fix: Key the limiter on the principal identity (optionally also per credential) as documented, rate limit failed authentications per remote address, and route negotiate through the concurrency gate.

findings.problem: Bucket-eviction threshold (50_000) and idle age (300 s) are unnamed, untunable literals; with >50_000 active callers the O(n) retain runs on every request under the global mutex.
findings.proposed_fix: Name and document the constants (or make them config), run eviction on a timer instead of per request.

findings.excerpt:
const KEY_REFRESH_MIN_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
const KEY_MAX_AGE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(3600);
findings.problem: JWKS refresh interval/max age (24-25), the 10 s HTTP timeout for discovery and JWKS (line 80) and the clock-skew leeway (`validation.leeway = 30`, line 185) are fixed and not configurable per provider. load_jwks also holds the key-cache mutex across the blocking network call, so one slow identity provider stalls every OIDC authentication.
findings.proposed_fix: Add per-provider jwks_refresh_secs, http_timeout_secs and leeway_secs to [[auth.oidc]] and fetch the JWKS outside the lock (singleflight).

findings.excerpt:
let raw_name = claims[self.cfg.username_claim.as_str()]
            .as_str()
            .or_else(|| claims["sub"].as_str())
findings.problem: Borderline (identity mapping): the identity is user:<preferred_username> taken from a mutable, provider-controlled claim, with lossy character mapping (any other character -> '-', truncated to 128 chars) and no issuer namespace. 'alice smith' and 'alice-smith' collapse to one identity, and with two [[auth.oidc]] providers the same username on a different issuer receives the same roles/bindings.
findings.proposed_fix: Namespace identities per provider (e.g. user:<issuer-alias>/<name> or a configurable identity_prefix), prefer the immutable sub (or require email_verified) and reject instead of silently rewriting names that contain disallowed characters; test with two providers issuing the same username.

findings.problem: Exporter queue, batch size, flush interval and POST timeout are fixed and cannot be tuned under telemetry.*; spans beyond the queue are dropped. SpanContext::traceparent() (line 251, 'to hand to downstream calls') has no caller and the response never carries the trace id.
findings.proposed_fix: Expose queue/batch/flush/timeout under [telemetry] with validation, and either use traceparent() (return it as a response header / put trace_id in log spans) or delete it.

findings.excerpt: /// W3C `traceparent`, passed through to logs.
findings.problem: Neither Ingress.traceparent nor the trace id reaches the logs: the per-request span (app.rs:207) records only op, request_id and transport. docs/protocol/agwp-v1.md:68 repeats the claim ('`traceparent` is propagated into logs and traces'); only the OTLP exporter uses it.
findings.proposed_fix: Add trace_id (from the incoming or newly sampled context) to the request log span, or correct the docs and the field comment.

findings.excerpt:
/// Peer address, for logs.
    pub remote: Option<String>,
findings.problem: Ingress.remote is never read by anything (not logged, not audited), and for HTTP it is always None (http.rs:61 callers pass None; the ConnectInfo<SocketAddr> service wiring in server.rs:208/212 is never extracted). Failed authentications and audit entries therefore carry no source address.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract ConnectInfo<SocketAddr> (and optionally a trusted X-Forwarded-For allow-list) in the HTTP handlers, include remote in the request log span and in auth-failure warnings.

findings.excerpt: const BINDINGS_TTL: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5);
findings.problem: Role-binding cache TTL (5 s) is fixed; it bounds how long a revoked role (granted/revoked by the offline `admin` CLI in another process, or another replica) stays effective, but cannot be tuned. Likewise the retry hints are literals: .with_retry_after(250) (app.rs:243) and .with_retry_after(200) (error.rs:136).
findings.proposed_fix: Add limits.bindings_cache_ttl_ms and limits.shed_retry_after_ms to configuration; derive the contention hint from the engine.

findings.excerpt: //! Server configuration (TOML file + environment overrides).
findings.problem: There are no environment overrides of configuration values: the environment supplies only secrets (bootstrap/metrics/OTLP-header tokens) and AG_SERVER_CONFIG/AG_DATA_DIR/AG_HEALTHCHECK_URL for the CLI. validate() also misses several settings: telemetry.log_format (anything other than 'json' silently means text, main.rs:109), limits.burst = 0 with a rate set (silently 1), repos.default_stream (only fails later on every create_repo), cors_origins, jwks_file existence, and zero values of max_request_bytes/max_object_bytes.
findings.proposed_fix: Implement AG_* env overrides for the documented keys (or correct the doc), and extend validate() with the missing checks (enum for log_format, StreamName::new(default_stream), file existence for jwks_file/tls files, non-zero limits).

findings.excerpt: #[arg(long, env = "AG_HEALTHCHECK_URL", default_value = "http://127.0.0.1:8080")]
findings.problem: The container healthcheck defaults to port 8080 and plain HTTP instead of deriving the probe URL from the server config; a deployment with another listen port or with TLS in the server (tls_cert set) reports 'unreachable' unless the operator also sets AG_HEALTHCHECK_URL.
findings.proposed_fix: Accept --config/AG_SERVER_CONFIG in healthcheck and derive scheme/host/port from [server] (https plus trust of the configured certificate when TLS is on).

findings.excerpt: ing.deadline_ms = Some(u64::MAX / 4);
findings.problem: Sentinel 'no deadline' for SSE subscriptions (same at grpc.rs:487). Related: a client-supplied Request-Timeout/grpc-timeout is accepted with no upper bound (http.rs:76, app.rs:255-257), so limits.default_deadline_ms is only a default, not a ceiling; an operator cannot cap request lifetime. Request-id generation falls back to the constant "req_unknown" if the RNG fails (http.rs:57, grpc.rs:60), giving every request the same id.
findings.proposed_fix: Add limits.max_deadline_ms (clamp client values) and an explicit Option/enum for 'streaming, no deadline' instead of a magic number; fail the request or use a counter-based fallback when random_id fails.

findings.excerpt: fn chunks(object_id: String, bytes: Vec<u8>) -> BoxStream<v1::ObjectChunk> {
findings.problem: 'objects.chunked' is advertised as streaming, but both directions are fully buffered: downloads load the whole object (up to 256 MiB) via get_object and then slice it into 1 MiB chunks (copying again with to_vec); uploads accumulate the whole object in ObjectSink.current (objects.rs:19,39) before verification, and HTTP PUT collects the body into a Vec (http.rs:404-414). With max_concurrent_requests = 512 the worst-case memory is ~128 GiB with no global in-flight-bytes budget.
findings.proposed_fix: Stream to/from the ObjectStore with incremental hashing, or add a global byte-budget semaphore sized by config ([limits] max_inflight_object_bytes) and document that chunking is a transport detail.

findings.problem: Operational timing/paging limits are scattered literals that an operator cannot tune and that duplicate ag_protocol::limits: job lease defaults (jobs.rs:35-37), long-poll waits (jobs.rs:37, streams.rs:14), SSE heartbeat 15 s/min 1 s and 500 ms poll (events.rs:95,166), SSE keep-alive 25 s (http.rs:1320), control DB busy_timeout 30 s (control.rs:159), and per-endpoint page caps 100/1000/500/5000 in admin.rs:103, streams.rs:121, events.rs:76, agents.rs:138, objects.rs:175 (verify limit 1000) that silently clamp.
findings.proposed_fix: Centralize these in ag_protocol::limits / a [limits] config block with documented defaults and surface the effective values in Negotiate.

findings.problem: All OIDC coverage runs against an in-process axum fake identity provider signing with throw-away Ed25519 fixtures; no test or CI job exercises a real provider (Keycloak/Dex: RS256, kid rotation, real discovery over TLS). docs/guides/sdks.md:527 admits 'TLS and OIDC against a real provider' are not covered. findings.excerpt: | Limits on blobs, ops, DAG depth, requests | ✅ request size, concurrency, per-credential rate limits and repository quotas on the server |
findings.problem: Marks repository quotas as fully done, but per-repo max_object_bytes is not enforced, workspace writes bypass the object quota, quotas are non-atomic, and defaults for most quota fields are not configurable (see findings above). docs/architecture/security.md:72 (the 'Availability' known-limit says there is no rate limiting or quota system, 'those belong to the server') and its 'planned server mode' text in the Known limits section are stale in the other direction: the server exists and none of its authn/authz/rate-limit/quota controls appear in the Controls table.

findings.problem: The topic filter is applied in Rust after reading only limit*4 (1024) audit rows. If none of those rows match the topics, the subscriber cursor is moved to the log's latest_seq, so matching events that sit beyond the 1024-row window are skipped permanently. replay() has the same root cause: it returns an empty page with latest_seq, so a client believes it is caught up. This breaks the documented guarantee 'A subscriber that was away loses nothing' (docs/protocol/agwp-v1.md events section) for any topic-filtered feed during bursts of non-matching events (job.claim, lease.acquire, ...).
findings.proposed_fix: Filter by topic in SQL (audit_after_topics(after_seq, topics, limit) with action = t OR action LIKE t || '.%') or loop in events_after until limit matches are found or the log is exhausted; only advance the cursor to the last row actually scanned, never to latest_seq. Add a test with >1024 non-matching events followed by one matching event and assert delivery over both SSE and replay.

findings.excerpt:
if st.call.principal.expires_at_ms > 0
    && st.app.clock.now().as_millis() >= st.call.principal.expires_at_ms
findings.problem: The doc comment (events.rs:83) says the stream ends 'when the credential expires or access is revoked' and http.rs:1298 says the feed 're-checks access on every batch'. The loop only re-checks expiry of the Principal snapshot taken at connect time and role bindings via with_repo; it never re-reads the credential row, so a credential revoked with DELETE /v1/credentials/{id} ('Revokes a credential immediately') keeps receiving the repository's audit feed (actors, targets, details) until it expires - up to 30 days for non-agent tokens.
findings.proposed_fix: On each loop iteration (or at least every few seconds) re-validate the credential: for AuthMethod::Token call control.credential(id) and end the stream with Unauthenticated if revoked_at_ms is set; for OIDC rely on exp. Add a test that mints a token, opens SSE, revokes the credential and asserts the stream terminates with an error event.

Fail-open on a security attenuation.

findings.excerpt: let max = self.app.cfg.limits.max_object_bytes;   (and repository.rs:34 `max_object_bytes: 0,`)
findings.problem: The per-repository Quota has max_object_bytes (proto Quota.max_object_bytes, settable through repo.configure; docs say 'a repository may carry a quota of its own'), but it is never read: uploads (grpc ObjectSink and HTTP PUT) only enforce the global cfg.limits.max_object_bytes. Quota.max_streams, max_open_proposals, max_total_object_bytes and requests_per_second/burst are enforced; this one is silently ignored.
findings.proposed_fix: Read the repo's quota in upload_sink/store_object and reject objects larger than min(global, quota.max_object_bytes) when it is > 0 (TooLarge / QuotaExceeded). Add a test configuring a 1 KiB repo quota and uploading 2 KiB.

findings.problem: The quota check uses a snapshot of object_bytes read before the engine call (and via a blocking SQLite call on the async worker); concurrent uploads each see the same `used`, so a repository can exceed max_total_object_bytes by (concurrency x object size). The counter itself is updated in a separate step after the put, so a crash leaves it permanently off ('approximate' per control.rs).
findings.proposed_fix: Reserve bytes atomically in the control DB (UPDATE repos SET object_bytes = object_bytes + ?size WHERE name = ? AND (?max = 0 OR object_bytes + ?size <= ?max)), roll back on failure, run it in spawn_blocking, and let gc/fsck recount. Add a concurrent-upload test.

max_changeset_ops: 100_000,

findings.problem: Negotiate advertises two limits as literals instead of the values the engine enforces (ag_types::limits::Limits::default() / Repository::limits(): max_ops 100_000, max_changesets_per_publication 10_000). They agree today by coincidence and will drift silently as soon as the engine limit changes or is made configurable, making the advertised protocol contract false.
findings.proposed_fix: Fill them from ag_types::limits::Limits::default() (or the server's configured Limits) and add a test asserting the advertised values equal the engine's.

findings.problem: `ag-server admin ...` ignores the real configuration file: there is no --config flag, so `admin create-repo` always creates a SQLite + filesystem repository even when the deployment uses [repos.storage] PostgreSQL/S3, with a hardcoded Quota::default() (main.rs:245) instead of the configured defaults. `admin mint` has a hardcoded `--ttl` default of 3600 (main.rs:78) and does not enforce auth.max_ttl_secs/max_agent_ttl_secs; `admin repos` silently truncates at 10_000 (main.rs:250); `--default-stream` default "main" duplicates config.
findings.proposed_fix: Give Admin the same --config/AG_SERVER_CONFIG option as Serve and build App from the loaded config; apply the configured TTL caps, default quota, default stream and storage template; page through all repos. Test create-repo against a Postgres/S3 config.

findings.problem: Deduplication is a linear scan of only the 1000 newest jobs (existing_validation_jobs at line 167 scans 500), although tx.job_enqueue already dedupes by an indexed dedupe_key. Beyond that window an existing job is missed, so a duplicate 'job.enqueue' audit entry and 'enqueued' metric are produced and prepare() under-reports existing jobs. Worse, a hit returns the existing job in ANY state: after a job failed permanently (e.g. a runner infrastructure failure) or was cancelled, request_validation / prepare(enqueue_validations) keeps returning that dead job and never queues a new one for the same (proposal, check, tree, policy_version), so validation cannot be retried until the tree changes.
findings.proposed_fix: Look the job up by dedupe_key with a Tx::job_by_key (public) instead of scanning; if the existing job is failed/cancelled, re-queue it (new Tx::job_requeue) or enqueue a fresh job with a generation suffix in the key; make existing_validation_jobs query by payload/dedupe prefix. Test: exhaust attempts, call request_validation again, expect a queued job.

findings.problem: Only worker-driven transitions are counted/audited. When a worker dies, Tx::job_claim silently reaps expired claims inside the claimer's transaction (requeue, or state 'failed' when attempts are exhausted) with no audit entry, no 'retried'/'failed' metric increment and no event in the feed. The shipped alert AgentGitJobsFailing (increase(agwp_job_events_total{event="failed"}[1h]) > 5) and the documented metric semantics therefore never see jobs that fail permanently because their runner crashed - the most common failure mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Have job_claim (and a periodic reaper) return the list of reaped jobs with their new state; in try_claim increment job_events{retried|failed} and append a 'job.expire' audit entry for each. Add a test: claim with a tiny lease, let it expire with attempts=max, claim again, assert failed metric and audit entry.

findings.problem: Only traces use the traceparent (trace.rs Tracer::begin). The request log span (app.rs:207 info_span!("request", op, request_id, transport)) carries no trace/span id, Ingress.traceparent's doc ('passed through to logs', app.rs:44) is false, SpanContext::traceparent() (trace.rs:251, 'to hand to downstream calls') is never called, and no response header or downstream call (JWKS fetch, jobs handed to workers) carries a traceparent, so there is no propagation beyond continuing an inbound trace.

findings.problem: Execution-plane tuning knobs (default/maximum job lease, long-poll ceiling, wake-up and cross-process rescan intervals) and the read_head long-poll ceiling are compile-time constants with no [jobs]/[limits] config section; an operator with slow sandboxes or aggressive load balancers (idle timeout < 30 s) cannot tune them. MAX_WAIT_MS is defined twice. limits.default_deadline_ms (default 60 s) silently interacts with them.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `[jobs]` (default_lease_ms, max_lease_ms, max_wait_ms, rescan_interval_ms) and `limits.max_long_poll_ms` to ServerConfig with validation (long-poll < default_deadline_ms) and use one constant source for jobs and streams.

// Poll the log at least every 500 ms so changes made by other server processes show up too.
... tokio::time::timeout(until_heartbeat.min(Duration::from_millis(500)), notified)   (also line 95 `15_000` / `.max(1000)`, line 133 batch `256`, line 76 replay `500`/`5000`, http.rs:1320 `Duration::from_secs(25)`)
findings.problem: Event-feed intervals and sizes are fixed: default heartbeat 15 s, SSE KeepAlive 25 s (a second, independent keep-alive), batch 256, replay limits 500/5000 and a 500 ms poll. Every subscriber runs a full with_repo call (authorization, control-DB repo lookup, spawn_blocking, audit query) twice per second even when idle, so N subscribers cost 2N DB round-trips/s; the cadence cannot be tuned for large installations or for proxies with shorter idle timeouts.
findings.proposed_fix: Introduce `[events]` config (poll_interval_ms, default_heartbeat_ms, batch_size, replay_max) and make the poll cheap (a single `audit_latest_seq` per tick shared per repository via the notifier, only reading rows when it advanced); drop the redundant axum KeepAlive or derive it from the heartbeat.

findings.problem: resolve_path reads the entire blob (up to 256 MiB) just to learn its size and turns any error (corrupt or missing object) into size 0, while the sibling paths use the metadata-only blob_len. findings.problem: 'Runs create at most once per (scope, key)' is only true within one healthy process: create() and the idempotency record are two separate transactions, so a crash or write error between them leaves the object created but unrecorded and a retry with the same key creates it again; the guard is a single process-wide mutex that serializes every keyed creation across all repositories and does nothing across processes. Records are never expired.
findings.proposed_fix: Record the key inside the same repository transaction as the creation (as propose_idempotent does), or use a UNIQUE(scope,key) row inserted first; scope locking per repository; add a TTL/cleanup for idempotency rows.

findings.problem: whoami decides which role bindings apply to the caller by substituting 'x' for '*' in the binding's repository glob and matching that invented repository name. It is wrong for globs with ?, [..] or {a,b} (the substituted name does not match its own pattern, so a held role is not reported) and for patterns where 'x' is excluded by a more specific sibling. The reported roles are a guess, not the real authorization result.

findings.excerpt: repo.meta().read(|tx| tx.leases_all(500))?
findings.problem: list_leases with active_only=false returns at most the newest 500 leases with no indication of truncation or paging.
findings.proposed_fix: Add page_size/page_token to ListLeasesRequest (keyset by acquired_at,id) or return a `truncated` flag.

findings.problem: The job index rebuild (startup and the 5 s rescan) silently returns on a control-DB error, ignores repositories it cannot open and treats read errors as 'no jobs', so work in a temporarily unreadable repository is invisible to claim_job (with an empty `repo`) until a later rescan - with no log line. It also opens every repository (up to the max_open pool, evicting hot ones) on each rescan and caps at 100_000 repos.
findings.proposed_fix: Log failures with the repository name, count them in a metric, iterate with paging instead of a 100_000 literal, and prefer a control-plane table of repos-with-queued-jobs updated on enqueue/claim so no repository needs opening.

findings.problem: claim_job removes a repository from the in-memory hint when its claim returned None; a job enqueued between that claim and the removal (note_jobs_queued ran first) is dropped from the hint and only found by the 5 s rescan, which is triggered only inside an ongoing long-poll after a timeout and only when the hint is entirely empty. Short-poll workers (wait_ms=0) may not see the job for a long time, and jobs queued by another server process are discovered only through this scan.
findings.proposed_fix: Re-check the repo after removal (or remove only if job_list(Queued,1) is still empty in the same transaction), and make the rescan independent of long-polling (background interval task).

findings.excerpt: "this worker does not hold the job (it finished, was cancelled, or its lease was taken over)"
findings.problem: The error text and the storage state machine (Tx::job_cancel, JobState::Cancelled) describe cancellation, but there is no API, route, gRPC method or automatic trigger that cancels a job: closing/updating a proposal does not cancel its queued validation jobs, so runners spend sandbox time on candidates that are already stale, and 'cancelled' is unreachable in the product.
findings.proposed_fix: Add CancelJob (and cancel queued/claimed validation jobs on proposal close/update or policy change) with a job.cancel audit entry and metric label; or remove the claim from the message.

findings.problem: The stored error is truncated to a literal 2000 characters but the audit entry written in the same transaction (and hash-chained forever) receives the full, untrusted req.error, which can be up to max_request_bytes (8 MiB) - an unbounded write amplification into the append-only audit log.
findings.proposed_fix: Truncate once (named constant, ideally configurable) and use the truncated string for both the job row and the audit entry.

findings.problem: The third tuple element is computed and never used, and a conflicted preview with no candidate is labelled strategy "merge" even though no merge was produced - the field is inferred from other fields rather than reported by the engine.
findings.proposed_fix: Have the engine's MergePreview carry an explicit Option<Strategy> and map it directly; delete the unused element.

findings.excerpt: Ok(v1::SubmitAttestationResponse { accepted: true })
findings.problem: `accepted` is a constant: it is true whenever no error was returned, yet the doc/comment says whether an attestation counts is up to the policy (trusted_issuers). Clients reading `accepted: true` may believe it counts toward the Validated verdict.
findings.proposed_fix: Return whether the issuer is trusted by the stream's current policy (counts: bool) or rename/document the field as 'stored'.

findings.problem: Publication results are read out of an untyped JSON value with silent 0 defaults, so a pending, failed or malformed publish reports 0 new changesets/blobs as if it were a real answer; other operation kinds fall through `_ => {}` with no result at all.
findings.proposed_fix: Store a typed PublishResult in the intent and deserialize it (error on mismatch); expose explicit pending/failed states.

findings.problem: /v1/capabilities (and gRPC Negotiate, grpc.rs:120) bypass App::dispatch, so the only unauthenticated API endpoint is not counted in agwp_requests_total, not rate limited, not traced and not shielded by the concurrency gate - while the docs say every operation is covered by the pipeline.
findings.proposed_fix: Route negotiate through a public variant of dispatch that skips authentication but applies metrics, tracing, an IP-keyed rate limit and the concurrency semaphore.

findings.excerpt: ag_crypto::random_id("req").unwrap_or_else(|_| "req_unknown".into())   (same in grpc.rs:60)
findings.problem: If the RNG fails, every request gets the same correlation id 'req_unknown', destroying log/trace correlation without any error; the 64-character id limit is duplicated in grpc.rs:58 instead of reusing MAX_REQUEST_ID.
findings.proposed_fix: Fall back to a process-unique counter id (pid + atomic counter) and share one helper between transports.

findings.problem: A magic sentinel is used to disable the deadline for streams; app.rs:221-223 then exports it as the span attribute agwp.deadline_ms (~4.6e18) and as the Request-deadline of the trace, and the `events.subscribe` span/latency histogram only measure stream setup.
findings.proposed_fix: Model 'no deadline' explicitly (Ingress.no_deadline: bool or Option<Option<u64>>) and omit the attribute.

findings.problem: The 'chunked streaming' of object and file downloads is a stream::iter over a fully materialised Vec: the whole object (up to 256 MiB) is read into memory by get_object/file_content, then copied again chunk by chunk (2x). Uploads (ObjectSink, HTTP PUT collect()) likewise buffer the whole object before store_object. With max_concurrent_requests = 512 the memory bound is 512 x 256 MiB. The advertised objects.chunked feature does not reduce server memory.
findings.proposed_fix: Expose a streaming reader from the object store (get_stream/put_stream with incremental hashing) and wire both transports to it; at minimum bound total in-flight object bytes with a semaphore.

findings.problem: Malformed entries in OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS (e.g. a header whose value contains a comma, or a bad name) are silently discarded, so an authentication header for a hosted collector can vanish and the only symptom is 401s counted in trace_export_failures.
findings.proposed_fix: Return an error from parse_headers and fail start-up (or log the offending name, never the value).

findings.problem: Eviction threshold and idle age are literals; limiter state is per process, so with several replicas the effective rate is rate x replicas; 'unlimited' growth is still possible if >50k distinct credentials are active within 300 s.
findings.proposed_fix: Name the constants and make them configurable; document per-process semantics (or back the buckets with the shared control DB for HA).

findings.problem: Exporter queue size, batch size, flush interval and POST timeout are fixed; operators with high request rates cannot size the queue (spans drop) or lengthen the timeout for a remote collector. Documented, but not tunable.
findings.proposed_fix: Expose them under [telemetry] (otlp_queue_size, otlp_batch_size, otlp_flush_interval_ms, otlp_timeout_ms) with validation.

findings.problem: shutdown() flushes but does not stop or join the thread (the JoinHandle is just dropped), contradicting its doc comment; spans emitted after the flush (late requests during graceful shutdown) can be lost without being counted.
findings.proposed_fix: Send a Shutdown message, join the thread with a timeout, and count undelivered spans as dropped.

findings.excerpt: let user = std::env::var("USER").or_else(|_| std::env::var("LOGNAME")).unwrap_or_else(|_| "unknown".into());
findings.problem: When neither --as, AG_IDENTITY, USER nor LOGNAME is set (containers, cron, systemd units, and every Windows session, which only sets USERNAME) the acting identity silently becomes the fake shared principal `user:unknown`. That identity is then written into the hash-chained audit log, reviews, reflog and changeset authors, and defeats policy rules such as forbid_self_approval (two different people are both user:unknown). A placeholder name is being used where real state (the OS account) is required.
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve the real OS account (USER, LOGNAME, USERNAME, or getpwuid_r / the `whoami` crate) and, if nothing can be determined, fail with an error that tells the user to pass --as / set AG_IDENTITY. Never invent an identity. Verify with a CLI e2e test that runs `ag snapshot` with env_clear() and expects exit 1 plus the hint, and one on Windows CI that USERNAME is honoured.

findings.excerpt: timeout: Some(std::time::Duration::from_secs(120)),   (same literal again at line 355 in `clone`)
findings.problem: Every remote call, including the single client-streaming `upload_objects` of an entire push and each object download, gets a fixed 120 s deadline that an operator cannot change by flag, env var or remote config. A large initial push over a slow link is cut off by the client with a deadline error. `clone` (line 351-357) builds its own Options by hand with `..Default::default()`, so it also drops AG_RUN and the ag/<version> user agent that `connect()` sets, a divergent duplicate of the connection logic.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `timeout` (and `connect_timeout`) to the Remote config and to clone/remote-add flags plus an AG_TIMEOUT env override. Use a much larger or no overall deadline for bulk transfer (upload/get_object) and keep per-call deadlines for unary calls. Make clone call the same `connect()` helper. Verify with an ag-server integration test that pushes a multi-hundred-MB history through a throttled proxy with a short and a long configured timeout.

findings.excerpt: page_size: 200,   // remote proposals;  `limit: 500,` (line 967, remote events replay);  `page_size: 1000,` (line 230, fetch);  `heartbeat_ms: 15_000,` (line 949);  `max_commits: 0` (line 1043, remote blame)
findings.problem: `ag remote proposals` requests one page of 200 and never follows `next_page_token`, so any repository with more than 200 proposals is silently truncated with no indication. `ag remote events` replays at most 500 events and does not report that more remain (the response carries latest_seq, which is ignored). `ag remote log -n` is clamped by the server to 1000 without notice. Page sizes are magic numbers that duplicate ag_protocol::limits::MAX_PAGE_SIZE, the follow heartbeat is hard-wired, and `remote blame` cannot pass --max-commits although local `ag blame` can (it sends 0 = server default).
findings.proposed_fix: Loop on next_page_token until exhausted (or until an explicit --limit), print a `(more: use --after <seq>)` hint or loop for events based on latest_seq, derive page sizes from ag_protocol::limits / negotiated Limits, expose --max-commits and --heartbeat flags. Verify against a real ag-server holding >1000 proposals and >5000 audit events that `--json` returns every row.

findings.excerpt: let list = ctx.repo.meta().read(|tx| tx.proposals_list(state.as_deref(), 200))?;   (also agents.rs:126 `tx.runs(name.as_deref(), 50)` and agents.rs:331 `tx.leases_all(200)`)
findings.problem: Local `ag proposal list`, `ag agent runs` and `ag lease list --all` have fixed result caps (200 / 50 / 200) with no --limit flag and no truncation notice, unlike `ag log -n`, `ag op list -n` and `ag stream reflog -n`. Output on a busy repository is silently incomplete, which is dangerous for scripts consuming --json.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `-n/--limit` (default documented, `0` or `--all` for unlimited) to these three commands, and emit a stderr notice or a `truncated: true` JSON field when the cap is hit. Verify with a CLI e2e test that creates >200 proposals and >50 runs.

Verify in the Windows CI job (build + the tokens_can_be_stored_with_restricted_permissions test ported to Windows).

findings.excerpt: let env_digest = env.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| { let mut h = Sha256::new(); h.update(command.join("\u{1f}").as_bytes()); h.update(std::env::consts::OS.as_bytes()); h.update(std::env::consts::ARCH.as_bytes()); format!("sha256:{}", hex::encode(h.finalize())) });
findings.problem: The signed attestation's environment digest, which policy can pin (ag-policy `env_digest` requirement) and which the sandbox worker computes from the real execution environment, is here just a hash of the argv string plus OS/ARCH. Two machines with different compilers, tool versions or PATH contents produce the same digest, so the field attests nothing about the environment. It is documented in validation.md, but the value has the same shape as the worker's real digest and could be mistaken for it.
findings.proposed_fix: Prefix local digests with a distinguishing scheme (e.g. `local-unsandboxed:sha256:`) so policy pinning can never accept it as a sandbox digest, and fold in real inputs (resolved absolute path and `--version` output of the executable, PATH, tool-specific lockfile hash) or require --env explicitly. Verify with a policy that pins the worker digest and shows the local run is rejected.

findings.problem: The only test that proves the README demo works reports success without running anything when bash or python3 is missing, so a misconfigured CI image yields a green but vacuous result. The Postgres branch in tests/cli.rs (line 161) likewise returns early with 'skipped' unless the environment variable is set.
findings.proposed_fix: Honour the existing AG_REQUIRE_BACKENDS convention: when it (or CI) is set, panic instead of skipping. Verify in the CI job that already sets AG_REQUIRE_BACKENDS=1.

findings.problem: An invalid run id is silently dropped (`.ok()`), so the client keeps talking to the server WITHOUT the `ag-run` header and acts as the bare credential instead of the agent run the caller asked for. `connect()` correctly rejects the same input with ClientError::Invalid("bad run id"); `with_run` swallows the error and changes attribution/permissions instead.
findings.proposed_fix: Return Result<Self> and propagate ClientError::Invalid for a header-unsafe run id (share the validation with connect()). Verify with a unit test that with_run("bad\nid") is an error and a real-server test that the header is present on every call.

findings.excerpt:
/// Capability negotiation and server limits.
pub async fn negotiate(&self) -> Result<v1::NegotiateResponse> { ... features: Vec::new(),
findings.problem: The AGWP spec says 'Clients call Negotiate first and use the intersection of features', and the client crate advertises capability negotiation and server limits, but `connect()` never negotiates and the `ag` CLI never calls it (only an ag-worker test does). Protocol version mismatches are never detected, the server's Limits (max_page_size, max_batch, max_object_bytes) are ignored, and the request sends an empty feature list. The 'negotiated' data is fetched by no production code.
findings.proposed_fix: Call negotiate() once after connect (cache it on the Client), fail with a clear error if agwp.v1 is not selected, store the returned Limits and use them for page sizes, batch sizes (missing_objects) and message-size caps, and expose the feature set to callers. Verify against a real ag-server (and one with lowered limits) in an ag-client integration test.

findings.excerpt:

                    .max_encoding_message_size(16 * 1024 * 1024)   (and `for batch in ids.chunks(5000)` at line 247; `page_size: 1000` in ag-cli remote.rs:230)
findings.problem: Protocol limits are re-typed as magic numbers instead of being shared or negotiated: the 16 MiB message cap duplicates ag-server's private `const MAX_MESSAGE` (grpc.rs:31), the 5000 batch size is unrelated to ag_protocol::limits::MAX_BATCH (10_000), and the 1000 page size duplicates MAX_PAGE_SIZE. If the server's limits change, clients break or under-use capacity without any compile-time link.
findings.proposed_fix: Export MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES (and use MAX_BATCH / MAX_PAGE_SIZE) from ag_protocol::limits and reference them from both server and client, or take the numbers from the negotiated Limits. Verify with a test that asserts client and server constants are the same item.

findings.problem: Magic number unrelated to the repository's real limit (ag_types::Limits::max_message_len is 64 KiB by default and is configurable via repo.limits()). `String::truncate` panics when the cut is not on a UTF-8 char boundary, so a >60 000-byte commit message with a multibyte character at byte 60 000 aborts the whole import with a panic. If the limit is configured lower than 60 000 + trailer, Changeset::build fails instead. Data is also silently lost (only an inline note).
findings.proposed_fix: Compute the budget from repo.limits().max_message_len minus the length of the Imported-From trailer, cut at the previous char boundary (floor_char_boundary / is_char_boundary loop), count truncated commits in ImportReport and print them in the CLI. Verify with a roundtrip test using a 70 kB message of 3-byte characters and a repo with a smaller max_message_len.

findings.excerpt: let email = format!("{}@agentgit.invalid", name.replace(['#', ':'], "."));
findings.problem: Every exported commit gets a fabricated address on a reserved non-routable domain, and committer is forced equal to author with a fixed `+0000` zone (lines 88-89). The importer maps the Git author's real e-mail into the identity (`user:alice@example.com`), but export turns it into the name `user:alice@example.com` with email `user.alice@example.com@agentgit.invalid`, so authorship cannot be recovered on the way back and `git shortlog`, mailmap, GitHub attribution and signing-policy tooling see placeholder identities. There is no option to supply real names/emails.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an identity map (`--author-map FILE`, mailmap-compatible) and, when the AgentGit identity name already contains an e-mail (as produced by import), emit it verbatim; make the fallback domain configurable (`--email-domain`). Optionally record the original author name/e-mail/timezone as changeset metadata on import so round trips are lossless. Verify with an import -> export test asserting `git log --format=%an,%ae` equals the source.

findings.excerpt:
let who = if c.author_email.is_empty() { &c.author_name } else { &c.author_email };
        let author = Identity::new(format!("user:{}", sanitize_identity_name(who)))   (run.rs:30: `if clean.is_empty() { "unknown".into() } else { clean }`)
findings.problem: The Git-to-AgentGit identity mapping is hard-wired: always `user:<sanitized e-mail>`, the human name is dropped, bots/agents cannot be mapped to agent: or service: principals, distinct e-mails that sanitise to the same string collide, and empty authors become the placeholder `user:unknown`. There is no way to supply an identity map.
findings.proposed_fix: Support an `--identity-map` file (git mailmap syntax plus target principal kind), keep the author name in changeset metadata, and fail or report (rather than invent `unknown`) when an author has neither name nor e-mail. Verify with a fixture repo containing a bot author and two colliding e-mails.

findings.excerpt:
let out = Command::new("git")
        .arg("-C")
        .arg(dir)
        .args(args)
        .env("GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT", "0")   (export.rs:66 and import.rs:49 spawn `git` directly with no environment hardening at all)
findings.problem: Git is invoked with the caller's ambient environment and the user's/system git config. GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE or GIT_INDEX_FILE exported in the environment (for example when `ag git export` runs from a git hook) override `-C <dir>` and make the bridge read or write the wrong repository; `log.showSignature=true` injects gpg output into the `git log --format=...` stream the importer parses; `i18n.logOutputEncoding` re-encodes %B before it is read with from_utf8_lossy. The binary name `git` and its location are also fixed (no AG_GIT/--git override). The three spawn sites are inconsistent with each other.
findings.proposed_fix: Route all three spawns through one helper that env_removes GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE/GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY/GIT_CONFIG*, sets GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null (or passes -c log.showSignature=false -c i18n.logOutputEncoding=UTF-8 -c core.quotePath=false), and allows an `AG_GIT`/`--git-bin` override. Verify with roundtrip tests run with GIT_DIR pointing elsewhere and with a global config enabling showSignature.

git(dir, &["log", "--topo-order", "--reverse", "--format=%H%x1f%P%x1f%an%x1f%ae%x1f%at%x1f%B%x1e", rev, "--"])?;
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out);
findings.problem: Commit metadata is parsed from `git log` text using in-band 0x1e/0x1f control-character separators and decoded with from_utf8_lossy. A commit message containing U+001E breaks parsing with 'unexpected log record', and non-UTF-8 author names/messages are silently replaced by U+FFFD with no report, so imported content differs from the source without any warning (only skipped paths and submodules are reported).
findings.proposed_fix: Read raw commit objects via `git cat-file --batch` (already used for blobs) and parse the header/message bytes, honouring the `encoding` header and reporting any lossy conversions in ImportReport, or at least use `git log -z` with NUL-delimited fields (NUL cannot occur in a commit). Verify with fixtures containing a latin1-encoded commit and 0x1e in a message.

findings.problem: git cat-file's stderr is discarded, so when it fails (missing/corrupt object, shallow or partial clone) the user only sees the secondary error "cat-file said '' for <sha>" with the real cause thrown away.
findings.proposed_fix: Capture stderr (pipe and read it on failure, or inherit it) and include it in GitError::Parse/Failed. Verify by importing a shallow/partial clone.

findings.problem: An unexplained, unconfigurable cap of five million changesets; larger histories cannot be exported at all (the error is mapped to a generic 'Unsupported'), and the whole ordered id list is materialised in memory.
findings.proposed_fix: Name the constant, make it a field of ExportOptions / CLI flag (or remove the cap and stream the topological order), and give an error that states the limit and how to raise it.
