findings.problem: Hand-rolled approximation of git's ref-name rules. It accepts names git rejects (`x.lock`, `a/`, `.hidden`, `a@{b}`, `@`, `a//b`, control characters other than newline), which then fail later inside fast-import with a less helpful message, after a repository may already have been created by `git init`. The real validator (git itself) is a required dependency of the bridge anyway.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate with `git check-ref-format --branch <name>` (or `refs/heads/<name>`) before touching the destination, and do the check before `git init`. Verify with a table test of invalid names.

findings.excerpt: Op::Delete { path } => buf.extend_from_slice(format!("D {path}\n").as_bytes()),  ...  buf.extend_from_slice(format!("M {mode} inline {path}\n").as_bytes());
findings.problem: fast-import treats a path that begins with a double quote as a C-style quoted string. RepoPath allows `"` (only control chars and backslash are forbidden), and the importer accepts such paths from Git, but the exporter writes them unquoted; I verified with git that `M 100644 inline "a".txt` fails with 'fatal: Garbage after path'. So a history containing a file named `"a".txt` imports fine yet cannot be exported, contradicting the documented round-trip guarantee 'for histories without skipped paths'.
findings.proposed_fix: Quote paths in fast-import syntax whenever they start with `"` (C-style escape of `"`, `\\` and non-printables) and add the case to history_survives_a_round_trip_with_identical_git_trees. Verify with a real git roundtrip.

findings.excerpt:
//! Submodules (gitlinks), paths AgentGit refuses to record ..., tags, notes, signatures,
//! committer identity and timezone offsets. Skipped paths are reported.   (docs/guides/git-bridge.md:27: 'Not carried over, and reported when it happens: ... tags, notes, signatures, committer identity and timezone offsets')
findings.problem: The guide says everything in the 'not carried over' list is reported when it happens, but ImportReport only contains skipped paths and a submodule count. Signed commits, committer != author, non-UTC offsets, annotated tags and refs other than the single --rev are dropped silently, so a user migrating from Git gets no signal that provenance data was lost.
findings.proposed_fix: Either add counters/warnings to ImportReport and CLI output (signed commits dropped, committer differs, non-zero tz offset, other refs/tags not imported) or rewrite the sentence to say only paths and submodules are reported. Verify with a fixture containing a signed commit and a differing committer.

findings.problem: The whole OCI backend (the one the docs recommend for hostile/multi-tenant workloads, and which the README advertises as 'or a container') is verified only against a shell script that echoes canned replies ('inspect' prints a file, 'kill' touches a file, exit 125 is scripted). Nothing proves that docker/podman accept the generated flags (--memory-swap, --ulimit cpu, --pids-limit, --tmpfs, --mount type=bind, --entrypoint), that read-only/cap-drop/no-new-privileges/network none are actually enforced, that OOMKilled/exit-125 mapping works with real output, that cleanup removes real containers, or that bind-mounted /work is writable. The real components are feasible: GitHub ubuntu-latest runners ship Docker (and Podman), and .github/workflows/ci.yml:35-42 already runs the sandbox suites on Linux. src/oci.rs:8-10, docs/architecture/sandbox.md:251-256, ROADMAP.md:47 and CHANGELOG.md all admit it is untested against a real runtime.
findings.proposed_fix: Add tests/oci_real.rs that runs against a real runtime (docker, and a second matrix leg with podman) using a small digest-pinned image pulled in CI (e.g. busybox@sha256:...). Assert from inside the container what the kernel shows (NoNewPrivs=1, Seccomp=2, CapEff=0, read-only root EROFS, no network, pids/memory limits hit -> PidsLimit/MemoryLimit via real OOMKilled, timeout leaves no container in `docker ps -a --filter label=ag-sandbox=1`). Make the job fail (like AG_REQUIRE_SANDBOX) when the runtime is missing in CI (AG_REQUIRE_OCI=1). Keep a tiny argv-construction unit test only; delete the FAKE script and the 'untested' disclaimers once green.

findings.excerpt:
let isolation = IsolationReport {
    verified: false,
    user_ns: false,
    mount_ns: true,
    pid_ns: true, ... seccomp: true, rlimits: true,
    host_root: false,
    memory: Enforcement::Runtime,
    tasks: Enforcement::Runtime,
    cgroup: Some(CgroupReport { memory: true, pids: true }),
findings.problem: Every isolation flag of an OCI run is a constant, not an observation. They feed environment_digest (digest.rs:40-56) and therefore what a signed attestation states about the environment. They can be false claims: a Docker daemon started with seccomp unconfined or a permissive default profile still reports seccomp: true; rootless Podman or userns-remap reports user_ns: false; `--oci-user 0:0` (a legal worker flag) runs the check as kernel-uid 0 yet reports host_root: false; cgroup limits are reported as set although the runtime may have silently ignored --memory (no cgroup swap accounting, cgroup v1 without memory controller) or --pids-limit. The 'requested, not observed' note exists but the digest still hard-asserts the boolean values.
findings.proposed_fix: Before `rm -f`, run `<runtime> inspect --format '{{json .HostConfig}}' <name>` and `<runtime> info --format json`; derive each flag from what the runtime reports (ReadonlyRootfs, CapDrop, SecurityOpt contains no-new-privileges/seccomp profile, NetworkMode, PidsLimit, Memory/MemorySwap, Ulimits, User, rootless/userns info) and set host_root from the effective uid. If an observed value differs from the request, return SandboxError::Runtime instead of running with weaker isolation; set verified: true only for flags actually read back. Cover with the real-runtime tests from the previous finding.

findings.excerpt: push(&["run", "--name", container_name, "--label", "ag-sandbox=1", "--pull", "never"]);
findings.problem: The sandbox always passes `--pull never`, and neither ag-sandbox nor ag-worker ever pulls or verifies the image. docs/guides/workers.md:108 and README advertise policies that name a digest-pinned `image` for container workers, but a job whose image is not already in the local store fails with 'Unable to find image' (mapped to SandboxError::Runtime -> Failure::retry in worker.rs:376-380) until the server's attempt limit is hit; the docs never tell the operator to pre-pull. `ag-worker run --sandbox oci --oci-image X` also does not validate X at start-up: a tag-only image is only rejected per job in Backend::sandbox_for (profile.rs:83-88), and the runtime/daemon reachability is never checked (see doctor finding). The label `ag-sandbox=1` is set so stale containers could be found, but nothing in the repository ever uses it (no reaper).
findings.proposed_fix: Add an explicit, digest-only ensure step in the OCI path: if `<runtime> image inspect <image@sha256:...>` fails, run `<runtime> pull <image@sha256:...>` (bounded by a configurable timeout, subject to a worker flag such as --oci-allow-pull and network policy), verify the resulting RepoDigests contains the pinned digest, and cache per image. Validate --oci-image (pinned, present or pullable) and the runtime/daemon (`info`) at worker start-up. Add a startup reaper that removes containers with label ag-sandbox=1 left by a crashed worker. Document the image-provisioning contract in docs/guides/workers.md and test it against a real registry-less local image.

findings.excerpt:
#[arg(long, default_value = "65534:65534")]
    oci_user: String,
 ... crates/ag-worker/src/profile.rs:96-106  Backend::Oci { user, .. } => parse_numeric_user(user), ... checkout.rs:220 fs::set_permissions(&target, ... if entry.executable { 0o755 } else { 0o644 })
findings.problem: For container workers the check runs as container uid 65534 but the checked-out tree is only chown'ed to that uid when the worker is root (tree_owner returns None for any non-root worker, and for a non-numeric --oci-user, silently). A non-root worker (the recommended deployment, also every rootless Podman setup, where container uid 65534 maps to a subuid and not to the host uid) leaves /work owned by the worker's uid with mode 0755/0644, so the container user cannot write to /work and any check that writes (cargo target/, npm install, test artifacts) fails or - worse - fails as a signed `fail` verdict for a tree that is fine. Nothing detects the mismatch at start-up and parse_numeric_user failure is ignored. This is exactly the class of bug the missing real-runtime test (finding 1) would have caught.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive the container user from the runtime/worker: for non-root workers default --oci-user to the worker's own uid:gid (rootful docker) or `0:0` under rootless podman (maps to the host user), expose the choice explicitly, and refuse to start (Profile::check) when a root worker's --oci-user is non-numeric. Verify with a real-runtime e2e test that a check can create files in /work under rootful docker, rootless podman and non-root docker client.

findings.problem: The cgroup v2 path (exact memory.max / pids.max / oom.group / memory.peak / cgroup.kill, the Enforcement::Cgroup claims in the IsolationReport and the digest) is only tested against a temp directory that merely stores written strings (cgroup.rs:126-172). Nothing shows the kernel accepts those writes, that cgroup.procs migration works from a user namespace, that OOM kills are classified as MemoryLimit, or that Drop's `cgroup.kill` + rmdir loop actually cleans up. A real delegated cgroup v2 is feasible in CI (ubuntu-latest runs systemd on cgroup v2: `systemd-run --user --scope -p Delegate=yes`, or a privileged container with a writable cgroup2 mount). docs/architecture/sandbox.md:214-217, ROADMAP.md:47 and CHANGELOG.md admit it is untested.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a Linux integration test (and a CI step that provides a delegated cgroup2 subtree with memory+pids controllers, failing when it cannot - AG_REQUIRE_CGROUP=1) that runs a memory hog and a fork bomb and asserts isolation.cgroup == Some({memory:true,pids:true}), Enforcement::Cgroup, ExitStatus::MemoryLimit from oom_kill, max_rss_bytes from memory.peak, and that no ag-sandbox-* cgroup directory remains. Keep the fake-directory unit tests only for parsing.

findings.problem: `..Limits::default()` silently fixes `open_files = 1024` (RLIMIT_NOFILE) and `file_size_bytes = 1 GiB` (RLIMIT_FSIZE, spec.rs:96-108) for every check on every worker. Neither the policy RunSpec, the worker CLI nor Profile can change them, although they are part of the environment digest and real builds hit them (linkers/test runners with many fds; artefacts or debug info over 1 GiB end with SIGXFSZ and a signed `fail` for a healthy tree). They are also the only two limits with no ceiling check in sandbox_spec.
findings.proposed_fix: Add open_files and file_size_bytes to Ceilings/Defaults (flags --max-open-files, --default-open-files, --max-file-size-mb, --default-file-size-mb with ceiling validation like the other four) and, if the policy should control them, to RunSpec in proto/ag-protocol; reject (Refusal) when the request exceeds the ceiling; cover with a worker e2e test that a check writing a 2 GiB sparse file passes when allowed and is refused/failed when not.

output_bytes: 8 << 20,
            tmp_mb: 512,
            tail_bytes: 8 * 1024,
            max_checkout_bytes: 4 << 30,
 ... main.rs:295  cpu_secs: d.cpu_secs,
findings.problem: Profile::new hard-codes the per-stream output cap (8 MiB), the sandbox /tmp size (512 MiB per check, held in RAM) and how much output is stored (8 KiB tail), and `main.rs::profile()` never exposes them: there is no --output-limit, --tmp-mb, --tail-bytes or --default-cpu-secs flag (Defaults.cpu_secs is copied from the default). An operator cannot size /tmp for a machine running N lanes or for builds that need a bigger /tmp (rust, node), nor keep more log tail for debugging, without recompiling. docs/guides/workers.md:79,169 present these as 'by default' as though they were adjustable.
findings.proposed_fix: Add --output-mb, --tmp-mb, --result-tail-kb and --default-cpu-secs flags (with env equivalents) wired into Profile/Defaults, validate sane ranges, and update docs/guides/workers.md. Consider letting the policy request /tmp size within a ceiling because it is already part of the environment digest.

findings.excerpt: ro_mounts: ag_sandbox::standard_system_mounts(),  // spec.rs:326 "they carry no [`Mount::identity`]" ; digest.rs:96 None => put(b'h', m.host.to_string_lossy().as_bytes()),
findings.problem: By default every sandbox mounts the host's /usr, /bin, /lib*, /etc/ssl/certs with no identity, so environment_digest binds only the host path string. Two workers with entirely different /usr contents (different compiler, libc, Python) produce the same digest, and the same worker produces the same digest before and after `apt upgrade`. The product feature 'a policy can pin required_environment_digest so only workers in that exact configuration can satisfy the check' (docs/guides/workers.md:127-136, ADR 'environment' binding) is therefore not backed unless the operator manually replaces the default mounts via --no-system-mounts and --mount HOST=IDENTITY; the worker neither warns at start-up nor derives an identity.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive a real content identity for the default mounts (e.g. hash of /etc/os-release plus the package database digest - dpkg status / rpm db / apk installed - or a Merkle hash of the mounted tree, cached at start-up) and attach it via Mount::with_identity; at minimum log a warning and report `environment_identity: path-only` in result_json when any mount lacks an identity, and make `ag-worker doctor` print the identities that will enter the digest. Add an e2e test that changing a mounted tree's content changes the digest.

findings.excerpt: run: cargo build --release --locked --target ${{ matrix.target }} -p ag-cli -p ag-server   (deploy/docker/Dockerfile:27: cargo build --release --locked -p ag-server -p ag-cli \)
findings.problem: The execution plane is advertised as a product feature (README.md:125-128 'Isolated execution', ROADMAP, docs/guides/workers.md tells operators to run `ag-worker run`), but ag-worker is not built or shipped by the release workflow, is not in the Docker image, and has no Compose/Kubernetes manifest or systemd unit (grep of deploy/ finds no worker). Operators must build it from source, and a container-based worker (which the sandbox page says is common) has no supported image with the right capabilities/seccomp settings for user namespaces.
findings.proposed_fix: Build and publish ag-worker in release.yml (all Linux targets; macOS only if the process sandbox is supported there), add a worker image/target to deploy/docker/Dockerfile and example Compose service + Kubernetes Deployment documenting the security context needed for the namespace sandbox (unconfined seccomp/apparmor or sysctl) and for the OCI sandbox (socket access), and smoke-test `ag-worker doctor` in CI inside that image.

findings.excerpt: let oci = ["docker", "podman"].iter().find_map(|rt| { std::env::split_paths(...).map(|d| d.join(rt)).find(|p| p.is_file()) }).map(|_| Availability::Available)
findings.problem: `detect()` and `ag-worker doctor` (main.rs:185-190) report the OCI sandbox as `available` merely because a file named docker/podman exists on PATH; the daemon, permissions on the socket, rootless setup, the configured `--oci-runtime` (any other name or path is never looked at) and the image are not probed. findings.problem: The comment above says 'Decide whether this worker can and will run it before spending bandwidth', but the pinned-environment check runs only after the complete check has executed (up to the full timeout). A worker that can never match the pinned digest claims the job, runs it for up to an hour, throws the result away and returns it to the queue, again and again until the server's attempt limit; it can also starve workers that could match.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute the digest before executing: add `Sandbox::environment_digest(&self, spec) -> Result<String>` that builds the IsolationReport the same way as run() (namespace: probe cgroup/sampler availability; oci: the observed HostConfig) and compare with required_environment_digest before checkout; keep the post-run comparison as a safety net.

findings.excerpt:
if lost.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
            return Disposition::Abandoned("the claim was lost while the check ran ...")  // docs/guides/workers.md:172  "the check is not interrupted: it runs to its own time limit and its result is discarded" ; main.rs:354 std::process::exit(130);
findings.problem: There is no cancellation path: Sandbox::run (lib.rs:100-109) takes no cancel token, so when the lease is lost (another worker already runs the job) or the operator sends the second signal, the check keeps burning CPU for up to its timeout and, on the second signal, `std::process::exit(130)` leaves OCI containers running (the docker client is in its own process group and is not killed; nothing runs `<runtime> kill/rm`). The `ag-sandbox=1` label that would let a reaper find them is never used.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a cancellation handle to the Sandbox trait (e.g. `run_cancellable(&spec, &AtomicBool)` checked in supervise()'s poll loop and wired to the lease-lost flag and to shutdown), have OciSandbox's on_kill hook run on cancel, and add a start-up/shutdown reaper for label ag-sandbox=1 containers. Test with a real runtime.

findings.excerpt: const RETRY_AFTER_MS: i64 = 10_000;  ...  let mut backoff = Duration::from_secs(1);  ...  backoff = (backoff * 2).min(Duration::from_secs(30));   // main.rs:316 timeout: Some(Duration::from_secs(120)),   // main.rs:342-343 lease: Duration::from_secs(args.lease_secs.max(5)), wait: Duration::from_secs(args.wait_secs.min(30)),

findings.excerpt:
const PARALLEL: usize = 8;
const CACHE_BELOW: usize = 64 * 1024;  ... page_size: 5000,
findings.problem: Checkout concurrency (8 parallel blob downloads), the small-blob cache threshold (64 KiB, unbounded entry count) and the manifest page size (5000) are fixed constants without configuration; on a high-latency link or a huge monorepo the operator cannot tune them, and the cache has no total-size bound.
findings.proposed_fix: Move them into Profile (--checkout-parallelism, --checkout-cache-mb with a byte budget) and keep page_size negotiated with the server's advertised maximum.

findings.problem: Resource-limit statuses are guessed: any non-zero exit (including an ordinary test failure) whose sampled peak happened to reach 90% of the memory limit is reported as MemoryLimit, and a SIGKILL near the CPU budget as CpuLimit (the +50 ms slack and the 90% threshold are magic numbers). The status goes into result_json/summary that humans use to debug and docs call 'best effort'. The signed verdict is fail in both cases, so correctness of the attestation is unaffected, but the reported cause can be wrong.
findings.proposed_fix: Report the cause only when observed: with cgroup v2 use memory.events oom_kill / pids.events; for the sampled path return MemoryLimit only when the supervisor itself killed it (verdict) and otherwise return the natural exit status with a separate `near_memory_limit: true` note; name the thresholds as documented constants.

            memory: if memory_limited { Enforcement::Rlimit } else { Enforcement::None },
            tasks: if task_limited { Enforcement::Rlimit } else { Enforcement::None },  // task_limit(): "Best effort: tasks the user starts elsewhere meanwhile eat into the allowance"
findings.problem: The process sandbox converts `pids` into RLIMIT_NPROC = (all tasks currently owned by the user, read from /proc) + allowance, a snapshot-based approximation, yet reports it as `Enforcement::Rlimit` (the same value the namespace sandbox uses for an exact per-namespace limit) and the notes (lines 48-83) do not say it is approximate. findings.excerpt:
report.seccomp,
        report.rlimits,
        report.host_root,   // DOMAIN = b"agentgit.sandbox.environment.v1\0"
findings.problem: The environment digest says 'attestations bound to this digest state which protections their check ran under', but protections are booleans: `seccomp: true` is identical whether the deny-list has 60 or 10 syscalls, across ag-sandbox releases, and the digest contains no kernel release, no sandbox/crate version, no hostname/INNER_ID/SHM_MAX/root-tmpfs constants. A release that weakens the filter or /proc masking yields the same digest, so a policy pin cannot detect it.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a versioned `profile` identifier (e.g. sha256 of the built seccomp program and the PROC_MASKED/PROC_READONLY/DEVICES lists, plus a SANDBOX_PROFILE_VERSION constant) and the kernel release to the digest (domain v2, documented), and cover it with the existing 'every ingredient changes the digest' test.

findings.excerpt:
const RUNTIME_ERRORS: [&str; 8] = ["Error response from daemon", "Cannot connect to the Docker daemon", "Unable to find image", "pull access denied", "invalid reference format", "unknown flag", "unknown shorthand flag", "Error: "];
        let from_runtime = stderr.starts_with(&format!("{runtime}:")) || RUNTIME_ERRORS.iter().any(|m| stderr.contains(m));
findings.problem: Whether exit code 125 is a runtime failure or the check's own exit status is decided by substring-matching the (untrusted, check-controlled) stderr; a check that exits 125 after printing 'Error: ' is reclassified as an infrastructure failure (job retried instead of a signed fail), and runtimes with other message texts/locales are mismatched. Only verified against the fake script.
findings.proposed_fix: Distinguish by observation instead of text: after the run, `inspect` the container: if it never existed or `.State.ExitCode`/`.State.Status` shows it never started, it is a runtime failure; otherwise the exit code is the command's. Verify against real docker and podman.

findings.problem: The results of `kill` and `rm -f` are discarded and the 10 s/20 s timeouts are fixed. If the daemon hiccups the container (and its tmpfs/memory) leaks silently with a still-running check, and the worker reports success; ag-sandbox has no logging so nobody learns about it. `inspect` for OOMKilled likewise degrades to `false` on any failure (line 288-289), turning an OOM kill into a plain exit status.
findings.proposed_fix: Return/propagate cleanup failures (SandboxError::Runtime or a note in IsolationReport.notes and a tracing event), retry with backoff, make the timeouts part of OciConfig, and fail the run when `inspect` cannot be read instead of assuming OOMKilled=false.

findings.excerpt:
// The protocol says `regular`; servers before that was fixed said `file`.
        "regular" | "file" => FileType::Regular,
findings.problem: A compatibility shim for a server wire format that, per CHANGELOG.md ('it said `file` on reads before the server was released'), never shipped; it keeps an undocumented second spelling alive in production code.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the "file" alias (and its writes-accept counterpart on the server side if no released client sends it) and keep only the documented `regular`; the entry_from_wire test already covers the strict form.

findings.excerpt: let nonce = ag_crypto::random_id("d").unwrap_or_else(|_| format!("d_{}", std::process::id()));  ... fn prepare_dir(dir: &Path) -> std::io::Result<()> { if dir.exists() { return Ok(()); } ... from_mode(0o755)
findings.problem: If the system RNG fails the job directory name silently becomes a predictable `d_<pid>`, and prepare_dir() accepts an already-existing directory without checking owner/mode, so a local attacker who pre-creates `<scratch>/<job>-<attempt>-d_<pid>` (or any pre-existing dir) gets the worker to write the checkout into attacker-controlled storage; new job dirs are always 0755/0644 even when the worker is not root, so other local users can read every checked-out tree.
findings.proposed_fix: Propagate the RNG error (fail the job) instead of falling back; create the job dir with `create_dir` (EEXIST is an error) and mode 0700 unless a root worker needs to map to another uid, in which case 0711/0755 only on the path components required; verify ownership of the scratch root at start-up.

findings.problem: Constants are baked into every check's environment. For the process backend ('ro_mounts and rw_tmp_bytes are not applied', process.rs:50) HOME and TMPDIR=/tmp are the host's shared, unbounded /tmp, so concurrent lanes (and other users) share ~/.cargo, ~/.cache and temp files: cross-job cache poisoning and non-reproducible results. `LANG=C.UTF-8` assumes the locale exists in every image/toolchain mount. They are documented but cannot be set per worker.
findings.proposed_fix: For Backend::Process give each job a private tmp under its job_dir and set HOME/TMPDIR to it; add a worker-level `--env KEY=VAL` (included in the digest) for defaults such as LANG; keep policy env overriding.

findings.excerpt: const SHM_MAX: u64 = 64 << 20;  ...  hostname: c"sandbox".to_owned(), ... root_opts: c"mode=0755,size=4m,nr_inodes=4096".to_owned(),  /  const BASE_CANDIDATES: [&str; 7] = ["/tmp", "/mnt", "/run", "/var", "/srv", "/opt", "/media"];
findings.problem: /dev/shm is capped at 64 MiB regardless of spec (workloads such as browsers, PostgreSQL or multiprocessing test runners need more), the root tmpfs size/inode budget and hostname are fixed, and the sandbox root is mounted on the first existing of seven fixed host directories (failing with 'none of [...] exists' on minimal hosts). None of these appear in SandboxSpec or the digest.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `shm_bytes` to SandboxSpec (default min(rw_tmp_bytes, 64 MiB)) and include it in environment_digest; keep the others as documented internal constants but derive the mount base from a configurable directory or a mkdtemp under the worker's scratch dir.

findings.problem: Platform stubs for non-Linux Unix (macOS): the stub reports IsolationLevel::Namespaces although it can never isolate anything; honesty depends on every caller calling availability() first (ag-worker does). Borderline: it is a legitimate cfg gate that fails closed in run(), reported low.
findings.proposed_fix: Return IsolationLevel::None from the stub's isolation() (or make NamespaceSandbox::isolation() return Option/Result) so a mistaken use cannot satisfy `min_isolation`; implement a real macOS isolation story (sandbox-exec/containers) per ROADMAP or document macOS as process-sandbox-only.

findings.excerpt:
static PROBE: OnceLock<Availability> = OnceLock::new();
        PROBE.get_or_init(probe).clone()
findings.problem: Availability is probed once per process and cached forever, including negative results from transient failures (EAGAIN/ENOMEM/ENOSPC under load, the 10 s probe timeout, a temporarily full /tmp). A long-running worker that hit one transient failure at start-up (or whose operator fixes the sysctl) reports the namespace sandbox as unavailable until restarted and, under --sandbox auto, refuses to start.
findings.proposed_fix: Cache only positive results (or retry negative ones with backoff and re-probe on `doctor`), and distinguish permanent causes (EPERM/EACCES/EINVAL) from transient ones.

findings.problem: The test `what_the_command_leaves_in_the_namespace_dies_with_its_init` computes the list of host processes that match the sandbox's leftover `sleep` commands and then throws it away; the remaining assertion inspects only direct children of the test process, which the sandbox's processes never are, so it passes even if the sandbox leaked daemons (the real coverage lives in limits.rs). A similar weak assertion is at isolation.rs:253 (`assert!(!o.stdout_lossy().is_empty())` for the mount/remount attempt).
findings.proposed_fix: Use unique_marker()/sleep_marker() like limits.rs and assert host_processes_matching(marker).is_empty() after the run, or delete the test; assert the exact error text of the remount attempt.

findings.problem: The worker's end-to-end suite silently degrades to the non-isolating process sandbox when namespaces are unavailable (and the isolation test itself returns early with SKIP; the real-server-binary test also skips when the binary is not built), so a green run on such a host proves nothing about the isolated path. The OCI backend has no worker-level e2e at all.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the degrade explicit-fail under AG_REQUIRE_SANDBOX (it already panics when set, so keep CI strict), require the ag-server binary under the same flag, and add worker e2e legs for Backend::Oci against a real runtime.

findings.problem: Every checkout error is classified retryable, including deterministic ones for the tree itself (CheckoutError::Bad: a symlink with an absolute or `..`-escaping target, invalid path, wrong object kind). Such a candidate can never be validated by any worker: the job bounces through the queue until the attempt limit and the proposal stays 'blocked' with no signed verdict; legitimate repositories containing e.g. an absolute symlink are permanently unvalidatable.
findings.proposed_fix: Classify CheckoutError::Bad for tree-content violations as Failure::permanent with a clear reason surfaced to the author (or materialise such symlinks safely - dangling links are harmless inside the sandbox, which cannot see host paths - and reserve the rejection for real traversal risks); keep size-over-limit as retry.

findings.excerpt: const form = ref({ name: '', description: '', stream: 'main' })  // :111 same literal in openCreate(); :123 default_stream: form.value.stream.trim() || undefined
findings.problem: The create-repository form prefills the default stream with the literal 'main' and then sends it explicitly, so the server's configurable default (cfg.repos.default_stream, used in create_repo when default_stream is empty) can never apply. An operator who configures a different default (e.g. trunk) gets 'main' from every repository created via the UI.
findings.proposed_fix: Leave the field empty with a placeholder, and send default_stream only when the user typed one so the server default wins. Better: have the server expose its default stream in /v1/capabilities (or a repos-defaults field) and show that as the placeholder. Verify with a real ag-server started with repos.default_stream='trunk': create a repo from the UI with the field empty and assert Repo.default_stream === 'trunk' (Playwright e2e against the real server).
findings.severity_note: configurable server value overridden by the client

findings.excerpt: const rev = computed(() => qRev.value || board.repo?.default_stream || 'main')  // HistoryView.vue:47 effectiveRev uses the same || 'main'; stores/board.ts:205 stream.value = value.default_stream || 'main'
findings.problem: While the repository record has not loaded (board.repo is null) or when default_stream is empty, Files, History and the board request the stream literally named 'main'. On a repository whose default stream is anything else this issues a wrong request (404 or the empty-state 'no changesets yet') and can flash or keep wrong data. The fallback hides the missing real state.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the 'main' fallbacks. Gate the first list/log/resolve request on board.repo being loaded (useResource already supports enabled(); the History/Files watchers need the same guard) and show the skeleton until default_stream is known. Verify in e2e with a repo whose default stream is not 'main' and assert the first network request carries that stream.

findings.excerpt: description="Queued proposals are integrated one at a time, in order, stopping at the first one that is blocked."  // :50-53 toasts.warn(`Queue stopped at ${shortId(res.stopped_at, 6)}`, `${n} processed before a proposal was blocked or conflicted.`)  // :32-40 TONE has queued/done/integrated/blocked/conflict/failed/skipped
findings.problem: The UI text contradicts the engine: ag-integrate Queue::run_queue documents 'A blocked or conflicting entry does not hold up the ones behind it' and loops over every queued entry. 'processed' therefore contains all entries, and stopped_at is merely the first blocked/rejected one, so 'Queue stopped at ... n processed before' is false. In addition the real queue state set is queued/done/blocked/rejected/failed (OpenAPI QueueEntry.state): 'rejected' (conflict or policy denial) is missing from TONE so it renders neutral, while 'integrated', 'conflict' and 'skipped' are states the server never emits.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite the empty-state and toast text to match the engine (entries are processed in order; blocked or rejected ones are marked and skipped, the rest continue) and report counts per outcome from res.processed[].state. Replace TONE with exactly the OpenAPI states (queued, done, blocked, rejected, failed) and derive the type from the generated schema. Fix the OpenAPI description of RunQueueResponse.stopped_at at the same time. Verify with a real queue holding one blocked proposal in front of an integrable one and assert the second is integrated and the first shows state 'blocked'/'rejected' with the correct tone.

findings.excerpt: const pass = s(result.outcome) !== 'fail'
findings.problem: A job.complete event is rendered as 'finished validation job (passed)' whenever result.outcome is anything other than the string 'fail'. The server only sets result.outcome when an attestation was submitted; a stale completion stores result {"stale": true} with no outcome, and a non-validate job has none either. Those are shown as green 'passed' in the live feed and proposal timeline, which asserts a verdict the server never gave.
findings.proposed_fix: Tri-state the display: outcome 'pass' -> passed, 'fail' -> failed, result.stale === true -> 'candidate was stale, no attestation', otherwise neutral 'completed' with no tone. Verify with a real worker run against a stale candidate (ag-worker tests already produce {"stale": true}) and with pass and fail runs, asserting the three sentences in the feed.

findings.excerpt: 'The approvals the policy requires are in for the current head.'  // :269-270 'not required', 'The policy requires no approval for this change.'  // :247 const required = typeof d.required === 'number' ? d.required : have + 1
findings.problem: The Approved verdict is inferred from the absence of a blocker even when the prepare result is missing or failed. With prep unavailable (still loading, or prepare errored) and zero reviews, the final else branch states 'not required: The policy requires no approval for this change', a claim with no evidence (ProposalView always passes a non-null reviews array, so this shows during every load). With prep unavailable but one approval it claims the policy's requirement is satisfied. When a blocker has no numeric 'required', the UI invents required = have + 1.
findings.proposed_fix: Only emit 'ok' or 'na' for Approved when prep is present and has no insufficient_approvals/changes_requested blocker; with prep absent or errored return tone 'unknown' ('checking' or 'could not be computed'). Drop the have + 1 invention and show only what the server detail provides. Better: have prepare return a structured approvals verdict (required, have, scope) so no inference is needed. Verify against a real server by forcing a prepare error and asserting the state is 'unknown', and with a policy of min 0 asserting 'not required'.

findings.excerpt: const bases = await api.history.mergeBase(repo, p.stream, p.head).catch(() => [] as string[])  // :30 .reflog(repo, p.stream, 500).catch(() => [])  // :33 .changeset(repo, landed).catch(() => null)  // :121 catch { authorLeases.value = [] }
findings.problem: All failures while computing the diff base are swallowed and turned into base '' (empty tree). A network blip, 403 or timeout then renders the proposal's entire tree as additions with the banner 'Comparing the empty tree with the proposal's head', i.e. a wrong diff presented as correct. For integrated proposals the reflog is capped at a hard 500 entries and falls back to parents[0] of the landed changeset, which is not the pre-integration stream head for merge integrations. loadAuthorLeases (:121) and auth.loadCapabilities (stores/auth.ts:87-93) likewise swallow errors, so IntegrateDialog silently offers no fencing tokens and the sign-in page silently hides the server's auth methods.
findings.proposed_fix: Propagate errors from diffBase into the diff resource so ChangesTab shows its ErrorState with retry; return an empty base only when the server answers that there is no merge base. Obtain the true pre-integration head from a server field on the proposal (e.g. integrated_from or the operation record) instead of searching a 500-entry reflog. Surface lease/capability load failures as a visible warning. Verify with a real server by stopping it mid-load and by integrating a merge-strategy proposal and comparing the shown diff to the changeset's real delta.

findings.excerpt: const value = await guarded('runs', mine, () => api.agents.runs(r, { limit: 100 }))  // :296 api.proposals.list(r, { state: 'open', page_size: 100 }), :297 { state: 'integrated', page_size: 6 }; RunsTable.vue:28 const limit = ref(100)
findings.problem: The board derives 'Agents running' from the newest 100 runs of any status and then filters isActive client-side. The server applies LIMIT before its active_only filter (ag-server list_runs: tx.runs(agent, limit) then retain status == 'running'; runs ordered by started_at DESC), so a long-running agent older than the newest 100 runs silently disappears from the live board, the quiet-run warnings and the lease holder mapping. Open proposals are capped at 100 the same way and BoardSummary shows board.cards.length (BoardSummary.vue:71) as the total with no truncation notice.
findings.proposed_fix: Fix the server to filter by status in SQL before LIMIT (add a runs_active query) and call it with active_only: true from the board; paginate or show 'N+ open proposals' with a link when next_page_token is non-empty (use a count field on the list response). Verify with a real server seeded with more than 100 finished runs plus one old running run and assert it appears on the board.

findings.excerpt: const from = Math.max(0, head.latestSeq - 2500)  // :21 limit: 2500  // :62 Showing events from the last ~2,500 in the repository; the audit log has the complete record.
findings.problem: A proposal's timeline is built by downloading the last 2,500 repository events and filtering them in the browser (the server cannot filter by target). In an active repository an older proposal's history falls outside the window and the tab states 'No events for this proposal yet', which is false. The window size is a hard-coded magic number and the whole 2,500-event payload is fetched on every refresh.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a server-side filter (target / ref, or a proposal-scoped events endpoint) to /events/replay or the audit endpoint and page through it; until then, never show the 'No events yet' empty state when the window did not reach seq 0, and offer 'load earlier events'. Verify against a real server with a proposal followed by more than 2,500 unrelated events.

findings.excerpt: if (isObj(p) && typeof p.min_approvals === 'number' && p.min_approvals < 1) add('warning', `protected_paths[${idx}].min_approvals`, 'A protected path with no required approvals protects nothing.')  // POLICY_SPEC at :35; summarizePolicy defaults at :357 approvalsMinForAgents: 1 and silent `return none` at :376
findings.problem: The policy editor ships a hand-copied schema (POLICY_SPEC) and validator that duplicate ag-policy and already disagree with it: the server rejects protected_paths[].min_approvals == 0 ('needs min_approvals >= 1') while the UI only warns; the server also enforces run.timeout_secs in 1..86400, valid run.env names, argv non-empty and that required_validations[].issuers appear in trusted_issuers, none of which the UI checks, so it reports 'Looks well-formed' for documents the server refuses. summarizePolicy re-implements the evaluator's defaults (approvalsMinForAgents: 1) and swallows a parse failure into a zeroed summary; board.policySummary (stores/board.ts:121) is not consumed by any component, so it is dead code that still claims to stand in for the evaluator.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the server the single source of truth: add a side-effect-free validate/dry-run operation (PUT /policy?dry_run=true or POST /policy/validate) that runs Policy::parse + validate and returns structured issues with JSON paths, and drive the editor's error list from it (debounced) while keeping only the JSON-position helper client-side. Optionally publish the policy JSON Schema generated from ag-policy in docs/protocol and generate POLICY_SPEC from it (checked in CI like check:api). Delete summarizePolicy/policySummary or feed them from a server-provided summary. Verify with a real ag-server by validating a document with min_approvals 0 and a timeout of 0 and asserting the UI shows the server's messages.

findings.excerpt: void enrich(items.slice(0, 60), mine)  // :98 watch(visible, (v) => void enrich(v.slice(0, 60), serial))  // :57 mapLimit(todo, 4, ...) and cell fallbacks counts[(row as Repo).name]?.streams ?? '–'
findings.problem: Stream and changeset counts for the repository list come from one GET per repository (N+1) for only the first 60 rows; every repository beyond the 60th (the list loads up to 1000) shows '–' permanently in the Streams and Changesets columns, and errors in the per-row requests are silently ignored. The listing endpoint documents that it leaves both counts at 0, so the UI works around a missing server capability with a placeholder.
findings.proposed_fix: Have the list endpoint return real counts (cheap metadata counts) or add a batch describe endpoint, then drop enrich(); if counts must stay lazy, fetch for rows as they scroll into view (virtualised table) and show an explicit 'unavailable' state on failure. Verify against a real server with more than 60 repositories.

findings.excerpt: await api.agents.extendLease(props.repo, l.id, 15 * 60_000)  // :65 toasts.ok('Lease extended by 15 minutes', l.scope)
findings.problem: The Extend action always extends by a fixed 15 minutes; the operator cannot choose a duration or learn the server's maximum lease TTL, and the number is an unnamed magic constant duplicated in the toast text.
findings.proposed_fix: Show a small duration picker (or a dialog) defaulting to the lease's original TTL (expires_at_ms - acquired_at_ms) and bounded by a server-advertised maximum; name the constant and build the toast text from the chosen value. Verify with a real server by extending a lease and checking the new expires_at_ms.

findings.excerpt: const POLL_MS = 8000  // components/agents/RunsTable.vue:40 setInterval(() => void runs.reload(), 10_000); api/sse.ts:203 timeoutMs: 20_000, :169 stallMs = 60_000; api/instance.ts:25 baseUrl: ''; stores/auth.ts:67 left - 120_000; stores/toasts.ts:50 9000/7000/4500; views/BoardView.vue:50 6000; stores/live.ts:12-13 KEEP = 300, BASELINE = 120; stores/board.ts:369 coalesce(flush, 180)
findings.problem: Operational timings and limits are scattered literals with no configuration surface: two different heartbeat polling intervals (8 s on the board, 10 s on the Agents page), the SSE connect deadline and 60 s stall watchdog (coupled to the server's own hard-coded 25 s keep-alive in http.rs), the API base URL (same-origin only, so a UI hosted apart from the API cannot be pointed at it outside the dev proxy), the credential-expiry warning window and the activity buffer sizes. An operator behind a slow proxy or with a different keep-alive cannot tune any of them.
findings.proposed_fix: Collect them into one documented config module (src/config.ts) with named constants, share a single poll interval between board and RunsTable, and allow overrides from a small runtime /config.json (or window.__AG_CONFIG__) served by ag-server next to the built files (web_dir), including apiBase. Ideally let the server advertise its SSE keep-alive and heartbeat expectations in capabilities so the stall watchdog is derived (e.g. 2.5 x keep-alive). Verify with e2e that a /config.json override changes the poll interval and base URL.

findings.excerpt: const DEFAULT_LIMIT = 1024 * 1024  // :23 const HARD_LIMIT = 8 * 1024 * 1024; components/admin/CredentialsManager.vue:64 const TTLS = [ 15 minutes ... 30 days ]; :364 hint="The server caps lifetimes (agents: at most an hour by default)."
findings.problem: The UI fetches /v1/capabilities (auth.capabilities) but only displays auth_methods and versions; it ignores capabilities.limits (max_object_bytes, max_page_size, max_request_bytes). Instead it hard-codes the file viewer ceilings (1 MiB / 8 MiB), page sizes (200 repos and directory entries, 100, 50) and a fixed credential-lifetime menu whose upper bound (30 days) and the 'agents: at most an hour' hint restate server config values (auth max_ttl_secs / max_agent_ttl_secs) that an operator can change, so the menu can offer lifetimes the server will refuse or omit ones it allows.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive the viewer ceilings and page sizes from capabilities.limits (clamp to max_page_size / max_object_bytes), and advertise the credential TTL caps (max_ttl_secs, max_agent_ttl_secs) in capabilities so the TTL select and its hint are built from them. Verify with a real ag-server started with a non-default max_ttl_secs and assert the select options and the hint change accordingly.

findings.excerpt: none: you can see only what is public
findings.problem: For a principal with no roles the card claims they can see 'what is public'. The server has no notion of public repositories (authorisation is purely role bindings; only /healthz and /v1/capabilities are unauthenticated), and RolesManager.vue:163 says the opposite ('Without a role, a user cannot even see that a repository exists').
findings.proposed_fix: Change to 'none: you cannot see any repository until an administrator grants you a role'. Verify with a real credential that has no bindings and assert GET /v1/repos returns an empty list.

findings.excerpt: are shown; compare narrower paths to see the rest.
findings.problem: The truncation notice tells the user to 'compare narrower paths', but neither the Compare page nor the proposal Changes tab has a path filter, although the diff operation accepts paths[] and endpoints.ts already types it. The advertised remedy cannot be used from the UI. Likewise ChangesTab.vue says 'Context is three lines' as a fixed context: 3 (useProposalData.ts:92, CompareView, ChangesetDetail).
findings.proposed_fix: Add a 'Paths' input (comma separated globs/paths) to CompareView and a per-file 'show full diff' action on the proposal and changeset views that re-requests diff with paths and a larger context; or reword the notice to what is possible. Verify against a real server with a diff larger than the server's truncation limit.

findings.excerpt: api.streams.reflog(repo.value, selected.value, 100)  // :172 subtitle="Append-only record of every head move"
findings.problem: The reflog card is subtitled 'every head move' but silently shows only the newest 100 entries with no paging or truncation notice.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a Load more control driven by a paged reflog (page_token) or at least show '100 most recent' when the limit is reached. Verify against a stream with more than 100 moves.

findings.excerpt: const blocked = computed(() => board.cards.length - ready.value)  // :78 {{ quiet > 0 ? `${quiet} quiet` : 'all heartbeating' }}
findings.problem: 'held back' is computed as every open proposal that is not provably ready, so proposals whose prepare result is still loading or failed are reported as held back (blocked). 'all heartbeating' is printed whenever no run is over the viewer-side threshold, including when zero agents are running.
findings.proposed_fix: Count held back only from proposals with loaded prep data and show 'checking N' separately; show 'no agents running' when activeRuns is empty. Verify with a real server while prepare is delayed.

findings.excerpt: return run.status === 'running' || run.status === 'stale'  // :19 liveness: run.status === 'stale' ? 'stale' : 'finished'; :11 DEFAULT_STALE_AFTER_MS = 120_000
findings.problem: OpenAPI defines status 'stale' as 'abandoned: no heartbeat', and the server actually stores and emits 'abandoned' (RunsTable.vue:56 even maps 'abandoned'), yet isActive() treats 'stale' as an active run and runHealth models it as live-but-quiet; if the server ever emits 'stale' a dead run would show on the board as active. The 120 s quiet threshold is a client-side guess independent of any server reaper timeout.
findings.proposed_fix: Align the status set with the server (running, completed, failed, abandoned) and fix the OpenAPI description; treat only 'running' as active; expose the server's abandonment timeout (when a reaper is configured) in capabilities and use it as the default quiet threshold. Verify with a real run that is reaped by the reaper CLI/endpoint.

findings.excerpt: export const ACTION_ROLE = { review: 'reviewer', integrate: 'integrator', ... createRepo: 'admin', admin: 'admin' } as const  // views/ReposView.vue:108 const canCreate = computed(() => auth.isAdminAnywhere); api/types.ts:65 ROLES; components/agents/AgentsList.vue:165 role options; stores/board.ts:150-154 + lib/glob.ts:16-19 scopesMayOverlap; components/admin/RolesManager.vue:27-30 client-side repoPatternMatches filter
findings.problem: Domain rules of the server are re-implemented in the browser: the role to action table, the role names, the agent role choices ('agent', 'reviewer'), the lease-overlap prefix rule and the role-binding repo filter. They are hints, but they already differ from the server (create_repo is authorised per new name via Cap::RepoCreate, not 'admin anywhere'), so controls are enabled or hidden incorrectly, and any server change silently drifts the UI.
findings.proposed_fix: Serve the effective permissions: extend /v1/whoami (or add GET /v1/repos/{owner}/{name}/permissions) to return the allowed operations per repository (and a can_create_repos flag), pass repo to /v1/roles instead of filtering locally, and take overlap data from the server's /predict and /leases responses. Remove ACTION_ROLE/ROLES duplication or generate them from the OpenAPI enums. Verify with e2e users holding only a name-scoped admin binding.

findings.excerpt: if (e instanceof ApiError && e.isNotFound && /no changesets yet/.test(e.message)) {  // FilesView.vue:75 same regex, comment 'Servers that predate the empty listing answered 404 "no changesets yet"'
findings.problem: Whether a stream is empty is decided by regex-matching the free-form English text of a 404 message. Any server wording change, localisation or proxy rewrite turns an ordinary empty state into a hard error (or the reverse), and FilesView carries compat code for server versions that no longer exist.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the server return an empty page (history log) or a typed error detail (e.g. code stream_empty) and key the UI on that; delete the legacy branch in FilesView. Verify against a real freshly created repository with no changesets.

findings.excerpt: export function __activeTickers(): number {  // api/clock.ts:27 /** For tests. */ export function resetServerClock(); lib/glob.ts:44 matchGlob and globToRegExp; lib/identity.ts:29 isHuman, samePrincipal, KIND_LABEL; lib/format.ts listSummary; api/instance.ts hasApiToken
findings.problem: Test-only hooks live in shipped modules and several exported helpers are referenced only by spec files, i.e. dead product code (matchGlob/globToRegExp, isHuman, samePrincipal, KIND_LABEL, listSummary, hasApiToken). Dead code keeps unverified behaviour in the bundle and suggests features (client-side glob matching, human detection) that nothing uses.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete the unused exports and their specs, or wire them into a real feature; move test hooks behind a test-only entry (import.meta.vitest or a separate test-utils module). Verify with tsc noUnusedExports / knip in CI.

findings.excerpt: real.value = await api.admin.gc(props.repo, { dry_run: false })  // :27 { dry_run: true }
findings.problem: The GC API accepts grace_ms and reflog_retention_ms, and endpoints.ts types them, but the panel never exposes them and always runs with server defaults; the text says young objects are kept 'for a grace period' without telling the operator how long, and the operator cannot tune retention from the UI.
findings.proposed_fix: Show the effective grace period and reflog retention (returned in GcResponse or capabilities) and add optional inputs that send grace_ms / reflog_retention_ms. Verify with a real dry run using a larger grace period and compare kept_young.

findings.excerpt: honouring `Retry-After`, with a cap. `429` is always waited out.
findings.problem: The README says 429 is always waited out, but api/client.ts (lines 223-231) stops after maxRetries (3) and rethrows when the computed wait exceeds maxRetryWaitMs (30 s), so a 429 with a long Retry-After or repeated 429s surfaces as an error.
findings.proposed_fix: Reword to 'retried up to 3 times, waiting at most 30 s per attempt' (and make those two values configurable as proposed above), or implement the unbounded wait. Verify with the existing client spec using a real server rate limit.

findings.excerpt: **a CI stand-in** claims `validate` jobs from the execution plane and submits an Ed25519-signed attestation for exactly the tree it was given. It does **not** run the command in the policy (`npm test`); it reports pass, or fail for proposals a test asks it to fail.
findings.problem: The documented end-to-end harness (e2e/, outside this audit's area but described in the web README) uses a simulated CI that signs a pass without running the check, although the real ag-worker (sandboxed execution plane) exists in the repository and is the component that produces these attestations in production. The Validated state, attestations and failing-check flows are therefore never exercised against real execution.
findings.proposed_fix: Run a real ag-worker in global-setup against the demo server with policy run specs for trivially fast commands (e.g. argv ["true"] / ["false"], network off) and drop the stand-in; keep a signing helper only for tests that need an attacker-style forged issuer. Verify that the pass and fail attestations in e2e come from the worker's identity.

findings.excerpt:
- The OpenAPI document lists `application/octet-stream` for the `200` of `objects.put`, which answers JSON
  (`{"object_id": ..., ...}`). `sdk/api-policy.json` overrides that one response; everything else about request and
  response bodies (`tree.file`, `objects.get`, `objects.put`, `events.subscribe`) comes from the document.
findings.problem: The claim is false today. openapi.json now lists `application/json` for the 200 of objects.put (`test/server-gaps.test.ts` line 140 asserts exactly that). `sdk/api-policy.json` has an empty `bodies` section (lines 62-64: "none today"), so nothing overrides the response. The README describes a workaround that no longer exists and a spec defect that has since been partly fixed. The same text is in the Python README.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete or rewrite the bullet in both READMEs (and docs/guides/sdks.md if it repeats it) to state what is true: the document lists JSON for objects.put, but its schema is still `{type: string, format: binary}` (see the PutObjectResult finding). Add a doc test, like the existing sdk/tools/sync_doc_samples.py check, that fails when a README claims an override that api-policy.json does not contain.

findings.excerpt:
* The OpenAPI document lists `application/octet-stream` for the `200` of `objects.put`, which answers JSON
  (`{"object_id": ..., ...}`). `sdk/api-policy.json` overrides that one response;
findings.problem: Same stale claim as in the TypeScript README. api-policy.json `bodies` is empty and openapi.json already lists application/json for objects.put, so no override exists.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove or correct the bullet and cover it with the same doc-consistency test as the TypeScript README.

findings.problem: The response model of objects.put is hand-written in each SDK (types.ts:38-43, sdk/python/scripts/generate.py:148-154, plus the SPECIAL signature at generate.mjs:141-142). The OpenAPI schema for that 200 is `{"type":"string","format":"binary"}` while the media type is application/json, so the wire message has no schema. The SDK types can drift from the server without any generator check. The comment also contradicts the READMEs.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a real `PutObjectResponse {object_id, stored}` message in proto/agwp and openapi.json on the server side. Point objects.put's 200 at it. Regenerate both SDKs and delete the three hand-written copies. The generators can then drop the 'objects.put' special case for the result type. Verify with test/server-gaps and test_server_gaps against a real ag-server.

findings.excerpt: timeout = httpx.Timeout(connect=30.0, read=idle_timeout_s, write=30.0, pool=30.0)
findings.problem: The event-stream connection uses fixed 30 s connect, write and pool timeouts that no client argument or CallOptions can change. They are not tied to `request_timeout_ms`. An operator behind a slow proxy, or one who wants fast failover, cannot tune them. The same line is in `_async.py:167`. The TypeScript client has no connect timeout at all for streams (transport.ts:234 `fetch(... signal: options.signal)`), so a blackholed host blocks until the OS TCP timeout. The two SDKs therefore disagree.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a `connect_timeout_ms` option (Python) and `connectTimeoutMs` (TypeScript) to the subscription options or the client config, defaulting to `request_timeout_ms`. Use it in both open_stream implementations; in TypeScript, arm an AbortController timer until the response headers arrive. Test against a real ag-server plus a listening-but-silent socket, as retries.test.ts already does for the unary path.

findings.excerpt: idle_s = (idle_timeout_ms or DEFAULT_IDLE_MS) / 1000
findings.problem: `idle_timeout_ms=0` is silently replaced by the 90 s default in Python (also line 130). In TypeScript `idleTimeoutMs: 0` disables the watchdog (sse.ts:136 `?? DEFAULT_IDLE_MS`, readSse `idleTimeoutMs > 0`). The Python argument is accepted but ignored for 0, and the watchdog can never be turned off. Python also has no equivalent of TypeScript's `reconnect: false`; `ReconnectPolicy(max_attempts=0)` still reconnects forever after a clean close that delivered events, because `failures` resets to 0.
findings.proposed_fix: Use `DEFAULT_IDLE_MS if idle_timeout_ms is None else idle_timeout_ms`. Treat 0 as 'no watchdog' by passing `read=None` to httpx. Accept `reconnect=False` and return after the first drop. Add real-server tests for both, mirroring events.test.ts.

findings.excerpt: return Number.isFinite(wait) && wait > 0 ? Math.max(base, wait + 10_000) : base;
findings.problem: The 10 s headroom added to a long-poll's `wait_ms` is an unnamed, non-configurable magic number. So is the local grace added to the deadline (line 343: `Math.min(1000, Math.max(100, Math.round(ctx.timeoutMs * 0.1)))`). The same values are duplicated in Python (_core.py:176 `wait + 10_000`, _core.py:181 `min(1000, max(100, round(timeout_ms * 0.1)))`). An operator on a high-latency link cannot tune them, and the server's `Request-Timeout` handling is not documented against them.
findings.proposed_fix: Introduce named, documented constants (`LONG_POLL_HEADROOM_MS`, `LOCAL_DEADLINE_GRACE_*`) and expose them through the existing client options (for example `longPollHeadroomMs`). Add one test that a configured value reaches the `Request-Timeout` header, against a real ag-server.

findings.excerpt: const QUERY_CSV = new Set(['topics']);
findings.problem: Query-array serialisation is chosen by the parameter name, in the generic transport (Python: _core.py:28 `_QUERY_CSV = frozenset({"topics"})`). openapi.json declares events.replay's `topics` as an array with no `style`/`explode` (OpenAPI default is repeated keys) and events.subscribe's `topics` as a comma-separated string. The server really wants commas for both. Operation-specific knowledge is therefore buried in transport code, and any future array parameter named `topics` would be mis-encoded.
findings.proposed_fix: Fix openapi.json (`style: form, explode: false` for events.replay `topics`, array type for subscribe) or add a per-operation `csvQuery` entry to api-policy.json. Have both generators emit the list into OPERATIONS, and make buildRequest/build_request use it instead of a global name set. Verify against a real ag-server with the existing events.replay topic-filter tests.

findings.problem: The `objects.upload` batch size 1000 is an unnamed constant, duplicated in Python (client.py:170-171 and 201-202). The server publishes its real limit in `NegotiateResponse.limits.max_batch` (10 000 today, crates/ag-protocol/src/lib.rs:58), but the SDK never reads it. If the limit changes, upload either under-uses it or breaks.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a named constant. Better, cache `limits.max_batch` from `negotiate()` (or fetch it lazily with `session.negotiate`) and use `min(limit, default)` as the chunk size. Test against a real ag-server by uploading more objects than the batch size.

findings.excerpt: if (connectedAt > 0 && Date.now() - connectedAt > 5000) failures = 0;
findings.problem: The 5 s 'connection was stable' window that resets the reconnect failure counter is an undocumented magic number (Python: _events.py:104 and 164 `> 5`). It cannot be changed through `ReconnectOptions` or `ReconnectPolicy`.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `stableAfterMs` to ReconnectOptions and `stable_after_ms` to ReconnectPolicy, default 5000, documented in both READMEs.

findings.excerpt: request: { repo: options.repo, after_seq: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, limit: 1 },
findings.problem: Subscribing 'from now' is implemented by replaying after an arbitrary sentinel (2^53-1, Python _events.py:30 `_PAST_THE_END`) and reading `latest_seq` from the empty answer. It relies on undocumented server behaviour that only test/server-gaps.test.ts pins. It is a side-channel trick, not a protocol operation.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an explicit protocol feature, such as `events.replay` with `after_seq` omitted plus `limit: 0` returning `latest_seq`, or a dedicated tail field on the stream. Document it in docs/protocol/agwp-v1.md and switch both SDKs to it. Keep the real-server gap test.

findings.problem: `headers()` takes a `hasBody` parameter, and all three callers compute and pass it (lines 229, 299, 329). The function never reads it. This is a dead argument that suggests behaviour, such as Content-Length or Expect handling, that does not exist.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the parameter and the computations at 229 and 329, or implement what it was meant for.

findings.excerpt:
if event is None or event.seq <= last:
                            continue  # already delivered
findings.problem: `_event()` is annotated `Event | None` but never returns None (an `error` frame raises, everything else is decoded). The `event is None` branch in subscribe_sync (line 93) and subscribe_async (line 153) is dead, so a malformed frame can never be skipped as the code suggests.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the return type to `Event` and drop the dead check. If heartbeat-like frames without data should be skipped, handle that explicitly in the parser and test it against the real server's heartbeat_ms mode.

findings.excerpt: Uint8Array.of(a.result === 'pass' ? 1 : 2),
findings.problem: Any `result` other than the exact string 'pass' is signed as 'fail' (Python signing.py:184 `bytes([1 if _get(a, "result") == "pass" else 2])`, where a missing key also becomes 'fail'). Likewise any file type other than 'symlink' is encoded as regular (changeset.ts:124, changeset.py:159). Only the TypeScript types guard this; runtime and Python callers get a silently wrong signature or changeset instead of an error.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate explicitly and throw `TypeError`/`ValueError` for any value outside {'pass','fail'} and {'regular','symlink'} (and for a missing `result`). Add unit tests plus a real-server upload of a symlink and an attestation.

findings.excerpt:
"retry": {
    "readPosts": [ ... ],
    "keyed": [ "repo.create", "objects.publish", "proposal.create", ... ],
    "natural": [ "objects.put", "repo.configure", ... ]
findings.problem: The retry class of each operation (read/natural/keyed/unsafe), which decides whether the SDK may resend a mutation, is a hand-maintained name list in the SDK repo. The server and OpenAPI do not carry it. Only the 'keyed' seven are verified by retry tests. The 'natural' list (23 operations) is asserted nowhere against real server behaviour, and a new server operation silently defaults to 'unsafe' (safe, but unreported).
findings.proposed_fix: Make the server the source of truth: add `x-agwp-retry` (and `x-agwp-idempotency`) extensions to openapi.json, generated from the Rust route table. Have both generators read them and delete the lists. Keep the real-server retry tests, and add one parametrised test that exercises every 'natural' operation twice.

findings.excerpt: "$comment": "Message-typed fields that the protocol declares optional (so the OpenAPI document says '| null') but that ag-server 0.1.0 always fills in. The SDKs type them as present; a live test per field fails if the server ever answers null."
findings.problem: The list `alwaysPresent.fields` is hand-written and pins the server version in a comment. It makes the SDKs claim a non-null type for eight optional fields (Python builds a zero-value default object, generate.py:113-114 `default_factory=lambda: {ref}()`, so an omitted `lease` becomes an empty `Lease()` rather than an error). Any other AGWP server, or a future ag-server, can answer null and the types lie. Only the contract test catches it, and only against ag-server.
findings.proposed_fix: Mark these fields `required` in the protobuf/OpenAPI schema, since the server always sets them, and drop alwaysPresent so the generators follow the document. Keep test/server-contract.test.ts and test_server_contract.py as guards.

findings.problem: The package version is duplicated by hand: pyproject.toml:7, sdk/typescript/package.json:3 and this line. Nothing checks that they agree, and the SDK never reports its version to the server (`negotiate()` sends client_name/client_version only if the caller supplies them).
findings.proposed_fix: Read the version at runtime from `importlib.metadata.version('agentgit-client')`, or generate the module from pyproject. Add a CI check that the Python and npm versions match, and send `client_name`/`client_version` by default in `negotiate()`.

findings.problem: Public client options exist only as test seams (Python: client.py:263-264 and 557-558). They are ordinary dependency injection, not a fake, but they put test-only behaviour in the production API surface, and the doc comments say so. Borderline.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep them but mark them `@internal`/underscore-prefixed (or move them to a `testing` entry point). The real-network tests already use recordedSleep; no behaviour change is required.

findings.problem: Unit tests use a canned `fetch` against the fake host `http://srv.test`, returning an invented `{}`, an invented objects.put answer (lines 184-187) and an invented negotiate answer `{"protocol_version":"agwp.v1","features":[],"auth_methods":[]}` (lines 212-217). A real ag-server is available to this suite (test/harness/server.ts) and FaultyNetwork already records requests over the real network. The Python twin is test_unit.py:100-105, 151-153, 168-172, 180-181 with `httpx.MockTransport` and `BASE = "http://srv.test"`. Only the stuck-page-token (pagination.test.ts:116, test_pagination.py:101), `agwp.v9` (negotiation-and-errors.test.ts:23) and empty-405 cases truly need a double, because the real server cannot produce them.
findings.proposed_fix: Run the header/URL/token/withRun/negotiate/objects.put checks through `FaultyNetwork` (TS) or `FaultyTransport` (Python) wrapped around the real ag-server, as retries.test.ts does. Keep the canned responses only for the three pathological server behaviours listed above, and say why in a comment.

findings.excerpt: '/home/user/bin/ag-server',
findings.problem: The test harness searches a developer-machine-specific absolute path (Python: sdk/python/tests/harness.py:36). Both READMEs advertise it as a supported location (typescript/README.md:398, python/README.md:430). It is an environment assumption baked into the harness and the docs, and it is wrong on every machine except one.
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve the binary from `AG_SERVER_BIN`, then `target/{debug,release}/ag-server` (optionally `which ag-server`). Drop the /home/user path from the harnesses and READMEs.

findings.excerpt: const m = /(?:addr=|listening[^\n]*?)(127\.0\.0\.1:\d+)/.exec(log.replace(ANSI, ''));
findings.problem: Both harnesses discover the server's port by regex-scraping its human-readable log (Python harness.py:142-144, `m and "listening" in line`). A log wording or format change breaks every SDK test. ag-server has no machine-readable way to report its bound address (server.rs:205/211 only log it).
findings.proposed_fix: Add a `--addr-file <path>` (or JSON line on stdout) option to `ag-server serve` that writes the bound address once it is listening. Have both harnesses read that instead of the log.

findings.excerpt: check(Object.keys(m.OPERATIONS).length === 91, `${name}: 91 operations`);
findings.problem: The package check hardcodes the operation count (the READMEs say '91 operations' too: typescript/README.md:7, python/README.md:8). It fails on every legitimate API addition, and the READMEs go stale silently.
findings.proposed_fix: Compare with the number of operations in docs/protocol/openapi.json read at check time. Generate the number in the READMEs, or drop it from the prose.

findings.excerpt: - **No runtime dependencies.** `fetch`, `AbortSignal` and `ReadableStream` are the only platform APIs used.
findings.problem: The code also uses `globalThis.crypto.getRandomValues` (encoding.ts:128), `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder`, `Headers`, `Response`, `URLSearchParams`, `AbortController`, `DOMException` and timers. The sentence understates the platform requirements, and the README itself says the package 'has not been run in a browser'.
findings.proposed_fix: List the real requirements (Web Crypto `getRandomValues`, Fetch API, Streams, TextEncoder) or drop the 'only' claim. Add a smoke test that loads the built package under a minimal global surface, or run the suite in a browser-like runtime.

findings.excerpt: * **Python 3.10 or newer.** The test suite passes on 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13; newer versions are not run here.
findings.problem: CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml, `sdk` job, lines 168-195) runs the Python SDK on a single interpreter (`uv sync` default) and the TypeScript SDK on Node 22 only. The claims 'passes on 3.10-3.13' (and the TypeScript README line 13, 'tests were run on 20.20 and 22.22', with `engines.node >=20`) are not backed by any automated matrix.
findings.proposed_fix: Add matrix jobs: python-version [3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13] with `uv run --python`, and node [20, 22], each running the real-server suite. Otherwise narrow the claim to what CI actually runs.

findings.excerpt: // scriptedExecutor is a built-in stand-in for an agent, for tests and demos.  ...  Model: s.cfg.Model, PromptDigest: hex.EncodeToString(digest[:]), Rationale: s.cfg.Rationale,  (scripted.go:100)  ...  if s.cfg.Delay > 0 { clock.Sleep(ctx, env.Clock, s.cfg.Delay) } (scripted.go:65-69)
findings.problem: A simulated agent ships in the production binary and is selectable by any production config via `type: scripted` (config.go:145,161-171,465-473; check.go:164-165 reports it as 'ok'; examples/orchestrator.yaml:43-49; README.md:260-262). It writes operator-supplied canned files, and it signs real provenance whose `model` and `rationale` are free text from the config (not what produced the change), so the audit trail can carry claims no model run backs. `delay` is a literal sleep standing in for work. This is exactly the 'simulated behaviour / stand-in' the product must not contain.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove `type: scripted`, `Scripted` config and `scriptedExecutor` from the shipped binary. Product executors are only `command`. For tests/demos build a separate test-only agent (a small Go `main` under integration/ built in TestMain, or the real `ag` CLI which already honours AG_TOKEN/AG_RUN/AG_KEY_FILE) and run it through the normal `command` executor. Keep the end-to-end proof: the real ag-server must still verify the agent's provenance signature (dependency_test.go). Update README, examples, config tests and check.go accordingly.

findings.excerpt: // Package fakeagwp is an in-memory AGWP v1 HTTP/JSON server for unit tests. ... It does NOT merge anything: tests script preparations and file contents directly.
findings.problem: An in-memory fake of the whole AGWP server (~2000 lines) is the backbone of the unit tests of advisor, app, cmd/orchestrator, events, execsched, review, scheduler, semindex and session (74 references in 14 files). The real server is feasible: the integration suite already starts the real `ag-server` per test, and CI builds it (`cargo build -p ag-server`, .github/workflows/ci.yml:205) and exports AG_SERVER_BIN. The fake re-implements authorization (roleAllows/capOf/readerCaps), scope containment, run/task/lease semantics, event feed, merge-base, diff and prepare, none of which is checked against the real server (see separate findings), so unit tests can pass while the product is wrong, and the fake must be kept in sync by hand.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the fake with a shared test harness that starts the real ag-server (move startServer/newWorld from integration/harness_test.go into an importable internal/testutil/realserver package, with the same AG_SERVER_BIN lookup) and port the unit tests of the nine packages to it; reuse the world helpers to create repos, roles, policies, tasks, proposals. Keep fault injection (429/500/dropped SSE) by putting a thin fault-injecting reverse proxy in front of the real server instead of re-implementing the server. Then delete internal/testutil/fakeagwp and the README mentions (README.md:90,315-317).

findings.excerpt: // ---- the CI worker (the trusted execution plane, played by the test) ---- ... "environment_digest": "env-test" ... map[string]any{"worker": "ci-test", "attestation": att, "result_json": map[string]any{"exit": 0}}
findings.problem: The trusted execution-plane worker is a hand-written test double (ciWorker.claim/complete) that signs a passing or failing attestation without running the policy's check (policy run argv is just ["true"]) and with a made-up environment digest. The real component exists in the repo (crates/ag-worker, `ag-worker run`, with `--sandbox process --insecure-allow-process-sandbox` suitable for CI) and CI does not build it, so the orchestrator's execution-scheduler path is never proven against a real claim -> sandboxed run -> attestation cycle; the test also re-implements the attestation canonical byte layout (canonStr/canonVarint), which can drift from the Rust implementation.
findings.proposed_fix: Build ag-worker in the orchestrator CI job (`cargo build -p ag-server -p ag-worker`), have the harness `ag-worker keygen`, put its public key in `trusted_issuers`, run `ag-worker run` against the test server and let it execute a real check (e.g. a command that passes and one that fails). Delete ciWorker.complete/canon* helpers. Assert the failed-validation and moved-head scenarios against real worker output.

findings.problem: A literal stub: the fake invents queued validation jobs that the real server does not return in this situation, and the execsched unit tests (validation-job counting, ValidationsQueued metric) assert on these invented jobs, so they prove behaviour the real server does not have.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete StubJobs. Cover job queueing/dedup only through the real server (integration/execsched_test.go already does for a policy with required_validations) and port the remaining unit assertions to a real-server test with a policy that requires checks.

findings.excerpt: e := agwp.ProvenanceEntry{ID: int64(len(r.provenance) + 1), Record: in.Record, PublicKey: a.PublicKey, Signature: in.Signature, Verified: true}
findings.problem: The fake marks every provenance record `Verified: true` after checking only that the signature string is 128 characters long (line 623); the real server verifies the Ed25519 signature over the canonical bytes. Any session/scripted-executor test that relies on `Verified` passes with garbage signatures and cannot detect a regression in agwp/provenance.go CanonicalBytes or agentkey.Sign.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove with the fake; assert provenance verification against the real ag-server only (dependency_test.go:73 already checks `Verified`). Add a test where a record is signed with the wrong key / tampered payload and the real server rejects or reports verified=false.

findings.excerpt:
if sp, ok := r.prepares[p.ID]; ok {
	cp := *sp ... return nonNilPrep(cp)  // SetPreparation(repo, proposal, agwp.Preparation{...}); SetPredict(...) at handlers.go:273-278
findings.problem: Tests hand-write the answer of integration.prepare and agent.predict (execsched_test.go has 14 such scripted calls, advisor_test.go others). The classification in execsched.classify, the advisor's conflict handling and the scheduler's predicted-overlap deferral are therefore validated against the test author's idea of the server's JSON, not against what the real server returns (README.md:340-347 itself documents a real-server prepare race that a scripted answer cannot exhibit).
findings.proposed_fix: Produce conflicts, blockers, validations and overlaps by constructing the real situations on the real server (two workspaces editing the same lines; policy with approvals/required checks; overlapping leases/task scopes) as integration/advisor_test.go and dependency_test.go already do, and drop SetPreparation/SetPredict.

findings.excerpt: return agwp.SyncResult{Status: "up_to_date", Head: w.Head, Conflicts: []agwp.Conflict{}}, 0, nil   |   admin.policy.set: return map[string]any{"stream": in["stream"], "version": 1}, 0, nil (line 517)   |   queue.list: {"entries": []agwp.QueueEntry{}} (519)   |   tree.diff: "truncated": false (607)   |   proposal.list: "next_page_token": "" (390)
findings.problem: Several fake endpoints return canned constants: workspace.sync never merges or conflicts, policy.set stores nothing and always answers version 1, the integration queue is always empty, diffs are never truncated, lists are never paginated, tree/blob ids are `tree-<12 hex>`/`blob-<hash>` instead of real content ids, negotiate advertises a fixed feature list with ServerVersion "fake" (server.go:808), whoami returns a fixed `*:<role>` (server.go:818), minted credentials always get role `writer` (handlers.go:837). Code paths depending on those behaviours (diff truncation flag in review, pagination loops in agwp.ListProposals/GetTree, queue view in /status) are only tested against the constant.
