findings.proposed_fix: Same as the fake itself: drop it and test against the real server, adding scenarios for truncated diffs (large change), >1000-item pagination (many tasks/proposals), a non-empty integration queue, and real policy versions.

findings.excerpt:
// The fake is test infrastructure, so these tests pin the behaviours other
// packages rely on to be faithful to the real server.   (README.md:315-317: "an in-memory fake AGWP server ... that mimics the real error model")
findings.problem: Fidelity to the real server is claimed but never verified: these tests exercise the fake against itself. No conformance test runs the same requests against the real ag-server and compares codes, retryable flags, status codes, ordering or error text, so the claim cannot be trusted and drift is invisible.
findings.proposed_fix: If any fake survives, add a conformance suite that replays an identical request script against the fake and the real ag-server (when AG_SERVER_BIN is set) and fails on any difference in status/code/body shape. Preferably delete the fake (see the first fakeagwp finding).

findings.problem: The only suite that runs against the real server silently turns into skips when the binary is not found. A mis-set AG_SERVER_BIN or a changed build path in CI (ci.yml:205-214) would keep the job green with zero real-server coverage, while the unit tests (all on the fake) still pass.
findings.proposed_fix: Fail instead of skip when `CI` is set or when `AG_REQUIRE_SERVER=1`; have the CI job set it and additionally assert that at least N integration tests ran (e.g. `go test -json` count check).

findings.excerpt: jitter: func() float64 { return 0.5 }, maxBody: 64 << 20,    // doc at line 270: "backoff is the exponential step ... with ±20% jitter"
findings.problem: The default jitter source is the constant 0.5, so production backoff (HTTP retries, client.go:276) and SSE reconnects (sse.go:128) have no jitter at all although the code and comments promise ±20%. app.go never calls WithJitter. After a server restart every orchestrator client and every repository follower retries in lock-step (thundering herd). maxBody 64 MiB is also fixed and not configurable.
findings.proposed_fix: Default `jitter` to `rand.Float64` (math/rand/v2) and keep WithJitter only for tests; verify with a unit test that two clients produce different delays and that delays stay within ±20%. Expose max response size via config if operators need it.

findings.problem: The same helper generates the Idempotency-Key (newKey, client.go:448). If the RNG fails, every mutation is sent with the identical key `orch-000...0`; the server then replays the first recorded response for a different request or answers idempotency_key_reused, i.e. a mutation (proposal.create, lease.acquire, run start) can be silently answered with another request's result. The comment is wrong for idempotency keys.
findings.proposed_fix: Make newKey/newRequestID return an error (or panic, as crypto/rand failure is unrecoverable) instead of a constant; propagate from `do` as a hard failure. Unit-test the error path with an injectable reader.

findings.problem: When the reviewer/advisor credential variable is unset the components are still enabled and wired to the orchestrator's own credential, which by design lacks proposal.review (README.md:127-129, requirements.go:21-26). In `run` this only produces a warning; afterwards every review/advice pass is guaranteed to fail with permission_denied and be logged as a reconcile error forever. It is a fallback that cannot work (silently does nothing useful) and the warning text ('posted with the orchestrator's identity') is misleading.
findings.proposed_fix: Make it a startup error (or automatically disable review/advisor for that repo and show `disabled: no credential` in /status and /readyz) instead of falling back; keep the fallback out of the code. Verify with an integration test: start without AG_REVIEWER_TOKEN and assert the documented behaviour against the real server.

findings.problem: If the server's conflict prediction fails (permission, 5xx, timeout) the scheduler silently proceeds as if there were no overlaps (debug log only, no metric, nothing in /status) and starts overlapping work that `placement: avoid` is supposed to defer. A swallowed error that hides lost functionality.
findings.proposed_fix: Log at warn, count it (e.g. orchestrator_prediction_errors_total), expose `prediction_error` in scheduler Status, and make the behaviour explicit and configurable (`placement_on_predict_error: defer|start`, default defer). Test against the real server with a credential lacking `predict`.

findings.excerpt:
mu        sync.Mutex
attempts  map[string]int
tempFails map[string]int
retryAt   map[string]time.Time
awaiting  map[string]awaitInfo   // in-memory only; candidates() adopts any in_progress task with attempts==0 (line 349)
findings.problem: The retry budget (`schedule.attempts`, README.md:166), the EX_TEMPFAIL counter and the backoff timers live only in process memory. After an orchestrator restart a task that failed and was waiting for retry is in_progress with no live run, so it is adopted as attempt 1 again: `attempts: N` and the 'at most ten' tempfail limit are not honoured across restarts, and a crash-looping orchestrator or executor can retry a task without bound.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive attempts from server state: count the task's finished failed runs (ListRuns by task/agent, run summaries already record attempt numbers) when rebuilding after restart, and persist retryAt/tempFails in state_dir or as run summaries. Verify with an integration test that restarts the orchestrator between attempts (harness already supports StateDir reuse).

findings.problem: `approved` is inferred from the absence of two blocker codes. A proposal with no review at all is reported `approved: yes` when the policy requires no approvals, and also when a partial/odd preparation simply lacks the blocker; the 'four independent states' (README.md:26) therefore show a state that nobody established. `ready_to_integrate` (line 438) is derived from it.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute approval from real data: read the proposal's reviews (GetProposal) for the current head and the policy's approval requirement from the preparation; report `na` when the policy requires none, `unknown` when preparation lacks the information, `yes` only when the server confirms enough approving reviews. Add integration cases for min:0 policies and request_changes.

findings.problem: For a proposal into an empty stream only the first 60 files are fetched, files over 128 KiB or that fail to download are skipped with the error swallowed, and the rest are counted as added with 0 lines and no patch. Secret scanning, size and test checks therefore silently never see most of an initial import, and the summary does not say so (Truncated stays false), while the comment claims to have inspected the change. The limits are not configurable.
findings.proposed_fix: Inspect all files (page through the tree; use the server's tree.diff against the empty tree if supported) or, when a limit applies, set Summary.Truncated and name the uninspected files in the comment; surface fetch errors. Move the limits to `review:` config. Test against the real server with an initial import containing a planted secret in file #61.

findings.problem: Proposal analysis ignores the documented/configured `index.max_file_bytes` (config.go:137, README.md:185, default 256 KiB) and `index.max_files`, using its own fixed 512 KiB / 30 / 10 instead: a configured argument that is accepted and ignored for half of the semantic index, and an operator cannot tune it.
findings.proposed_fix: Use c.o.Repo.Index.MaxBytes for GetFile and add configurable `index.proposal_max_files` and `index.proposals_per_pass`; mark `Partial` with the reason. Cover by a test that sets a small max_file_bytes and expects the proposal file to be skipped.

findings.excerpt: rt.advisor = advisor.New(advisor.Options{Repo: rc, API: a.advisorClient, Clock: a.clk, Metrics: a.metrics, Log: a.log})   // advisor.go:105: if o.Advisor == nil { o.Advisor = Rules{MaxFileBytes: o.Repo.Advisor.MaxFile} }
findings.problem: README.md:26 and rules.go:26-30 say the advisor is 'behind an Advisor interface so a smarter one can replace it', but nothing in config or wiring can select another implementation: Options.Advisor is never set and there is no registry/config key, so the interface is unreachable in the product. What ships is a regex/line-rule engine (rules.go: per-language import-line regexes, whitespace folding, 'union' of list entries) presented as a 'Conflict advisor'. It is disclosed as deterministic (README.md:360-363) but is heuristic matching, not analysis of code semantics.
findings.proposed_fix: Either implement the extension point for real (config `advisor.kind` with a registered, tested second implementation, e.g. an external command/HTTP advisor that receives base/ours/theirs and returns Suggestions, verified against real conflicting workspaces) or delete the claim. For the rules engine, validate suggestions by applying them through the real server (workspace sync with `resolutions` then prepare) before posting 'Complete' ones, and drop confidence labels that are not measured.

findings.excerpt: rt.review, err = review.New(review.Options{Repo: rc, API: a.reviewer, Reviewer: "service:reviewer", ...
findings.problem: The reviewer identity printed in every posted comment ('<sub>... run by a service identity (service:reviewer)') is a hardcoded string, not the identity the credential really authenticates as (known from Whoami in Preflight). With the fallback credential or a differently named service account the comment states the wrong author.
findings.proposed_fix: Take the identity from a.principals["reviewer"].Identity after preflight (pass a func or set it in Run) and test against the real server with a reviewer credential minted for a different subject name.

findings.problem: Nothing is redacted or re-checked: `orchestrator config` marshals the whole struct, including `executors[].env` values and `scripted.files`, which may hold secrets pasted by an operator. Validation only checks that *_env names match an identifier regex, which a token like `agt_cred_abc...` also satisfies, and the resulting 'environment variable <token> is empty or unset' error (config.go:407,425) then echoes the pasted token. The 'never carries a token' guarantee is not implemented.
findings.proposed_fix: Implement real redaction in Redacted (mask env values whose keys look secret and all `env` values by default) and reject values of the form of known credentials in the file (agt_ prefix, high-entropy strings in *_env fields) without echoing them in messages; add tests for both.

findings.problem: `check` re-implements the server's role-binding repo patterns with only exact / `*` / trailing-`*` support, whereas the server matches them with the globset crate (crates/ag-server/src/authz.rs:240 glob_match: `?`, `[..]`, `{a,b}`, inner `*`). A valid binding such as `acme/we?` or `*/web` makes `check` report a false 'no admin role on <repo>' error (check.go:91-93).
findings.proposed_fix: Do not guess: determine access by a real probe per repository (an admin-only dry call or a minting attempt with the exact scope) or at least compile the pattern with the repo's glob package using globset semantics; add a test against the real server with a wildcard binding.

findings.excerpt:
// maxSymbols bounds the derived tables: beyond it, further definitions are not indexed.
const maxSymbols = 200_000   (rebuildLocked: if x.symbols >= maxSymbols { break }, line 132)  |  extract.go:49-51 maxDefsPerFile = 500, maxIdentsPerFile = 512; extract.go:98-100 defs = defs[:maxDefsPerFile]
findings.problem: Definitions beyond 200,000 in total, 500 per file, and identifiers beyond 512 per file are dropped without any counter, log or field in /index/status (Skipped covers only files), so symbol queries and `references` counts are silently incomplete on large repositories; none of the limits can be tuned.
findings.proposed_fix: Count dropped definitions/identifiers in Skipped/Stats and metrics, log once per sync, and move the limits to `index:` config (max_symbols, max_defs_per_file, max_idents_per_file). Test on a generated large file / repository.

findings.excerpt:
// Package semindex is a lightweight, incremental symbol index ... They are careful line-based scanners, not parsers: ... 
// index.go:162: References is the heuristic count of identifier occurrences across the indexed files
findings.problem: The 'semantic index' and 'semantic overlap' are regex line scanners plus identifier-text counting: no scopes, no types, no imports resolution, so `references` counts every textual occurrence of a name (including other symbols with the same name, strings, comments) and `caller_affected` overlaps (overlap.go:327-342) are name matches. Disclosed in README.md:361-363 and docs/guides/orchestrator.md:386-387, but the feature name and API (`/index/files`, `references`) suggest more than it does.
findings.proposed_fix: Back the index with real parsers: go/parser+go/types (or SCIP indexers such as scip-go, rust-analyzer, scip-typescript, scip-python) or tree-sitter grammars, and compute references from resolved symbols; verify against fixtures with homonymous symbols. Until then rename to 'symbol index' and mark `references` as textual.

findings.problem: The reviewers are keyword/regex/entropy heuristics (README.md:27, 360-363 discloses it) with thresholds an operator cannot tune and a fixed secret-rule set that cannot be extended (only an allow-list exists); the test-presence check is a filename convention. Findings such as 'Source changes without test changes' or a missed secret depend on these fixed numbers and patterns.
findings.proposed_fix: Expose the thresholds and add `review.secret_rules` (name+regexp) and `review.test_paths` to config; for secrets, optionally run a real scanner (gitleaks/trufflehog rules) as a `command` check. Validate with the planted-secret integration test plus false-positive fixtures.

findings.problem: The advisor re-implements the Rust merge engine's clustering rule in Go and claims equivalence without any cross-check, and silently degrades to 'one big replaced block' (-> 'needs a person') above fixed limits. If the server's merge changes, the advisor's regions will disagree with the server's real conflicts without any test failing.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a conformance test that generates random three-way inputs, applies them through the real ag-server (two workspaces, sync with and without resolutions) and compares conflict regions with Merge3; make the limits configurable and report when the degradation happened in the suggestion notes.

findings.excerpt:
case errors.Is(err, agwp.ErrResponseTooLarge):
	return &File{Content: make([]byte, max+1)}, nil // reported as "too large" by the rules
findings.problem: A zero-filled placeholder buffer of up to max+1 bytes (1 MiB by default) is fabricated to signal 'too large' to the rules via its length, instead of carrying the condition explicitly; it allocates needlessly and any rule that looks at content would see fake data.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `TooLarge bool` (and Size) to advisor.File, have Rules.Suggest check it, and drop the fabricated buffer; unit-test with the real server returning too_large for an oversized file.

findings.problem: Refresh (15s) and Recent (20) are never wired to config (app.go:209 does not set them), ListJobs is capped at a fixed 200, and errors from ListJobs/ListQueue are swallowed so /status shows a stale or empty validation/integration queue without any error indication.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `validations.refresh`, `validations.recent` and `validations.jobs_limit` to config, and record job/queue listing errors in Status.LastError (or separate fields). Test with a credential lacking jobs.read/queue.read against the real server.

findings.excerpt: agwp.WithRetry(agwp.RetryPolicy{MaxAttempts: a.cfg.Server.RetryMax, BaseDelay: 250 * time.Millisecond, MaxDelay: 5 * time.Second, MaxRetryAfter: 30 * time.Second})  |  sse.go:62-70 HeartbeatMs 15000, IdleTimeout 60s, BackoffBase 500ms, BackoffMax 30s  |  app.go:127 MaxIdleConnsPerHost = 8 (also client.go:154)
findings.problem: Only the attempt count of the HTTP retry policy is configurable; base/max delay, the Retry-After cap, SSE heartbeat request, reconnect backoff and connection-pool size are fixed in code, so operators cannot adapt the client to a slower server, a strict rate limiter or many repositories.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `server.retry: {base, max, max_retry_after}`, `server.stream: {heartbeat, backoff_base, backoff_max}` and `server.max_idle_conns` to config with the current values as defaults, validated in config.validate and shown by `orchestrator config`.

findings.excerpt: left < 72*time.Hour (app.go:305, check.go:134)  |  left < 24*time.Hour (app.go:439)  |  clock.Sleep(ctx, a.clk, 10*time.Minute) (app.go:425)  |  context.WithTimeout(ctx, 30*time.Second) (app.go:394)  |  sctx := WithTimeout(..., 5*time.Second) (app.go:374)  |  admin http.Server timeouts (admin.go:154-155)  |  doCheck 60*time.Second (main.go:141)
findings.problem: Operational timing constants (credential expiry warning thresholds, credential re-check interval, preflight timeout and backoff cap, HTTP shutdown timeout, admin server read/write timeouts, `check` deadline) are fixed and undocumented; check.go and app.go also use time.Until instead of the injected clock.
findings.proposed_fix: Name the constants, document them, and expose the ones an operator would tune (`credential_warn_before`, `check.timeout`, `admin.timeouts`) in config; use a.clk for expiry maths so it can be tested.

findings.excerpt: if len(summary) > 2000 { summary = summary[:2000] + "..." }; for attempt := 0; attempt < 3; attempt++ { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second) ... (manager.go:274-285)  |  TTLSecs: 60 (manager.go:295)  |  session.go:185 heartbeat 10s, session.go:257-267 finishTask 3x15s with real time.Sleep, session.go:336-376 stderr tail 512/600/500, session.go:351 result file 8<<10  |  command.go:42 cmd.WaitDelay = 2 * time.Second  |  scheduler.go:212 ListRuns limit 1000, scheduler.go:488 stale := max(3*ex.Beat, time.Minute)
findings.problem: Retry counts, per-call timeouts, summary/stderr/result sizes, the finish-task credential TTL, the WaitDelay for orphaned pipe holders and the orphan-staleness rule are magic numbers scattered through session handling; none is configurable and finishTask sleeps with the real clock (time.Sleep) instead of the injected one. Active runs above 1000 would not be seen by the orphan reaper.
findings.proposed_fix: Gather them into named, documented constants with config overrides where operationally relevant (`executors[].wait_delay`, `schedule.orphan_after`, summary/tail limits), replace time.Sleep with clock.Sleep, and paginate ListRuns instead of a fixed 1000.

findings.excerpt:
# NOTE: this Dockerfile has not been built by its authors (the machine it was
# written on has a Docker client but no daemon). ...  ARG VERSION=dev   (app.go:37: var Version = "dev")
findings.problem: The only packaging of the service is unbuilt and untested; neither .github/workflows/ci.yml nor release.yml nor deploy/ builds or references the orchestrator image, so no shipped artifact carries a real version (Version stays "dev", User-Agent `agentgit-orchestrator/dev`). README.md:354-356 admits it.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a CI job that `docker build`s the image, runs `orchestrator version`, `check` and a smoke `run` against a real ag-server container (compose), and wire release.yml to pass VERSION=${tag}; then remove the NOTE and the README caveat.

findings.excerpt:
URL=http://127.0.0.1:18090
ADMIN=http://127.0.0.1:19090
BOOT=worked-example-bootstrap-token-0123456789abcdef
findings.problem: The runnable example fixes the server and admin ports and uses a hardcoded, publicly visible bootstrap admin token exported into the server's environment; if someone adapts the script to a reachable host it is an admin credential everybody knows. The script also defaults the tool paths (ag-server on PATH).
findings.proposed_fix: Generate the bootstrap token at run time (e.g. `openssl rand -hex 24` / `head -c24 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1`) and pick free ports (or take them from env), keeping the throw-away loopback behaviour.

findings.excerpt: The binary is taken from `$AG_SERVER_BIN`, then `PATH`, then `/home/user/bin/ag-server`; the tests skip with a message when there is none.   (harness_test.go:52, integration/doc.go:6)
findings.problem: A developer-machine path (`/home/user/bin/ag-server`) is part of the documented and coded lookup order, i.e. an environment assumption baked into docs and test harness.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the machine-specific fallback; require AG_SERVER_BIN or PATH (or build it with `cargo build -p ag-server` and use target/debug/ag-server relative to the repo root found via `go env GOMOD`).

findings.excerpt: // Operations in this file are NOT used by any orchestrator component. They exist for operators' tooling and for the test suites ...  |  clock.go:71 "Fake is a manually advanced clock for tests."  |  manager.go:342 "Close is Shutdown(cancel) with a short deadline, for tests."  |  client.go:116 WithJitter "(tests)"; agentkey.go:50 FromSeed "(tests)"
findings.problem: Test-support code is compiled into production packages: admin-only client operations (Integrate, SetPolicy, GrantRole, CreateRepo, CreateTask, CloseProposal), clock.Fake, Manager.Close, WithJitter, FromSeed. The structural test (integration/structure_test.go) enforces the trust boundary only by selector name, so the production client library carries the very operations the service promises never to use. Borderline: the code is real, but it is not product code.
findings.proposed_fix: Move the admin operations to a separate package (e.g. internal/agwp/agwpadmin or internal/testutil/admin) imported only by tests, and move clock.Fake to internal/testutil/clocktest; delete Manager.Close or move it to a _test helper. Then the structural test can forbid importing that package from non-test code, which is stronger than matching method names.

findings.excerpt: image: ghcr.io/paffin/agentgit-server:latest   (also kustomization.yaml:19 `newTag: latest`, compose.yaml:59 `${AG_VERSION:-latest}`; release.yml:104-105 pushes only `ghcr.io/paffin/agentgit-server:${{ needs.verify.outputs.version }}`)
findings.problem: Every shipped deployment default points at the `latest` tag, but the release workflow never pushes `latest` (only X.Y.Z), and no tag or release exists at all (`git tag -l` is empty). `kubectl apply -k deploy/kubernetes/base` therefore ends in ImagePullBackOff. The documented remedy (pin 0.1.0, .env.example:27 `AG_VERSION=0.1.0`, kustomization.yaml:19 comment) points at an image that does not exist either. Compose only works because `up --build` builds locally under that name.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the default resolvable: have release.yml also push `latest` (docker/metadata-action; `latest` only for non-prerelease tags) and publish a real first release (-rc first). Better, drop the `latest` default and make the Kustomize `newTag` and compose `AG_VERSION` explicit and required (`${AG_VERSION:?pin a released version}`). Verify with a CI job that pulls the tag the manifests name from ghcr.io after a release dry-run (workflow_dispatch against a fork or an -rc tag).

findings.excerpt: - {target: x86_64-apple-darwin, os: macos-13}
findings.problem: The macOS x86_64 release leg runs on `macos-13`, a runner image GitHub retired in December 2025; today (Oct 2026) the job cannot be scheduled, and `fail-fast: true` takes the whole release down with it. docs/operations/releasing.md:9 and ROADMAP promise macOS x86_64 archives. The workflow header (line 5) admits it has never run, so nothing has proven any leg.
findings.proposed_fix: Build x86_64-apple-darwin on a current runner (`macos-15-intel`) or cross-compile it on `macos-14` with `--target x86_64-apple-darwin`. Add a `workflow_dispatch` dry-run mode (build and package, skip push/publish) and run it in CI on a schedule so the pipeline is exercised before the first real tag.

findings.excerpt: cargo build --release --locked --target ${{ matrix.target }} -p ag-cli -p ag-server   (Dockerfile:27 likewise: `-p ag-server -p ag-cli`; archive step line 68 copies only `ag` and `ag-server`)
findings.problem: The release archives and both container images omit `ag-worker`, the execution-plane worker that README.md:127 and docs/guides/workers.md (`ag-worker keygen/doctor/run`) present as part of the product. A user who installs from a release or the image cannot run the sandboxed validation path at all and must build from source; README Install covers only `ag` and `ag-server`.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `-p ag-worker` to the release build, include the binary in the tarballs and add an `ag-worker` image target (cc-debian distroless, plus the toolchain mount story from workers.md). Extend the CI `images` job to run `ag-worker doctor` in the image and the README Install section to name the artifact.

findings.excerpt: cargo build --release --locked -p ag-server -p ag-cli  (no Node stage; deploy/docker/ag-server.toml and deploy/*/ag-server.toml never set `web_dir`)
findings.problem: docs/guides/web-ui.md:22-27 and README ("Clients: a Web UI") describe a Web UI served by ag-server, but the image has no UI build and none of the shipped configs set `server.web_dir`. A Compose or Kubernetes deployment has no Web UI; the operator must run `npm ci && npm run build` by hand and mount the dist directory. The roadmap task 'embed UI in ag-server' is still open.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a Node build stage to the Dockerfile (apps/web `npm ci && npm run build`), copy dist to /usr/share/agentgit/web and set `web_dir` in deploy/docker/ag-server.toml; or embed the dist in the binary (include_dir / rust-embed). Verify in the CI `images` job by `curl`ing `/` and asserting the app's index.html and the CSP headers from the running container.

findings.excerpt: deploy: name: deployment files ... python3 scripts/check_deploy.py --strict ... cargo test -p ag-server --test deploy_configs   (docs/operations/deployment.md:25 `docker compose up` has not been run end to end; :23 no manifest applied to a real cluster)
findings.problem: The Compose stack (PostgreSQL + MinIO + server + observability profile) and the Kubernetes manifests are only linted (kustomize/kubeconform/promtool/`compose config`). README promotes them as the way to run the server with PostgreSQL and MinIO, yet no CI job ever runs them, although ubuntu runners have Docker and `helm/kind-action` is available. Consequence: defects listed elsewhere in this audit (NetworkPolicy, job label, image tag, tmp dir) are invisible.
findings.proposed_fix: Add CI jobs that (1) `docker compose up -d --wait` with a generated .env (also with `--profile observability`), then run `ag clone/push/integrate` against it and assert PostgreSQL schemas and MinIO objects appear, scrape `/metrics` through the bundled Prometheus and check `up==1`; (2) create a kind cluster, `kubectl apply -k` base and the prometheus-operator overlay (install the operator CRDs/chart), wait for rollout, run the same smoke test through a port-forward and from a second namespace to exercise the NetworkPolicy.

findings.excerpt: expr: up{job="agentgit"} == 0   (source: alerts.yml:7; servicemonitor.yaml:10-21 sets neither `jobLabel` nor a relabeling)
findings.problem: The generated PrometheusRule hardcodes `job="agentgit"`, which is the `job_name` of the two plain Prometheus scrape configs. A ServiceMonitor without `jobLabel` labels the series with the Service name, i.e. `job="ag-server"`. In the Operator overlay `up{job="agentgit"}` therefore matches no series and AgentGitDown can never fire: the most important alert is dead exactly in the deployment mode that ships it. promtool/kubeconform cannot detect this.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the label deterministic: add `jobLabel: app.kubernetes.io/part-of` (value `agentgit`) or a `relabelings` rule setting `job=agentgit` in servicemonitor.yaml, or select the alert on `up{service="ag-server"}`/a label both modes share. Add `promtool test rules` unit tests for every alert (including a case that proves AgentGitDown fires when the target disappears) and verify in the kind CI job by killing the pod and waiting for the alert in Prometheus.

findings.excerpt:
ingress:
    - from:
        - podSelector: {}
      ports: [{protocol: TCP, port: 8080}]   (ingress-nginx rule is commented out, lines 18-21)
findings.problem: The only shipped ingress rule admits pods of the same namespace. The Prometheus Operator overlay adds a ServiceMonitor, but Prometheus normally runs in another namespace (e.g. monitoring), so its scrapes of /metrics are dropped by the shipped policy, as is traffic from any ingress controller. The base+overlay combination is internally inconsistent and the user must discover and edit it.
findings.proposed_fix: Ship the overlay with a NetworkPolicy patch admitting the Prometheus namespace (configurable via a kustomize patch/replacement, default `monitoring`) and document or provide an ingress overlay. Verify in the kind job by scraping from a pod in a different namespace.

findings.excerpt:
alert: AgentGitSlowRequests
 expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(agwp_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))) > 5   (same query shape in dashboard panels 'Latency (all operations)' agentgit-overview.json:104 and 'Slowest operations (p95)' :164)
findings.problem: agwp_request_duration_seconds is observed for every operation (crates/ag-server/src/app.rs:229 `started.elapsed()`), including long-poll operations by design: `jobs.claim` and `streams.head` wait up to 30 s (api/jobs.rs:37, api/streams.rs:14) and `events.subscribe` is a stream. Idle execution-plane workers poll continuously, so p99 sits at multiple seconds and the 5 s alert flaps or is permanently firing, and the description ('check storage latency') is misleading; the dashboard panels are skewed the same way.
findings.proposed_fix: Exclude long-poll/streaming operations from the SLO latency query (`operation!~"jobs.claim|streams.head|events.subscribe"`) or record them in a separate histogram/with a `long_poll` label; derive the exclusion list from the server's route table instead of hand-typing it. Add `promtool test rules` cases with idle-worker-shaped series, and check the dashboard against a real server with an idle ag-worker.

findings.excerpt:
debug:
    verbosity: basic ... exporters: [debug]   (comment line 16: "Prints a summary of what arrives. Replace or extend with a real backend")
findings.problem: The collector wired up by `docker compose --profile observability` (compose.yaml:87-93) terminates every trace in a `debug` exporter that only prints counts. No trace backend exists in the profile and Grafana has no tracing datasource, so 'OpenTelemetry traces' (README, observability.md) are collected and discarded; the Compose server config even leaves `otlp_endpoint` commented out (ag-server.toml:21-22), so with the shipped defaults no spans are ever produced.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Grafana Tempo (or Jaeger) to the observability profile, export through `otlphttp` to it, provision a Tempo datasource in Grafana and enable `otlp_endpoint = "http://otel-collector:4318"` in the compose server config when the profile is active (env-substituted). Verify in the Compose CI job by creating a proposal and querying Tempo's search API for the span `proposals.create`.

findings.excerpt:
/// Externally visible base URL (for links in responses and OIDC redirects).
    pub public_url: Option<String>,
findings.problem: The configuration key is parsed, stored and documented as driving links and OIDC redirects, but nothing in the server reads it (zero uses outside config.rs). Operators who set it behind a proxy get no effect and no warning.
findings.proposed_fix: Either implement it (use it for absolute URLs in responses/`capabilities` and for any OIDC redirect/discovery logic, validate it is an http(s) URL) with a server test asserting the emitted URLs, or remove the key and its documentation so that `deny_unknown_fields` rejects it.

findings.excerpt: "Checks (all must pass; used by CI)"; README.md:359-362: "test names and commands mentioned in docs are verified against the code (`scripts/check_docs.py`)" (README.ru.md:365-367 same)
findings.problem: No workflow invokes scripts/check_docs.py (`grep check_docs .github` is empty; the `docs-and-demo` job runs only gen_cli_docs, gen_readme_assets and quickstart.sh). The README's and docs/README.md's 'the docs are checked' claim is false for link rot, renamed tests and non-existent commands; the script's command check is also silently skipped when no `ag` binary is found (line 128).
findings.proposed_fix: Add `AG=target/release/ag python3 scripts/check_docs.py` to the `docs-and-demo` job (after the release build) and make a missing binary a failure under CI (`--strict`). Also extend DOC_FILES to apps/web, sdk/* and services/agent-orchestrator READMEs, which hold many claims.

findings.excerpt: "Every step asserts the exit code it expects, so CI runs this script as a test: the README transcript cannot drift away from what the tool really does."  (README.md:46-47, docs/README.md:31-32)
findings.problem: The script (and crates/ag-cli/tests/quickstart.rs) asserts exit codes and the final 'Demo finished' line only. The README transcript (lines 49-71: messages, `cargo test` instead of the script's `sh -c`, tree hashes, 'Integrated (merge): stream is now at ...') is hand-edited and never compared with real output, so the stated guarantee against drift does not hold.
findings.proposed_fix: Capture the script's output and check the README excerpt mechanically: generate the README block from a normalized run (ids/hashes masked) and add `--check` to CI the way gen_cli_docs.py does, or assert the key message lines (`Denied by policy`, `Blocked (policy v1)`, `Integrated (merge)`) in quickstart.rs. Adjust the script's CI command to what the README shows or state the substitution.

findings.excerpt: "Starts moto (a Python re-implementation of the S3 API ...)"; postgres-and-s3.md:209-213: "Verified against PostgreSQL 16 and moto ... Not yet run against Amazon S3, MinIO"; adr-traceability.md:44
findings.problem: The S3 object backend, its hand-written SigV4 signer, conditional PUT, CopyObject age refresh and GC lock are verified only against moto, a mock of S3. A real S3-compatible server (MinIO single binary or container) is available on CI runners and is the very server the Compose stack ships, yet no test or CI job touches it, so path-style addressing, `If-None-Match` handling and CopyObject-onto-itself semantics of the shipped configuration are unproven.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a `scripts/minio-test.sh` (pinned MinIO release, same AG_TEST_S3_* contract) and run the full S3 suite (`AG_REQUIRE_BACKENDS=1 ... cargo test --workspace`) against real MinIO in CI next to moto; run the suite against real AWS S3 on a scheduled job with a dedicated bucket. Keep moto only as the independent signature checker.

findings.excerpt: "... covered by tests that run a fake runtime script"; docs/architecture/sandbox.md:251-256 "Untested against a real runtime ... fake runtime script (tests/oci.rs)"; README.md:128 "(rootless namespaces, or a container)"; gen_readme_assets.py:271 "or an OCI container"
findings.problem: The OCI sandbox backend, advertised in the README feature table and architecture diagram as an isolation option, has only been exercised against a shell script pretending to be docker/podman. Whether a real runtime accepts and enforces the generated flags is unknown; the IsolationReport is forced to `verified: false`. Docker and Podman are preinstalled on GitHub's ubuntu runners.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a CI job that runs `tests/oci.rs`-equivalent suites against real Docker and real Podman with a digest-pinned image (e.g. busybox@sha256:...), reading enforcement back from inside the container (`/proc/self/status`, cgroup files, network, read-only root, memory/pids limits) so the report can truthfully claim `verified: true`; then delete the fake runtime. Until then qualify the README bullet and the SVG ('experimental, unverified').

findings.excerpt: "... by unit tests against a fake cgroup directory"; sandbox.md:214-217 "The cgroup code was not exercised against a real cgroup v2 hierarchy ... the kernel-facing behaviour is untested"
findings.problem: The exact memory/pids enforcement via delegated cgroup v2 is validated only against a tempdir that imitates the cgroup file layout; the kernel semantics (controller enabling order, `memory.max`, OOM kill detection, `cgroup.kill`) are untested, yet the docs present cgroup limits as the 'exact' mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Run the limits suite in CI on a runner with cgroup v2 and a delegated subtree (`systemd-run --user --scope -p Delegate=yes` or a privileged container with the cgroup2 mount) with AG_REQUIRE_CGROUP=1, asserting a hog is killed by the kernel OOM and a fork bomb is stopped by `pids.max`; remove the fake-directory tests that stand in for kernel behaviour.

findings.excerpt: async fn start_oidc() -> Oidc { ... tests/fixtures/oidc-test-ed25519.pem ... }  (fixtures/README.md:3 "play the part of an OpenID Connect provider"; docs/guides/sdks.md:526-527 "TLS and OIDC against a real provider" not covered)
findings.problem: README.md:163 advertises OIDC login, but the OIDC path (discovery, JWKS fetch/refresh, RS256/ES256 verification, group mapping) is tested only against an in-test issuer that serves a static Ed25519 key. Real providers (Keycloak, dex) are available as containers; RS256 with key rotation, `kid` selection and discovery documents are the common production case and unverified.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a CI job that starts dex or Keycloak (pinned image) with a realm/client, obtains a real ID token (password/device or client-credentials grant), points `[[auth.oidc]]` at its issuer via discovery (no `jwks_file`), and asserts `whoami`, group-to-role mapping, expiry and a rotated signing key. Keep the in-process issuer only for negative cases.

findings.excerpt: "It is tested against a fake collector, not against a specific backend (Tempo, Jaeger, a vendor)." (crates/ag-server/tests/tracing_export.rs:63 `Collector::start(200)`)
findings.problem: The hand-written OTLP/HTTP JSON exporter is verified only against a test-local HTTP handler. A real OpenTelemetry Collector (the one the Compose profile ships) is available and would reveal encoding or content-type incompatibilities.
findings.proposed_fix: In CI run `otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib` (pinned) with the file exporter, point the server at it, issue operations and assert the received spans (names, trace/parent ids, attributes) from the collector's output.

findings.excerpt:
// Scripted is the built-in demo/test executor: it edits a virtual workspace,
// signs provenance and opens a proposal.   (Delay time.Duration `yaml:"delay"` at line 170; docs/guides/orchestrator.md:126-132 "Built-in stand-in for an agent ... model: scripted-demo")
findings.problem: The production orchestrator binary ships a stand-in 'agent' that writes canned files from config, optionally sleeps (`delay`) to imitate work, and signs real provenance records claiming `model=scripted-demo`. The guide's reference configuration and its 'real run' transcript (orchestrator.md:239) use it as the default executor, so the headline demo of the 'Agent Platform' is produced by a simulated agent, and signed provenance can state a model that never ran.
findings.proposed_fix: Move the scripted executor behind a test/demo build tag or an explicit `--enable-demo-executors` flag that is refused by `check` in production configs, and stop recording `scripted-demo` as a model in provenance (use an explicit `synthetic: true`). Ship a real executor (an LLM agent driver, e.g. the Claude API/SDK invoked as a `command` executor with workspace/lease/provenance plumbing) and base the worked example and README on it.

findings.excerpt: ("Agent platform", "Go · scheduler, advisor", 200)   (README.md:403; docs/guides/orchestrator.md:384-387 "The advisor and the reviewers are deterministic heuristics, not a model"; services/agent-orchestrator/README.md 'Advisor ... deterministic rule-based suggestions', 'Reviewers ... likely secrets ...')
findings.problem: The architecture diagram, ROADMAP and the Go 'agent platform' present an 'advisor', 'reviewers' and a 'semantic index' as agent intelligence, but they are regexp/rule matching (secret patterns, whitespace-only resolutions) and a line-based symbol extractor. The limitation is disclosed in the limits table, but the product surface (names, diagram, review comments posted as 'service:advisor'/'service:reviewer') still reads as intelligence.
findings.proposed_fix: Either implement model-backed Advisor/Reviewer behind the existing `Advisor` interface (provider-configurable, output always a `comment` review, evaluated against a labelled conflict/secret corpus) and keep the rules as a baseline, or rename them honestly (`conflict-hints`, `lint-reviewer`) in code, review author identities, diagram and docs; replace the line-based indexer with tree-sitter/LSP-based extraction or call it 'symbol grep'.

findings.excerpt: "Unit tests ... use a fake clock and an in-memory fake AGWP server (`internal/testutil/fakeagwp`) that mimics the real error model, injected failures, SSE and dedup of validation jobs."
findings.problem: The orchestrator's unit suites run against a hand-written imitation of the server's error model, SSE and job dedup, which can drift from the real ag-server; the real binary is available in CI (the integration job builds it).
findings.proposed_fix: Run the scheduler/session/execsched suites against the real `ag-server` (as `integration/` already does), keeping the fake only for fault injection that the real server cannot produce, and add a contract test that replays recorded real-server transcripts against the fake.

findings.excerpt: "Nothing here has run yet — the first tag is its first test" (also services/agent-orchestrator/Dockerfile:8 "has not been built by its authors"; docs/guides/orchestrator.md:377 "It has not been built")
findings.problem: The release pipeline and the orchestrator image are shipped untested by admission, and the orchestrator Dockerfile is not built by CI nor by the release workflow, so a documented deployment artifact (docs/guides/orchestrator.md section 9) does not demonstrably exist.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the orchestrator image to the CI `images` job (build + `orchestrator check` against a started ag-server) and to release.yml (push `ghcr.io/paffin/agentgit-orchestrator:X.Y.Z` with provenance); add a `workflow_dispatch` dry-run of the whole release workflow so the first real tag is not its first test.

findings.excerpt: pub const DEFAULT_JOB_ATTEMPTS: u32 = 5;  (worker.rs:24 `const RETRY_AFTER_MS: i64 = 10_000;`; docs/guides/workers.md:96 "five by default", :89 "10 s delay")
findings.problem: The docs say validation jobs get 'five by default' attempts and a 10 s retry delay, implying tunability, but no server/policy/worker setting exists for either; operators with flaky runners cannot adjust them.
findings.proposed_fix: Expose `max_attempts` and `retry_delay_secs` per required validation (policy `run` spec, bounded by a server ceiling) and as an `ag-worker` flag for the retry delay; document the keys and cover them in the jobs integration tests.

findings.excerpt: const QUEUE: usize = 4096; const BATCH: usize = 256; const FLUSH_EVERY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2); const POST_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5);  (control.rs:248 `LIMIT 1000` behind observability.md:24 "at most 1000 counted per repository"; api/jobs.rs:37 and api/streams.rs:14 `MAX_WAIT_MS: u32 = 30_000`)
findings.problem: Trace exporter queue/batch/flush/timeout, the queued-jobs gauge cap and the long-poll ceiling are fixed constants that observability.md and workers.md publish as facts; a deployment under load (or a slow collector) cannot tune them, and `agwp_jobs_queued` silently saturates at 1000 per repository.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `[telemetry] otlp_queue`, `otlp_batch`, `otlp_flush_ms`, `otlp_timeout_ms` and `[limits] max_long_poll_ms` to ServerConfig (validated, defaults unchanged); compute `agwp_jobs_queued` with a COUNT instead of a capped LIMIT or export a `capped` flag.

findings.excerpt: "Defaults you may want to know about: a write transaction waits up to 30 s for the repository's write lock ... a transaction that sits idle for 10 minutes is ended by the server"  (crates/ag-storage/src/meta/pg/mod.rs:83,85 `lock_timeout: Duration::from_secs(30)`, `idle_in_transaction_timeout: Duration::from_secs(600)`)
findings.problem: PgOptions has both fields, but neither ag-integrate's StorageConfig, the server config nor the CLI ever sets them, and the reference table (lines 160-174) lists only `pool_size`. The documented 'defaults' are in fact the only values, so busy multi-writer deployments cannot adjust lock wait or idle cut-off. Static-only S3 credentials (line 109) similarly rule out IAM roles/IRSA on AWS.
findings.proposed_fix: Expose `lock_timeout_secs` and `idle_in_transaction_secs` under `storage.meta` (additive, validated) and document them in the reference table; add an S3 credential provider chain (web-identity/instance profile) or state the limitation prominently in the README honest-limits table.

findings.excerpt: HEALTHCHECK --interval=15s ... CMD ["/usr/local/bin/ag-server", "healthcheck", "--url", "http://127.0.0.1:8080"]
findings.problem: The health check hardcodes port 8080 and overrides the `AG_HEALTHCHECK_URL` variable that the subcommand supports (main.rs `env = "AG_HEALTHCHECK_URL"`). An operator who changes `server.listen` or enables TLS in the mounted config gets a permanently 'unhealthy' container (Compose/Swarm restart loops).
findings.proposed_fix: Drop `--url` from the HEALTHCHECK so the env default applies, or let `ag-server healthcheck` derive the address and scheme from `AG_SERVER_CONFIG` (`server.listen`, TLS on/off); cover it in the CI `images` job with a container started on a non-default port.

findings.excerpt: "Nothing in this file has been built in CI yet — see docs/operations/deployment.md"
findings.problem: Stale claim: ci.yml:129-166 (`images` job) now builds both targets, starts the server image and waits for its health check. The comment contradicts CI and the deployment page ('CI builds it'), so readers cannot tell which statement is true.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete the sentence (or point to the `images` CI job) and keep deployment.md as the single place that states what has been verified.

findings.excerpt: "The inputs are pinned (`Cargo.lock` with `--locked`, a fixed Rust image tag in the Dockerfile)"  (Dockerfile:14 `FROM rust:${RUST_VERSION}-bookworm`, :17-19 unpinned `apt-get install cmake clang`, :33/:41 `gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian12:nonroot`)
findings.problem: Base images are referenced by moving tags, not digests, and build tools are installed unpinned, so 'pinned inputs' overstates reproducibility (the page does admit bit-for-bit builds are unproven).
findings.proposed_fix: Pin `rust`, `distroless` (and `minio`/`postgres`/`grafana` in compose) by `@sha256:` digest, let Dependabot (docker ecosystem) maintain them, pin apt packages or use a pre-built toolchain image, and verify with a CI job that builds twice and compares digests.

findings.excerpt: "Every command below is exercised by [`examples/quickstart.sh`] and `crates/ag-cli/tests/cli.rs`."
findings.problem: The guide shows `ag agent heartbeat`, `agent reap --timeout`, `agent disable`, `lease extend`, `task create/ready/done` and the queue; the CLI test files (cli.rs, quickstart.rs, remote.rs) and quickstart.sh never invoke them (only `task depend`, `lease acquire/list`, `agent register/start/finish`, `predict` appear). `ag git import/export` and `ag queue` are likewise absent from CLI tests (ag-git's tests cover the library only).
findings.proposed_fix: Add CLI tests (or extend quickstart.sh) for the missing commands (heartbeat/reap/disable/enable, lease extend/release, task create/ready/done/cancel, queue add/list/run, git import/export, op list/resume, recover), or reword the claim to the commands that are actually covered; extend check_docs.py to cross-check documented subcommands against test invocations.

findings.excerpt: "## What is deliberately not here (yet)\n\nA network server, the AGWP protocol, PostgreSQL/S3 backends, a Web UI, SDKs for other languages, rename detection and blame."
findings.problem: The architecture overview (and its crate table at :60 listing `Meta` as SQLite-only and `ObjectStore` as fs/memory) says all of these do not exist, while the README, ROADMAP and code have them. Same stale statements: security.md:59 and :72 ('requires the planned server mode', 'no rate limiting or quota system'), SECURITY.md:51 '(planned) server mode', agents.md:149 'A network API is on the roadmap', adr-traceability.md:35/:69/:74/:76 (OpenTelemetry/Prometheus, API-only virtual workspaces, autonomous review, event replay marked not built), storage.md:146 'until the server exists', CONTRIBUTING.md:24 '~200 tests, a few seconds' (README: about 550, minutes) and :70 project layout without server/worker/sandbox.
findings.proposed_fix: Update these passages to the current state (server, PostgreSQL/S3, Web UI, SDKs, rename detection, blame, virtual workspaces, replay all exist), regenerate crate tables from `cargo metadata`, and add a CI check that fails when a doc contains 'planned'/'not here (yet)' for a feature listed as implemented in the traceability table.

findings.excerpt: "## [0.1.0] — 2026-10-17 ... First public alpha."; [0.1.0]: https://github.com/Paffin/AgentGit/releases/tag/v0.1.0 (line 122); ROADMAP.md:7 "0.1 — shipped (alpha)"; SECURITY.md supported-versions table '0.1.x'
findings.problem: The changelog, roadmap and security policy describe 0.1.0 as shipped and supported, but the repository has no `v0.1.0` tag (`git tag -l` is empty), no GitHub release and no published image or archive, so the compare/release links in the changelog are dead and nothing exists to which 'security fixes on the latest 0.1 release' could apply. The server, workers, Web UI etc. sit under [Unreleased] and `Cargo.toml` still says 0.1.0.
findings.proposed_fix: Cut a real release through the (dry-run-verified) workflow, or relabel the sections as unreleased and remove the dead links; bump the workspace version when [Unreleased] is promoted so `scripts/check_release.py` ties tag, Cargo.toml and CHANGELOG to the same content.

findings.excerpt:
"## 11. Web UI — не копия GitHub

Вместо того чтобы делать очередной интерфейс ... AgentGit должен показывать жив

> **Текст обрывается.** Исходное сообщение с ADR было обрезано ... Дополнить, когда будет полная версия."
findings.problem: The foundational ADR that the whole documentation set ('traceability maps every ADR promise') relies on is truncated mid-sentence; §11 and everything after it are missing, and adr-traceability.md:424 states 'the rest was never received'. A specification with an unfinished section is a placeholder in the product's documentation.
findings.proposed_fix: Complete §11+ from the original source or replace it with an accurate, English ADR describing the Web UI decisions actually implemented (ADR-0007), and remove the truncation note.

findings.excerpt: "Flat tree manifests: measured at 100 000 files, an integration takes a few hundred milliseconds"
findings.problem: ADR-0006 states the numbers were taken with one thread, an in-memory object store and in-memory SQLite, 'CPU costs of the engine, not of a deployment (no network, no disk latency)' and explicitly 'not measured: PostgreSQL or S3 latency'. The README gives the figure without that qualification, so readers will assume it applies to a real deployment.
findings.proposed_fix: Qualify the README sentence ('engine CPU cost, in memory') or add a real benchmark (on-disk SQLite, PostgreSQL + MinIO, concurrent integrators) to the scale suite and publish those numbers.

findings.excerpt: "They are taken from the seeded demo world (plausible agents, task titles and file paths)" ... localStorage.setItem('agentgit.staleAfterSec', '10')  (README.md:189 "Real screenshots of the UI running against a real server"; hero SVG verdict states hardcoded at gen_readme_assets.py:80)
findings.problem: The README screenshots show real UI against a real server but with fabricated seed data (agents dep-updater, test-fixer..., invented proposals) and a forced 'Quiet' agent produced by lowering the stale threshold to 10 s; the banner's four verdicts ('clean merge', '1/1 passed', '1 of 2', 'not yet') are static text. The README does not say the content is demo data, so it reads as observed live agent work.
findings.proposed_fix: Caption the screenshots as 'seeded demo data' (and the banner as an illustration), or capture them from a repository populated by the real orchestrator/quickstart flow without UI tweaks.

findings.excerpt: "they use `$AG_SERVER_BIN`, then `/home/user/bin/ag-server`, then `target/debug/ag-server` ..."  (same literal fallback in sdk/python/tests/harness.py:36, sdk/typescript/test/harness/server.ts:18, apps/web/e2e/support/server.ts:20, services/agent-orchestrator/integration/harness_test.go:52, and the SDK/web/orchestrator READMEs)
findings.problem: A developer-machine path is baked into five test harnesses and their documentation; on any other host it is dead weight, and in the Go integration suite a missing binary makes tests skip ('skip with a message') rather than fail, so a green run can mean nothing ran.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the `/home/user/bin` fallback everywhere; resolve the binary from `$AG_SERVER_BIN` then `target/{debug,release}`, and make a missing binary a hard failure when `CI` is set (as AG_REQUIRE_BACKENDS does).

findings.excerpt: # The metrics token reaches Prometheus as a mounted file (secrets/metrics_token) ... source: ./secrets/metrics_token   (.env.example:8-10 "Also write the same value to secrets/metrics_token")
findings.problem: The same secret must be hand-copied into `.env` and `secrets/metrics_token`; if they differ Prometheus gets 401, `up` stays 0 and the (mis-labelled) down alert fires. The stack also embeds the bucket name `agentgit` in two files (ag-server.toml:34 and compose.yaml:54) and the Postgres password raw in a URL (compose.yaml:72) that breaks for passwords containing `/@:`.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Compose `secrets:` with `environment: AG_METRICS_TOKEN` (or a one-shot init service that writes the file from the same variable) so there is one source of truth; derive the bucket from a single `S3_BUCKET` variable; URL-encode or build the DSN in an entrypoint.

findings.excerpt: read_only: true   (no tmpfs; deployment.yaml:71-72 mounts `{name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp}` as an emptyDir for the same image)
findings.problem: The Kubernetes manifest gives the read-only container a writable /tmp, but the Compose service sets `read_only: true` without any tmpfs. Whether ag-server/SQLite/rustls need /tmp is not verified because the stack was never run; if they do, the Compose deployment fails at runtime.
findings.proposed_fix: Run the Compose stack in CI (see the deploy finding) and add `tmpfs: [/tmp]` if required, or prove by test that the server never writes outside /data and drop the k8s /tmp volume.

findings.excerpt: "Three ready-made ways to run it, all under deploy/ ... | **Binary** | trying it, small teams, systemd | `ag-server serve --config ag-server.toml` |"
findings.problem: deploy/ contains Compose, Docker and Kubernetes only; there is no systemd unit, sample bare-metal ag-server.toml or install script for the 'Binary' way, although it is listed among the ready-made ways 'all under deploy/' and recommends systemd.
findings.proposed_fix: Add deploy/systemd/ag-server.service (DynamicUser, StateDirectory, hardening, EnvironmentFile for secrets) with a sample config and test it in CI with a systemd-nspawn/VM job, or remove the claim.

findings.excerpt: env = {"PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/bin", "AG_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN": "x", ...}
findings.problem: The `docker compose config` checks run with a hardcoded PATH (and no HOME), so on macOS/Homebrew or Nix hosts the check either cannot find docker or fails spuriously even though `have('docker')` succeeded; also check_deploy only parses metric names from metrics.rs source with a regex (line 70-95) rather than from a running server as alerts.yml:2 claims.
findings.proposed_fix: Inherit the caller's environment (`dict(os.environ, **secrets)`) and drop the PATH override; to back the alerts.yml:2 claim, start the real ag-server in the script, exercise operations that create the label vectors, scrape /metrics and compare names there.

findings.excerpt:
# Alerting rules for AgentGit. Every metric used here is exported by ag-server;
# scripts/check_deploy.py verifies that against a running server.
findings.problem: check_deploy.py never contacts a server; it greps `Opts::new("...")` names out of crates/ag-server/src/metrics.rs. Label-dependent expressions (`code=~"internal|..."`, `event="failed"`, `outcome`) are therefore not validated at all.
findings.proposed_fix: Either correct the comment or implement the check against a real server, plus `promtool test rules` fixtures that assert each alert's labels exist in a scrape of the real exposition format.

findings.excerpt: "Exit codes (stable, safe for scripts and agents to rely on):" ... "| 3 | **blocked** ..." ... "Global options: `-C/--repo`, `--as <identity>` ..."
findings.problem: docs/reference/cli.md is described as GENERATED from `ag --help`, but its exit-code table and global-options line are static text in the generator, not derived from `crates/ag-cli/src/main.rs` (`exit::ERROR/BLOCKED/REFUSED`) or the clap definition, so `--check` cannot catch drift in them.
findings.proposed_fix: Have `ag` print its exit-code table (e.g. `ag help exit-codes` / `--help` epilog sourced from the `exit` module) and have the generator embed that output; add a CLI test asserting the constants match the printed table.

findings.excerpt: "The `pg_dump` / restore round trip of a repository whose objects stay in the bucket was exercised by hand with the real CLI ... backing up and restoring the bucket ... was not exercised."
findings.problem: The only documented procedure for backing up PostgreSQL-backed repositories (where `ag backup` refuses) was verified manually once and is not automated, although PostgreSQL is available in CI via pg-test.sh.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a backends-job test that runs init, integrate, `pg_dump`, `DROP SCHEMA`, `pg_restore` and `ag verify` (matching audit head) against the throwaway cluster, plus the MinIO/S3 bucket copy variant once a real MinIO is in CI.

verdicts.reason: Narrowed: the production Negotiate route (ag-server/src/api/session.rs:44-45) re-states the engine limits as literals (100_000, 10_000) instead of reading them from ag_types::Limits, and ag-integrate/src/history.rs:184 hides a bare 5_000_000. Limits::default() is the only limits source in repo.rs:140, so the literals match today but can drift silently. The headline claim that limits must be operator-configurable is not a defect: docs/architecture/object-format.md:57,87 document them as fixed decode/validation rules, and per-deployment values would make replicas disagree on which changesets decode.

verdicts.reason: Timestamp::now() is the production time source (SystemClock in ag-storage/src/clock.rs:19, worker attestation, GC cutoff, S3 grace window), and time.rs:24 maps a pre-1970 clock to 0 via unwrap_or(0), so a wrong value is silently fabricated. Timestamp wraps an i64 and already supports negative values (the test formats -1 correctly), so the truthful value is representable and the fallback is unnecessary. The u128-to-i64 truncation is not reachable for real clocks, so this is low severity.
verdicts.refined_fix: In crates/ag-types/src/time.rs: `pub fn now() -> Self { Self(millis_since_epoch(SystemTime::now())) }` plus `fn millis_since_epoch(t: SystemTime) -> i64 { match t.duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH) { Ok(d) => i64::try_from(d.as_millis()).unwrap_or(i64::MAX), Err(e) => i64::try_from(e.duration().as_millis()).map(|m| -m).unwrap_or(i64::MIN) } }`. verdicts.reason: RepoPath::validate (path.rs:99) only matches .git/.ag with eq_ignore_ascii_case, so `.git.`, `.git `, `GIT~1`, `.git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION` and `.g<U+200C>it` all pass. verdicts.refined_fix: In crates/ag-types/src/path.rs replace the `eq_ignore_ascii_case` check with a helper that, for each component, takes the part before the first ':' (NTFS alternate streams), drops ignorable code points (U+200C..=U+200F, U+202A..=U+202E, U+206A..=U+206F, U+FEFF), strips trailing '.' and ' ', and compares the result ASCII-case-insensitively to `.git` and `.ag`. Also reject the 8.3 short names `git~<digits>` and `ag~<digits>` (case-insensitive). Return PathError::Reserved(comp) for all of these. Plain names such as `.gitignore`, `a.git` and `a:b` must stay valid. The rule is unconditional on all platforms, as Git's verify_path does. Skip the Windows device-name and MAX_PATH sub-claims; they are portability limits, not the .git code-execution vector.

verdicts.reason: Identity::new accepts `agent:#x` (name `#x` is non-empty and '#' is allowed), but principal() (identity.rs:97-102) builds Identity("agent:") directly with an empty name, so the documented 1..=128 invariant is broken. principal() is used in authorization comparisons (ag-server workspaces.rs:46, agents.rs:21, jobs.rs, ag-policy eval.rs:261). Registered agent names (registry.rs validate_name) and OIDC names (oidc.rs sanitizer drops '#') cannot start with '#', so exploitation needs an admin-minted subject or a locally chosen --as label. That makes it low severity but still a true invariant violation.
verdicts.refined_fix: In crates/ag-types/src/identity.rs, Identity::new, after the length check add: `if name.split('#').next().is_none_or(str::is_empty) { return Err(IdentityError::BadLength); }` so the part before any '#' must be non-empty, and update the IdentityError::BadLength message to mention it. principal() can then stay as is, because its head is guaranteed non-empty. Add a unit test that `Identity::new("agent:#x")` and `Identity::new("user:#")` are Err, and a proptest that for every valid id `Identity::new(id.principal().as_str()).is_ok()`.

verdicts.reason: The `_ => System` arm of kind() also covers the legitimate `system` prefix, so it is not a fabricated privileged fallback. Identity's field is private and its only constructors are new() (which restricts the prefix to user/agent/service/system) and principal() (which keeps the prefix), so no other prefix can reach kind(). The finding itself concedes the arm is unreachable. The duplicated prefix list is a maintainability nit with no behavioural defect.

KeyPair::from_seed is real Ed25519 key construction, not a mock or stub. It is the production restore path in KeyPair::load (lib.rs:245), and `SigningKey::from_bytes` is equally public in ed25519-dalek, so hiding the wrapper protects nothing. The other callers are tests (ag-integrate/tests/policy.rs, ag-policy/src/eval_tests.rs, ag-crypto unit tests), and cross-crate tests need a deterministic constructor. A minted guessable key only affects the holder who chose the seed, and no security boundary is crossed.

The doc sentence at lib.rs:169 says the KeyPair's secret is zeroized on drop. That is true: ed25519-dalek 3.0.0 depends on zeroize unconditionally per Cargo.lock, so the SigningKey is wiped. It does not promise that transient hex/JSON/read buffers in save/load are wiped, so no claim is left unimplemented. Wiping those copies would be optional hardening beyond the documented threat model (security.md lists keys as not encrypted at rest), not a stub or mock.

The 0600 creation mode (lib.rs:216-220) and the group/other check on load (lib.rs:230-237) are both #[cfg(unix)] only, so on Windows the private signing key is written with inherited ACLs and loaded unchecked, silently. KeyStore::create/load (ag-agent/src/registry.rs:43-50) back `ag agent register` and issuer keys in the CLI. The in-progress Windows workflow states Windows is a supported platform for the CLI, server and clients, and the worktree's ag-crypto has no ACL handling. docs/architecture/security.md:45 and guides/agents.md:22 state 0600 / refusal behaviour with no platform qualifier. The ag-worker path is unix-only, so the exposure is the CLI/agent key store.
verdicts.refined_fix: In crates/ag-crypto add `[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies] windows-sys` (0.61.x is already in Cargo.lock) with features Win32_Foundation, Win32_Security, Win32_Security_Authorization, Win32_Storage_FileSystem. Implement #[cfg(windows)] counterparts: in save, create the file with a protected DACL granting access only to the current user's SID (CreateFileW with SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES from `D:P(A;;FA;;;<current user SID>)`, or SetNamedSecurityInfoW with PROTECTED_DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION right after create_new). In load, read the DACL with GetNamedSecurityInfoW and return CryptoError::InsecurePermissions if any ACE other than the current user, SYSTEM or Administrators allows access. Use a cfg(not(any(unix, windows))) fallback that returns an explicit error. Add a Windows-gated test that inspects the saved file's ACL and a test that load rejects a file whose DACL grants Everyone read. Extend the KeyStore::open directory permission (registry.rs:24-33) the same way. Update security.md:45 to state the per-OS behaviour.

verdicts.reason: MemoryHistory is a fully working in-memory implementation of the ChangesetSource trait, not a stub. It is used only by unit tests of the pure algorithms in ag-dag/src/tests.rs and ag-tree/src/tests.rs, and no production code constructs it (the product uses StoreHistory and HybridGraph). The doc on ChangesetSource (source.rs:19-23) says history algorithms work over 'the object store, the metadata index or an in-memory test fixture'. grep finds exactly two non-blanket impls of the trait: StoreHistory (ag-storage/src/history.rs:31) and MemoryHistory. verdicts.reason: MAX_AUTHOR_LEN (160) and MAX_NAMESPACE_LEN (128) in ag-changeset/src/lib.rs:41-42 are only pre-allocation length bounds for Reader::str. The real validation (Identity::new, Namespace::new) re-runs right after on the decoded string (lib.rs:220,226). They do not conflict today: the longest valid identity is 7+1+128 = 136, which is below 160, and the namespace cap equals Namespace's 128. The `.min(4096)` preallocation cap is a local DoS guard. Nothing is wrong now, and the drift risk is hypothetical.

Verified in the manifests: ag-types, ag-object, ag-changeset and ag-crypto have `description = "AgentGit: <crate>"` placeholders. The same placeholder is in ag-dag, ag-diff, ag-tree, ag-storage, ag-merge, ag-policy, ag-agent and ag-integrate, so the finding undercounts (12 crates). verdicts.reason: limits.rs documents these as `Limits::default()` and docs/architecture/object-format.md:87 lists the same values; max_ops, max_parents, max_message_len and max_tree_entries decide whether a content-addressed changeset is valid, so per-deployment tuning would make replicas disagree on validity. The operational limits (request/object bytes, rate, concurrency) are already configurable in ag-server/src/config.rs. The two literals in session.rs:44-45 equal the defaults, so clients are not misled today. Wanting a knob is a feature request, not a stub or hardcode defect.

`duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)` only fails for a clock set before 1970, and the `as i64` truncation needs about 292 million years, so it is unreachable. The consumers fail safe on the fallback: the GC cutoff in object_store.rs:545 becomes negative and deletes nothing. `Clock::now()` is infallible and used throughout the code, so making it fallible would be a large API change for a state that is not realistic.

path.rs:99 only does `eq_ignore_ascii_case` against `.git`/`.ag`. Nothing in the crate or workdir/mod.rs (`safe_target`/`write_entry`) handles NTFS aliases (`.git.`, `.git `, `GIT~1`, `.git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION`) or HFS+ ignorable code points (`.g<ZWNJ>it`). These are the classic git verify_path bypasses and they re-open the code-execution vector the comment says is closed; `.ag.` can alias AgentGit's own `.ag/` directory (config, meta.db, keys). security.md:70 only mentions case collisions, not aliasing. macOS is a release target and the Windows port is in progress. The check belongs in the platform-independent `RepoPath` so a Linux server rejects the path for every client, as git does.

(3) `trim_end_matches(['.', ' '])` (Win32 strips trailing dots and spaces). (4) Compare ASCII-case-insensitively to `.git`/`.ag`. (5) Also reject 8.3 short names `git~<digits>` and `ag~<digits>` (ASCII-case-insensitive, digits only). Return `PathError::Reserved(original_component)` on a match. No NFC step is needed because the reserved names are pure ASCII, and do not reject ':' or other Windows-illegal characters globally, because that would invalidate legitimate Linux paths. Add unit tests. Reject: `.git.`, `.git `, `a/.GIT. /x`, `GIT~1`, `git~12`, `.git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION`, `.g\u{200c}it`, `.AG.`, `.ag ::$DATA`. Accept: `.gitignore`, `a.git`, `git~`, `git~x`, `ag~x`, `...`. Reword the doc comment on RESERVED_COMPONENTS and the RepoPath rules, update the `RepoPath` row in docs/architecture/object-format.md, and add a security.md note. As defense in depth for the Windows port (task 20), add a `#[cfg(windows)]` check in workdir `safe_target` rejecting Windows device names (CON, NUL, COM1..9, LPT1..9) and `<>:"|?*`. Verify with the proptest in path.rs and, once Windows CI exists, a checkout of a tree built from such names.

verdicts.reason: I confirmed the trace. `Identity::new("agent:#run1")` is accepted ('#' is in the allowed set and the name is non-empty), but `principal()` (identity.rs:97-102) builds `Identity("agent:")` directly. That value violates the documented 1..=128 name rule, would fail `Identity::new`/`Deserialize`, and makes `agent:#a` and `agent:#b` share one principal. Principals are compared for self-approval (ag-policy/eval.rs:261), workspace ownership (workspaces.rs:46) and provenance (ag-agent/provenance.rs:131,193). Exploitability is low because an admin must mint such an identity, but the invariant breach is cheap to remove.
verdicts.refined_fix: Do not tighten `Identity::new`: `Changeset::decode` re-validates the author with it, so stored `agent:#x` authors would stop decoding. Instead make `principal()` always return a valid identity: `match self.0.split_once('#') { Some((head, _)) if !head.ends_with(':') => Identity(head.to_string()), _ => self.clone() }`, with a comment that a name consisting only of a run suffix is its own principal. Add tests: `Identity::new("agent:#a").unwrap().principal() == itself`, `agent:#a` and `agent:#b` have distinct principals, and a proptest over names from the allowed alphabet that `Identity::new(id.principal().as_str()).is_ok()`. Add one sentence to the Identity row in docs/architecture/object-format.md. Optionally have the agent registry and `Identity::of` reject an empty base name.

verdicts.reason: The wildcard arm of `kind()` is unreachable. The field is private and both constructors keep a validated prefix: `new` checks the four prefixes and `principal()` keeps the `kind:` head. `System` is also the least privileged kind in the code. ag-server/src/api/admin.rs:213 refuses to mint credentials for `System` identities, and policy checks compare against `User` or `Agent`. The duplicated prefix list is a maintainability nit, not a privileged fallback.

`from_seed` is the necessary building block of `KeyPair::load` (lib.rs:245) and a normal key-import API. It gives no capability beyond `ed25519_dalek::SigningKey::from_bytes`, which any in-process caller already has, and no production path calls it with a fixed seed. The real component (`generate`/`load`) is what production uses; the fixed seeds appear only in tests, so nothing is faked.

The doc sentence is on `KeyPair`, and its only secret field is a dalek `SigningKey`. I confirmed ed25519-dalek 3.0.0 has `zeroize` in its default features, so that statement is accurate. The transient copies in load/save are a defense-in-depth gap, but security.md:67 already documents that keys are not encrypted at rest and sit as plaintext JSON on disk. Scrubbing heap copies adds little against that stated threat model, and nobody is misled.

The docs on `save` and `load` honestly say 0600 and the permission check apply 'on Unix'. Windows is not yet a supported target. ci.yml builds only ubuntu and macos, release.yml ships only linux and darwin targets, and ag-cli/src/cmds/remote.rs:68-95 uses `std::os::unix` unconditionally, so it does not compile on Windows. The ACL work belongs to the in-progress Windows task (#20) and is not a present defect. Once Windows ships, key-file ACLs must be added or the gap documented in security.md.

`MemoryHistory` is a plain deterministic in-memory implementation of the `ChangesetSource` trait, documented as a test/tooling fixture. It is used only by the ag-dag and ag-tree unit tests, and the product path uses `StoreHistory`, so nothing fakes history. Gating it behind a feature would complicate dev-dependencies for no user benefit, and `.expect("lock")` on a poisoned lock is the standard idiom.

The doc comment at source.rs:21-23 names the metadata index as a backend, but `ChangesetSource` has only `StoreHistory` (ag-storage/src/history.rs:31), `MemoryHistory`, and the `&T`/`Arc<T>` forwarding impls. There is no metadata-index implementation anywhere in crates/ or docs. The statement is false, though the impact is limited to developers reading the comment.
verdicts.refined_fix: In crates/ag-changeset/src/source.rs replace lines 21-23 with: "History algorithms (`ag-dag`, `ag-tree`) are written against this trait so they work identically over the object store (`StoreHistory` in `ag-storage`) and an in-memory fixture ([`MemoryHistory`])." Do not add a metadata-index implementation unless a caller needs one.

verdicts.reason: The caps are consistent with validation. `MAX_NAMESPACE_LEN` 128 equals the `Namespace::new` limit, and `MAX_AUTHOR_LEN` 160 is above the longest valid identity (`service:` plus 128 characters is 136), so no valid value is rejected. Both are bounds on a string-length prefix, applied before the real `Identity::new` and `Namespace::new` validation. The `.min(4096)` is the standard cap on pre-allocation from an untrusted count; the real bound is `limits.max_ops`. These are format and decoder constants, and changing them would be a format change.

I confirmed `description = "AgentGit: ag-xxx"` is a name-echo placeholder. It is wider than reported: 12 crates have it (ag-agent, ag-changeset, ag-crypto, ag-dag, ag-diff, ag-integrate, ag-merge, ag-object, ag-policy, ag-storage, ag-tree, ag-types), while ag-cli, ag-client, ag-git, ag-protocol, ag-sandbox, ag-server and ag-worker have real ones. The text shows up in cargo metadata and any registry listing. It is cosmetic, but it is placeholder data with a zero-risk fix.
