verdicts.reason: Confirmed by code and by running it. tree.rs:304 maps every Tree::from_entries error to ours.clone() with no conflict. merge_trees is called in production from integrate.rs:396, workspace.rs:266 and virtual_ws.rs:192. In a throwaway crate (path deps on the real ag-merge) with max_tree_entries=4, base {a,b}, ours +{o1,o2} and theirs +{t1,t2} returned Ok(clean=true, conflicts=[], tree==ours, no t1). integrate.rs:406 would then diff to empty ops and commit a merge with parents [h,p] that contains none of theirs.

tree.rs:238 turns every Tree::apply error into Ok(None), so TooManyEntries (apply checks it at ag-tree lib.rs:215 before check_path) is sent to merge_full and hidden there (same root cause and same repro as finding 0). Note that NoOpPut and DeleteMissing cannot arise from the ops built here (Put is emitted only when the entry differs from ours, Delete only when ours has the path), so TooManyEntries is the only non-FileDirectory error that is reachable.

lib.rs:31-32 says 'Merge does not detect renames in this version' while the same file re-exports detect_renames/Rename and the MIN_SIMILARITY constants, tree.rs has plan_renames plus the RenameRename/RenameDelete ConflictKinds, ALGORITHM_VERSION is ag-merge/2, and merge-semantics.md has a full 'Renames' section. The table at lib.rs:13-20 also omits TooLarge, RenameRename and RenameDelete. This is user-visible rustdoc that states the opposite of the code.
verdicts.refined_fix: Replace the lib.rs:31-32 paragraph with: 'Since `ag-merge/2` the merge is rename-aware: a file that exists only in the base is paired with a file that exists only in a side, first by identical bytes and then by line similarity (see [`detect_renames`] and the `MIN_SIMILARITY`, `MAX_SIMILARITY_*` bounds). When one side moved a file and the other edited it, the edit is merged at the new path. Both sides moving it to different paths is `RenameRename`; a move against a delete is `RenameDelete`. Directory renames and copies are not detected; they appear as per-file renames and adds.' Add table rows: `file larger than MAX_TEXT_MERGE_SIZE edited on both sides | TooLarge conflict`, `both sides renamed to different paths | RenameRename conflict`, `one side renamed, other deleted | RenameDelete conflict`. Optionally add a doc-sync test that asserts the 'ag-merge/2' tag appears in docs/architecture/merge-semantics.md.

verdicts.reason: lib.rs:49 hardcodes 'ag-merge/2+ag-diff/1', duplicating ag_diff::ALGORITHM_VERSION ('ag-diff/1', ag-diff lib.rs:17). Grep shows that constant is referenced nowhere else. The ag-diff docs (lib.rs:7) say behaviour changes bump it, but nothing ties the merge tag to it. The tag is written into merge changeset messages at integrate.rs:421, workspace.rs:276 and virtual_ws.rs:221, so a missed sync would produce wrong audit metadata. It is a latent drift risk rather than a current bug, and the tag should stay an explicit literal because changing it changes merge changeset ids.

MAX_TEXT_MERGE_SIZE is a named, public, documented constant (merge-semantics.md, TooLarge ConflictKind) that is deliberately pinned for determinism, so it is a design decision and not a hardcoded-value defect. The read-before-check ordering at tree.rs:501-505 is accurate, but it is bounded by max_blob_size per blob (three blobs at most, only when both sides changed the same huge file), and BlobIo has no size API. That makes it a minor optimisation that needs a public trait change, not a defect.

The 2048 cap is documented in the ag-diff module docs and in merge-semantics.md:66-67 ('always correct but not minimal'), so the claim that it is undocumented is wrong. The finding's own scenario does not false-conflict: I ran merge_text on a 20k-line file where ours rewrites lines 0-3000 and theirs rewrites 17000-20000, and it returned Clean. Prefix/suffix trimming makes the fallback hunk equal the true hunk when a side has one contiguous edit region. Only a single side with several distant edits and a total edit distance over 2048 degrades. That is a deliberate memory/determinism trade-off, and conflicting is the safe direction.

The four rename thresholds are named pub constants, documented in rename.rs module docs, merge-semantics.md ('more than 200 deleted or added files ... means exact matches only') and ADR-0005 (line 24). They are pinned on purpose so the result depends only on the inputs. This is a documented design bound with no defect; making it configurable is a feature request.

This is a feature gap, not a stub. ConflictRegion is part of merge_text's public result, and production uses merge_text's `rendered` output for `ag sync` marker files (workspace.rs:~300). ConflictInfo{path, kind} is the deliberately small API shape, and the documented resolution flow (merge-semantics.md 'Conflict resolution flow') is marker files plus `ag snapshot`. Exposing regions through HTTP/gRPC/SDKs is a product enhancement spanning many crates, not something the engine hides or fakes.

unified_diff feeds display only. The consumers are `ag diff` terminal output and the FileDiff.patch JSON string (api_support.rs:38), which only the web DiffFile.vue parser reads. Its headers are the non-git `diff --ag` form, and no docs claim it is patch-applicable. Nothing in the repo applies it. U+FFFD rendering for non-UTF-8 text is the conventional behaviour for a String/JSON diff view, and NUL-based binary detection is documented. This is not simulated behaviour.

8192 appears once, inside is_binary, and its doc comment already says 'a NUL byte in the first 8 KiB'. All callers (tree.rs:507, rename.rs:178, blame.rs, api_support.rs) go through the function, so nothing is duplicated. Extracting a named constant is cosmetic, and the finding itself calls it borderline and git-like.

The 'ours'/'theirs' labels are the documented git-style marker format (merge-semantics.md: `<<<<<<< ours` / `=======` / `>>>>>>> theirs`). workspace.rs:11 and workspace.rs:347 rely on exactly these prefixes, so they are consistent and intentional. Because merge_text is a pure function of three byte strings, the labels carry no stream names. Custom labels and diff3 base sections would be an enhancement, not a defect.

Confirmed in ag-dag lib.rs. Every id in `results` is pushed only right after `*entry |= RESULT` (loop at ~lines 202-206), so `flags[id] & STALE == 0 || flags[id] & RESULT != 0` is always true. The filter is a no-op, and correctness comes from the later pairwise is_ancestor elimination. merge_bases is called in production (integrate.rs, workspace.rs, virtual_ws.rs). The impact is low: dead, misleading logic with no behavioural effect.
verdicts.refined_fix: Replace `let mut candidates: Vec<ChangesetId> = results.into_iter().filter(|id| flags[id] & STALE == 0 || flags[id] & RESULT != 0).collect();` with `let mut candidates: Vec<ChangesetId> = results;` and add a comment that the explicit is_ancestor pass below is what removes redundant bases. Behaviour is identical because the predicate was always true. The existing merge_bases_match_naive proptest guards it.

verdicts.reason: This is test-only code. Mem in ag-merge/src/tests.rs and tests/scale.rs is a faithful content-addressed BlobIo (hash_blob), not canned data, and the finding itself calls it borderline. The production adapter RepoBlobs (ag-integrate/src/repo.rs:288) runs against the real object store in the ag-integrate engine tests. Missing error-propagation tests are a test-coverage wish and not a stub or mock hiding behaviour.

The ignored scale tests are deliberately labelled `#[ignore = "measurement"]`. ADR-0006 and the README report the numbers as a one-off measurement ('Release build on a 4-vCPU Intel Xeon @ 2.10 GHz cloud VM'; README: 'measured at 100 000 files'), not as a CI-enforced guarantee. Wall-clock assertions in shared CI would be flaky. Rename+edit correctness and incremental/full agreement are covered by the normal tests (the strategies_agree proptest and the rename tests), which cargo test --workspace runs.

The descriptions are terse but accurate, and no crate is published. docs/operations/releasing.md:52 states 'no publishing to crates.io', and release.yml builds binaries for GitHub releases only. The metadata therefore never reaches a registry or docs.rs, and nothing in production reads it.

Confirmed in tree.rs:301-305: Tree::from_entries(...) errors are matched with `Err(_) => ours.clone()`, and the FileDirectory conflicts are only pushed for the file/dir case. from_entries in ag-tree/src/lib.rs:153 returns TooManyEntries when merged.len() > limits.max_tree_entries, and nothing pushes a conflict for it. merge_incremental declines on the same condition (apply, lib.rs:215), so merge_full returns `ours` with empty conflicts and is_clean() is true. integrate.rs:398-406 then computes head_tree.diff(&merged.tree), which is empty, so a merge changeset with parents [head, proposal] is built that drops all of theirs. That is silent data loss. The strategies_agree proptest only uses lim(), so this branch is untested.

The ops in merge_incremental (tree.rs:224-237) are built so that NoOpPut and DeleteMissing cannot occur: a Put is emitted only when want != ours.get(path), a Delete only when ours has the path, and the BTreeMap keys are unique. So the only reachable apply errors are FileDirectoryConflict and TooManyEntries, and both are meant to go to merge_full, the documented reference algorithm (comment at 194-198). The fallback is therefore not what hides the problem. Once finding 0 is fixed, merge_full recomputes TooManyEntries and returns Err, and any hypothetical engine bug is answered by the reference algorithm. Narrowing the match would only save a redundant recomputation on a rare path.

lib.rs:31-32 says `Merge does not detect renames in this version`, but rename.rs exists, merge_trees calls plan_renames (tree.rs:137), ALGORITHM_VERSION is `ag-merge/2`, and merge-semantics.md and ADR-0005 describe rename-aware merging. The table at lib.rs:13-20 also omits TooLarge, RenameRename and RenameDelete, which tree.rs defines and merge-semantics.md lists. The crate docs state the opposite of the code.
verdicts.refined_fix: In crates/ag-merge/src/lib.rs replace lines 31-32 with a paragraph saying: since `ag-merge/2` the merge is rename-aware. Before the per-path rules, each side is compared with the base: exact renames (identical bytes) first, then similar ones (>= MIN_SIMILARITY percent, files <= MAX_SIMILARITY_FILE_SIZE, within MAX_SIMILARITY_CANDIDATES and MAX_SIMILARITY_WORK, otherwise exact only). A file moved on one side and edited on the other is merged at its new path, and the Conflict carries `origin`. Directory renames and copies are not detected; they appear as one rename per file or as an add. Extend the table with: `file over MAX_TEXT_MERGE_SIZE (16 MiB) on any side | TooLarge conflict`, `both sides moved the file to different paths | RenameRename conflict (at the old path)`, `one side moved it, the other deleted it | RenameDelete conflict (at the new path)`. Add a unit test that fails when the doc and the code drift, for example one asserting that `include_str!("../../../docs/architecture/merge-semantics.md")` contains `ALGORITHM_VERSION` and each ConflictKind variant name.

verdicts.reason: lib.rs:49 hand-copies `+ag-diff/1`. grep shows ag_diff::ALGORITHM_VERSION (ag-diff/src/lib.rs:17) is referenced nowhere outside its own definition, although the ag-diff docs say it is `recorded alongside merge results`. No test ties the two together. engine.rs:147 pins only the full literal. So bumping the ag-diff constant after a behaviour change changes nothing in the Merge-Algorithm trailer written at integrate.rs:421, workspace.rs:276 and virtual_ws.rs:221. The rest of the finding is not warranted: MAX_TEXT_MERGE_SIZE, the rename thresholds and MAX_EDIT_DISTANCE are part of the versioned, documented algorithm `ag-merge/2`, and making them configurable parameters would be a separate, speculative feature.

MAX_TEXT_MERGE_SIZE is a named, pub, documented limit (merge-semantics.md line 30: `a file over 16 MiB on any side` gives a TooLarge conflict). It is part of the deterministic algorithm tagged `ag-merge/2`, and making it a per-repo setting would make results depend on config unless the tag changed with it. The memory ordering is a real micro-issue, since tree.rs:501-505 reads all three blobs before the size check. But it only occurs for a both-sides-modified file, it is bounded by max_blob_size, and fixing it means a breaking change to the BlobIo trait. No operator is misled, because the behaviour is documented and TooLarge is reported as a typed conflict.

MAX_EDIT_DISTANCE is a documented, versioned property of ag-diff/1. The module docs (ag-diff/src/lib.rs:9-12) and merge-semantics.md both say beyond 2048 the middle becomes one hunk that is correct but not minimal. The finding's example is also wrong. Rewriting 3000 lines at the top on one side and 3000 lines at the bottom on the other gives two separate trimmed hunks (prefix/suffix stripping runs per side against base), which do not overlap, so merge_text (text.rs) merges them cleanly today. A false conflict needs a single side with more than ~1000 changed lines spread widely and the other side editing inside that span. That is an accurate, documented limitation, and replacing Myers with a linear-space variant would change ag-diff/1 semantics for a corner case.

The four rename thresholds are documented in rename.rs module docs (lines 11-18), merge-semantics.md (`more than 200 deleted or added files, or too many line comparisons, means exact matches only`) and ADR-0005. They are deliberately fixed so the result stays a pure function of the trees, and they are pinned under the `ag-merge/2` tag. Above 200 candidates exact-content renames still work, and moved-and-edited files fall back to an explicit, typed DeleteModify conflict that the user can resolve. That is a disclosed bounded-work limitation (README says `Rename detection is per file`), not a hidden defect.

This is a feature request, not a stub or a defect. Conflicts are typed through the ConflictKind enum (README: `Typed conflicts; nothing is guessed`), and merge_text already returns structured ConflictRegion values as public API. ag-integrate::ConflictInfo carries {path, kind string} and ag sync writes the full markers into the files, so locations are available to agents. Nothing in the docs promises region-level data in the API. Extending the protocol and SDKs with regions is roadmap work, not a correctness or honesty problem.

unified_diff is a display renderer. It returns a Rust String, and its doc says only that it renders a line-based diff and reports binary data in one line. String::from_utf8_lossy is the standard way to show non-UTF-8 text through the String/JSON API, and the U+FFFD characters make the non-UTF-8 content visible instead of hiding it. Both versions of a changed line still appear as -/+ lines, so a change is never hidden. Nothing in the docs promises that the output can be applied with patch. Byte-exact patch output would be a new feature.

The NUL-in-first-8-KiB rule is a documented heuristic (ag-diff doc comment, and merge-semantics.md `NUL in first 8 KiB`) that mirrors git's approach. It is part of the versioned ag-diff/1 behaviour. It is not presented as intelligence, and naming the literal would be cosmetic. Treating UTF-16 as binary only yields a conservative Binary conflict. It never produces a wrong merge.

The `<<<<<<< ours` / `=======` / `>>>>>>> theirs` markers are a documented file-format convention (merge-semantics.md, last section). workspace.rs has_markers and the `ag snapshot` refusal depend on the exact prefixes. Fixed git-style labels are standard and the output is deterministic. Per-side labels or a diff3 base section would be an enhancement, not something that hurts or misleads users.

The filter at ag-dag lib.rs:219 is indeed always true: RESULT is set at lines 203-205 before each push to `results` and flags are only OR-ed. But it is harmless dead logic. Correctness comes from the explicit sort/dedup and pairwise is_ancestor redundancy elimination on lines 220-235, which is commented and covered by the merge_bases proptest against a naive implementation. Nobody is misled or hurt, and `implementing real stale pruning` would be a risky algorithm change for a cosmetic cleanup.

The Mem BlobIo in ag-merge tests (tests.rs and tests/scale.rs) is a faithful content-addressed store using ag_object::hash_blob, not canned data. ag-merge is a pure-logic crate that should not depend on ag-storage. The real-store path, via RepoBlobs over Repository (ag-integrate/src/repo.rs:286-296), is exercised by the ag-integrate tests (e.g. tests/engine.rs). Keeping the in-memory double for fast property tests is the right design.

The scale tests state they are measurements (`Ignored by default (a measurement, not a check)`), and ADR-0006 gives the exact command to reproduce them. README:402 says `measured at 100 000 files`, which is an accurate statement of a past measurement, not a continuously guarded SLA. The correctness behaviours inside (clean incremental merge, rename plus edit) are covered at small size by the normal ag-merge tests, including the strategies_agree proptest and the rename tests. A CI wall-clock budget at 500k entries would be flaky. This is an optional hardening idea, not a misleading claim.

The `AgentGit: ag-merge` style descriptions are terse but not false. adr-traceability.md:46 already says 'at-least-once; in-process consumer (tree derivation)' and derive.rs:46 says notification-only topics have no in-process consumer, so no external delivery is promised. The only derive_pending callers are integrate.rs:285 and publish.rs:373 (inline, in the request thread) plus tests; ag-server has no dispatcher task (server.rs only spawns rebuild_job_index). Both `let _ =` discard the Result and the DeriveReport, ag-integrate has no tracing dependency, and outbox_pending_count is read nowhere outside derive.rs and a test, so a failing derivation (outbox_fail stores attempts/last_error) is invisible to operators. The impact is limited because trees are a disposable cache that readers recompute, so severity is low to medium, and a threaded dispatcher is more than is needed.

Expired intents become terminal, so a rerun drains the remainder, but Blocked 'waiting' intents stay non-terminal and are oldest-first, so 10,000 or more of them would starve newer ones. The harm is silent and limited to extreme volumes, so severity is low.

verdicts.reason: MAX_CAS_ATTEMPTS = 8 is a deliberate bounded retry. A lost CAS means another integration just succeeded, so the system as a whole always makes progress, and the intent is persistent and resumable. The outer contract is defined and documented: the server maps Error::Contention to ErrorCode::Aborted with retry_after 200 ms (ag-server/src/error.rs:136), and troubleshooting.md:24 documents 'stream changed 8 times ... retry'. The test's 50-iteration outer loop is that documented client retry, not a symptom of a missing knob.

integrate.rs:184-187: `integration_result` turns a failed `serde_json::from_value` of intent.result into `Outcome::Invalid { reason: "unreadable result" }`, paired with the intent's real state (for example Integrated). The caller sees a contradictory result for an operation that actually succeeded, and the corruption or version skew is not reported. The function is reached from `operation()` and `operation_by_key()` (`ag op show`, the server operation endpoints) and from advance_integrate on terminal intents (integrate.rs:225-227), so it is on the production path. A rolling upgrade where a newer Outcome variant is read by an older binary is a plausible trigger.

The function already returns Result, and ag-server maps Error::Meta through `m.into()`. Add an fsck check (kind `unreadable_intent_result`) that reads terminal intents (`intents_in_states` for Integrated, Published, Rejected, Aborted) and attempts to deserialize each one's result as Outcome. Test: write a bad JSON into intents.result for a terminal intent via raw SQL and assert that `operation()` returns Err(Meta(Corrupt)) and fsck reports `unreadable_intent_result`, on both SQLite and PostgreSQL.

verdicts.reason: The placeholder author, timestamp and 'preview' operation id exist only to build a throwaway Changeset in compute_candidate when merge_meta is None. It is never stored (`if merge_meta.is_some() { put_changeset }`, integrate.rs:432) and merge_preview ignores the Merge `id` (`Candidate::Merge { new_tree, head_tree, base, .. }`, line 466). Building it is useful: `Changeset::build` applies the same Limits checks (max_ops, message length) as the real integration, so skipping it would let a preview report a clean merge that then fails at integrate time. No placeholder data reaches any output.

with_stores has no production caller: the only callers are tests (tests/common/mod.rs:44) and `ephemeral` (itself used only by workdir/tests.rs); the CLI and server go through Repository::open. The phantom layout is also not silently dangerous: the doc comment states that reopen and backup are unavailable, reopen then fails with a Config error (no .ag/config.json), and backup would fail at copy_dir because `<tmp>/ag-ephemeral/.ag/store/objects/objects` is never created.

Repository::ephemeral is a documented in-memory constructor for tests and embedding. It is not used by the CLI, the server or any other production path, and it substitutes nothing the product ships. Its sole caller is the unit test workdir/tests.rs:9. Removing or gating it is cosmetic API hygiene, not a defect, and finding 22 shows the same memory stores are intentionally what ag_storage::testing uses.

The failpoints are inert in production: Failpoints::arm is called only from tests (tests/engine.rs:245-306, tests/lifecycle.rs:86), no binary arms one, and `hit` on an empty set is an uncontended mutex lookup at seven protocol steps that each already perform database transactions. The integration tests under tests/ link the library without cfg(test), so gating would need a feature plus a self dev-dependency for no behavioural gain. This is the standard fault-injection pattern, not simulated behaviour.

workdir/mod.rs:245-249 writes the file and then calls `set_permissions(0o755 or 0o644)`, which overrides the process umask. A user with umask 077 therefore gets world-readable checked-out files, unlike git, which creates files as 0666/0777 & ~umask. write_entry is reached from checkout_tree and update_dir, which the CLI uses (repo.rs, policy.rs:166).
verdicts.refined_fix: In `write_entry` (workdir/mod.rs, `FileType::Regular` arm) replace `fs::write` plus `set_permissions` on unix with: `use std::io::Write; use std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt; let mut f = fs::OpenOptions::new().write(true).create_new(true).mode(if entry.executable { 0o777 } else { 0o666 }).open(&tmp)?; f.write_all(&data)?;`. The kernel then applies the umask, so 022 gives 755/644 as before, while 077 gives 700/600. Keep `fs::write` under `#[cfg(not(unix))]`. Test as an end-to-end test in ag-cli/tests/cli.rs that runs a real `ag checkout` via `sh -c 'umask 077; ag ...'` in a tempdir and asserts the modes (umask is process-global, so do not test it in-process), plus the existing 755/644 assertions under umask 022.

It is reachable through `ag queue run` (flow.rs:502) and the gRPC/HTTP queue.run. It is not 'forever': it resolves when the lease is released or expires and the entry is enqueued again. The queue and fencing features simply do not compose, and no doc mentions this.

Add `fencing_tokens: &[u64]` to `Repository::enqueue` and `Tx::queue_push`, expose it as `ag queue add <proposal> --fencing-token N` (flow.rs:479) and as a new field in the Enqueue request in proto/agwp/v1/agwp.proto (then regenerate openapi.json and the SDKs). In `run_queue`, parse `entry.fencing_tokens` and pass it as `IntegrateRequest.fencing_tokens`. Stale tokens stay safe because lease_blockers compares them to the active lease's token at integrate time. Test on real SQLite and PostgreSQL: agent A holds an exclusive lease on src/**, enqueues its proposal with the token, a different integrator runs the queue, and the proposal lands. A stale token must give state 'blocked' with the 'stale_or_missing_token' blocker.

verdicts.reason: The code is honest: backup.rs:72 refuses PostgreSQL with a pointer to pg_dump, a refusal tested at tests/lifecycle.rs:522. But the adr-traceability.md DR row is marked ✅ with evidence '`ag backup` (DB first, GC held off, verified), `ag verify`' and no PostgreSQL caveat. durability.md:82-84 admits the pg_dump/restore round trip was 'exercised by hand', and grep finds no automated pg_dump/pg_restore test. Implementing a dump inside `ag` would be wrong, since pg_dump or PITR is the right tool, so the defect is the unqualified claim and the missing automated proof.
verdicts.refined_fix: 1) Change the evidence cell of that traceability row to: '`ag backup` for SQLite with files or S3 (DB first, GC held off, verified). PostgreSQL: not wrapped by `ag`; `pg_dump`/PITR, then reconcile with `ag verify` ([durability](../operations/durability.md#postgresql-and-s3))', with 🟡 until step 2 lands. 2) Add a test in crates/ag-integrate/tests/storage.rs, gated on AG_TEST_POSTGRES_URL (scripts/pg-test.sh already locates the PostgreSQL binaries), that integrates a change on a real PostgreSQL repository, runs `pg_dump --schema=<schema> --format=custom`, runs DROP SCHEMA, runs `pg_restore`, reopens the repository and asserts `fsck().is_ok()` with the same audit_head. Once it passes in the CI `backends` job, flip the row back to ✅ and cite the test name, and replace 'exercised by hand' in durability.md.

verdicts.reason: `n > 100_000` (history.rs:113) is a parser-side sanity bound that returns an explicit 'revision suffix too large' error, and `max_dag_depth.min(5_000_000)` (line 184) is a visited-node walk guard that surfaces as DagError::LimitExceeded. Neither silently changes results, and Limits itself is intentionally fixed (see finding 3). Naming the constants is style only, not a functional or operational defect.

These are response-size and DoS guards that fail loudly or flag themselves: diff_report sets `truncated` (api_support.rs:79-82), ancestors_between returns an explicit Invalid error beyond MAX_NEGOTIATED, and the blame limits (4 MiB, 100 000 lines) are documented as refusals in docs/guides/history.md:51. They do not hide data or misreport state. Making them per-deployment configuration is a feature request, not a hardcode defect, and the protocol-facing ones should stay consistent across servers and clients.

The claim that fx() uses in-memory stores by default is accurate (TestMeta::new uses Meta::open_in_memory, TestObjects uses MemoryObjectStore), but that is real SQLite and the suites test engine logic, and the same suites run unchanged on PostgreSQL and S3 in the CI backends job. The default FS backend is covered by real-disk tests elsewhere: init_repo in 11 lifecycle tests and 2 engine tests, the ag-storage FsObjectStore unit tests (object_store.rs:434-540), the ag-cli e2e tests that drive the real `ag` binary, and the ag-server HTTP and gRPC flows. The gap is a marginal test-matrix preference, not an uncovered product path.

The claim that an external consumer can never receive the event is wrong. crates/ag-server/src/api/events.rs builds the SSE/replay feed from the audit log, and integrate.rs:549 writes the `stream.integrate` audit row with the same data (old_head, new_head, version, operation_id) in the same transaction. derive.rs:46 documents that notification-only topics have no in-process consumer, and adr-traceability.md:46 already says 'in-process consumer (tree derivation)'. Building a webhook dispatcher would add a second event channel nobody asked for.

No background dispatcher exists. derive_pending is called inline only at integrate.rs:285 and publish.rs:373, with `let _ =`, yet publication-and-integration.md:43, storage.md:131 and the derive.rs header say 'asynchronously (the outbox dispatcher)'. outbox_pending_count and outbox_history have no caller outside tests, so a persistently failing derive is invisible to every tool. The impact is only slower reads, because trees are disposable and recomputed.
verdicts.refined_fix: Keep the inline pass. (1) Correct the three doc sites to say derivation runs inline after the commit, is best-effort, records failures on the outbox row (`attempts`, `last_error`), and is retried by the next publish/integrate or by `ag reindex`. (2) Make failures visible. Add `Tx::outbox_failing_count()` (`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM outbox WHERE dispatched_at IS NULL AND last_error IS NOT NULL`) in crates/ag-storage/src/meta/outbox.rs. Add informational `outbox_pending: u64` and `outbox_failing: u64` fields to `FsckReport` (fsck.rs), and print them with the oldest `last_error` in `ag verify`. Do not make them `issues`, because `ag backup` runs fsck on its copy and a retry-able derive failure must not fail a backup. (3) Add a lifecycle test that makes `derive_tree` fail once, for example by damaging a keyframe's parent object. Assert that fsck reports `outbox_failing == 1`, that the next `derive_pending` clears it, and that `last_error` is NULL afterwards.

verdicts.reason: The 64 in publish.rs:373 (and 256 in integrate.rs:285) is the size of an internal catch-up pass over disposable derived data. Events beyond the batch stay pending in id order and are picked up by the next pass, so correctness does not depend on it. The swallowed error is the same issue as finding 1 and is covered by its fix.

Limits::default() is the documented format-level validation rule set (docs/architecture/object-format.md:87, security.md:29), enforced when changesets and trees are decoded and published. A per-repository override would make the same history valid in one repository and invalid in another, which breaks clone, push and fetch. Operators already cap request size and use quotas on the server (ag-server config `limits.max_request_bytes`).

The PostgreSQL defaults are documented in docs/operations/postgres-and-s3.md:79-81, storage.md:89 and ADR-0004 (lock_timeout 30 s, idle-in-transaction 10 min). `pool_size` is already configurable and the rest are library-level PgOptions. Write transactions are a few short statements, so these are sane defaults rather than defects. Six more validated config fields would add surface for no demonstrated operator harm.

S3Config's max_retries 5 and 5-minute request_timeout are internal client defaults. docs/operations/postgres-and-s3.md:122 documents the retry behaviour. They only matter on pathological links, and 256 MiB blobs would need to run under about 1 MB/s to hit the deadline. This is a tuning wish, not a defect.

I read fsck.rs in full. It checks objects, the changeset index, parents, stream heads (only the head's cached tree is compared), reflog ends and the audit chain. It never touches pins, open-proposal heads, workspace head/base, reviews, queue rows, intents or leases. Yet storage.md:123 states 'referential consistency is checked by `ag verify`', and durability.md:78-81 tells operators to use verify to reconcile a restored database against the bucket. The fsck.rs doc comment also claims 'the derived tree caches' are recomputed, when only stream-head caches are. GC fails closed on a missing root, so this misleads but does not lose data.
verdicts.refined_fix: In fsck.rs, after the stream loop, iterate `self.meta.read(|tx| tx.live_roots())?`. It already returns stream heads, pins, open-proposal heads and workspace head/base. For each id call `self.history.changeset(&id)`. Do not use `is_ready`, because proposal and workspace heads may legitimately be unpublished. On `SourceError::NotFound` push `FsckIssue{kind:"dangling_root", ...}`; on any other error push `unreadable_changeset`. Add an additive `roots_checked: usize` to `FsckReport`. Narrow the doc comment to 'the cached tree of every stream head, recomputed from history'. Rewrite storage.md:123 to list exactly what `ag verify` checks, and state that reviews, attestations, queue rows, intents and leases are not cross-checked. Add `dangling_root` to the table in docs/operations/troubleshooting.md:72. Extend crates/ag-integrate/tests/lifecycle.rs with raw-SQL corruption (`UPDATE pins SET changeset=..`, `UPDATE workspaces SET head=..`) on `disk_repo`, asserting `dangling_root`.

verdicts.reason: Windows has no executable bit, and `#[cfg(not(unix))] is_executable() -> false` is the standard portability fallback. No workflow builds or tests Windows (ci.yml only has ubuntu and macos; release.yml has no Windows target), and no doc claims Windows support. docs/architecture/security.md:70 treats Windows only as a case-folding caveat. The behaviour belongs to task #20 and can only be validated on a Windows runner, so it is not a shipped defect today.

The limitation is stated honestly in four places: adr-traceability.md:44, postgres-and-s3.md:209-212, ADR-0004:76 and the s3-test.sh header. moto runs as a separate HTTP server that independently recomputes SigV4 signatures, not an in-process mock. The suites are driven by `AG_TEST_S3_ENDPOINT` (tests/common/mod.rs:85-104), so any real S3 or MinIO runs them with one command. A MinIO CI job would be nice to have, but it is not a misleading claim.

Sockets, FIFOs and devices cannot be represented as a FileType (only regular and symlink exist), so skipping them is the same convention git follows. mod.rs:89 and the tests document and pin the behaviour (`report.skipped`). Nothing a user could restore is lost, and nobody is misled about tracked content.

`intents_in_states` orders by `updated_at` (oldest first) and `recover` is a manual, re-runnable command (`ag recover`, flow.rs:442). Expired intents leave the set on each run, so a backlog above 10 000 drains over successive runs. Starvation would need more than 10 000 fresh Blocked intents, which is unrealistic.

MAX_CAS_ATTEMPTS is an internal optimistic-retry budget. When it is exhausted, Error::Contention maps to `ErrorCode::Aborted` with `retry_after(200)` (ag-server/src/error.rs:136). docs/guides/sdks.md:193 documents that the SDKs retry retryable errors with exponential backoff and full jitter. The operation is idempotent and resumable, so the outer retry loop in the test is exactly the intended client behaviour.

The fallback runs only when a stored Outcome JSON fails to deserialize, which needs version skew or manual database edits. The returned reason is the explicit text 'unreadable result' and `state` still carries the real intent state, so the corruption is not disguised as a plausible validation error. It is a deliberate degrade on an extremely rare path.

I verified that in compute_candidate the placeholder MergeMeta is used only when `merge_meta` is None (the dry-run preview). In that case `put_changeset` is skipped (integrate.rs:433). `merge_preview` discards the id (`Candidate::Merge { new_tree, head_tree, base, .. }`), so the placeholder never reaches storage or an API response.

`with_stores` is called only by `ephemeral` and tests, and its doc says reopen and backup are unavailable. The phantom path `<tmp>/ag-ephemeral` is never created by any code, so `reopen()` fails with 'not an AgentGit repository' and the object copy in `backup()` fails with ENOENT. Reading someone else's data would need another party to plant a full repository at that exact path. That is a contrived misuse of a test-oriented constructor.

`ephemeral` is a documented embedding and test constructor ('for tests and embedding') over the same trait objects the product uses. It does not pose as production behaviour and has no operator-visible effect. Real FS and Repository::init paths are covered by `disk_repo` (12 uses), the ag-cli e2e tests and the ag-server tests.

Failpoints are one-shot, only reachable by code already holding an in-process `Repository` handle (the same trust level as the engine itself), and documented as 'tests only; never armed in production' (repo.rs:193, failpoints.rs:7). The tests/ integration suites need them, so `#[cfg(test)]` cannot gate them. A mutex lookup next to database transactions is negligible.

write_entry (workdir/mod.rs:243-249) does `fs::write` and then `set_permissions(0o755|0o644)`, so the process umask is ignored. Under umask 077 or 027 (common on hardened hosts) checked-out and synced files become group- or world-readable, which is broader than what git and every ordinary create would give. Nothing documents this, and the only test checks the exec bit.
verdicts.refined_fix: In workdir/mod.rs write_entry, replace the unix branch with a creation that lets the kernel apply the umask (no unsafe, no libc): `use std::io::Write; use std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt; let mode = if entry.executable { 0o777 } else { 0o666 }; let mut f = fs::OpenOptions::new().write(true).create_new(true).mode(mode).open(&tmp)?; f.write_all(&data)?;`. Keep `fs::write` under `#[cfg(not(unix))]`. `create_new` also gives O_EXCL on the temp name. Default umask 022 still yields 0644/0755. Change the existing assertion `mode & 0o111 == 0o111` in workdir/tests.rs:45 to `mode & 0o100 != 0` so it holds under any umask. Add a crates/ag-cli/tests/cli.rs case that runs `sh -c 'umask 077; ag checkout ...'` against a real tree and asserts regular files are 0600 and executables 0700. This avoids changing the umask of the test process.

verdicts.reason: An exclusive lease held by the proposal's author makes the queued integration fail closed with a visible `stale_or_missing_token` blocker. That text is recorded on the queue row ('blocked', queue.rs:~70). It is not blocked forever: it clears when the lease is released or expires, and `ag integrate --fencing-token` is the direct path. Carrying tokens through the queue needs a schema column plus proto, OpenAPI and SDK changes (EnqueueRequest has no such field) for a rare combination.

The refusal is explicit in the code error, postgres-and-s3.md:15 and troubleshooting.md. durability.md gives a complete PostgreSQL procedure (pg_dump, copy the bucket after the dump, restore, then `ag verify`) and records a hand-run round trip. Reimplementing pg_dump inside the engine would be worse than using the standard tool. The traceability row's evidence column is merely terse, and the capability itself exists.

`~N`/`^N` above 100 000 is an input-sanity bound on a revision suffix (`^N` is already bounded by max_parents = 16). The 5 000 000 walk cap is a DoS guard on an interactive log walk. `max_dag_depth` is a fixed format limit (see finding 3), not an operator-configurable one, so there is no 'configurable limit' being undercut.

These are named response-size and input-sanity caps. The diff report sets `truncated` (api_support.rs), blame limits are documented in docs/guides/history.md:51 ('Limits, always reported'), and negotiation, attestation-count and title caps reject oversized input explicitly. Nothing is silent or misleading, and no operator need for tuning is shown.

The engine suites deliberately test engine logic over the ObjectStore trait. The default FS store has its own tests in ag-storage/src/object_store.rs, and the real FS plus SQLite path runs through `disk_repo` in the lifecycle and storage tests, the ag-cli e2e tests (cli.rs, quickstart.rs) and the ag-server tests. CI also runs the whole suite on PostgreSQL + S3. A plain `cargo test` therefore does exercise the shipped default backend.

Confirmed: proto Conflict.kind promises snake_case codes, but integrate.rs:402, workspace.rs:294 and virtual_ws.rs:200 fill it with ConflictKind's Display text (tree.rs:63-81), and convert.rs:238 passes it through. The web UI (ProposalView.vue:272, spec fixtures use 'content'/'both_added') and the Go advisor ('Reported by the server as') each assume a different shape, and rename_rename/rename_delete are missing from the documented set.
verdicts.refined_fix: Add ConflictKind::code() in crates/ag-merge/src/tree.rs returning content|both_added|delete_modify|binary|type_change|too_large|file_directory|rename_rename|rename_delete. In ConflictInfo (ag-integrate types.rs) set kind to the code and add `#[serde(default)] message` holding the Display text; update integrate.rs:402, workspace.rs:294, virtual_ws.rs:200. Add `string message = 3;` to proto Conflict, list all nine codes in its comment, and copy both fields in ag-server convert::conflict. Update ProposalView.vue (badge from kind, message as title) and Go agwp.Conflict plus advisor render to use Message. Regenerate openapi.json and the TS/Python schemas. Add per-kind merge tests that assert the wire kind over HTTP and gRPC.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed: events.rs:1-8 and to_event set topic to the audit action, and the audit actions in the code are stream.integrate, proposal.create, lease.acquire, job.enqueue, run.start, policy.set and so on. None of the proto's examples is an audit action; 'stream.updated' is only an outbox topic (integrate.rs:556), not an event. docs/protocol/agwp-v1.md:174 is correct, but the proto comment is copied into openapi.json and both SDK schemas, so generated docs mislead.
verdicts.refined_fix: Rewrite the Event.topic comment to list real audit actions (stream.integrate, stream.cas, proposal.create, proposal.review, lease.acquire, job.enqueue, run.start, policy.set, ...) and to say the topics filter is a dotted-prefix match (topics=["proposal"] matches proposal.create). Then regenerate docs/protocol/openapi.json, apps/web/src/api/schema.gen.ts, sdk/typescript/src/generated/schema.ts and the Python models. Add an ag-server test that subscribes with topics=["proposal.create"] and receives the event.

verdicts.reason: The status mismatch is real: registry.rs:202 writes 'abandoned' and storage meta/agents.rs:38 documents it, while the proto and the generated schemas promise 'stale', which no code path ever sets. The missing server-side reaper is not a defect by itself: reap is a documented manual command (docs/guides/agents.md:19, `ag agent reap`), and the web UI derives staleness from last_heartbeat_ms (runs.ts).
verdicts.refined_fix: Fix the contract only. Change the Run.status comment to: "running", "completed", "failed" or "abandoned" (set by `ag agent reap` when the heartbeat is older than the timeout; clients derive liveness from last_heartbeat_ms). Regenerate openapi.json and the TS/Python schemas. Add a line to docs/guides/agents.md that server deployments should run `ag agent reap` on a schedule. A background reaper in ag-server is a separate feature and not required to fix this defect.

verdicts.reason: Only the SetPolicy part holds. The Conventions text calls SetPolicy 'naturally idempotent', but ag-integrate admin.rs:283-301 calls policy_put, which always appends MAX(version)+1 and writes an audit row, and policy.md:67 says a new version invalidates earlier attestations. A retry or a GitOps-style re-apply therefore silently blocks validated proposals. The other ~19 idempotency_key fields are each labelled 'Accepted and ignored: this operation does not deduplicate', so they are an honestly documented limitation.
verdicts.refined_fix: Make SetPolicy genuinely idempotent. In Repository::set_policy (crates/ag-integrate/src/admin.rs:283), inside the write transaction compare the sha256 of the canonical document with tx.policy_current(stream).doc_hash. If they are equal, return the current PolicyRow without appending a version or an audit entry. Correct the proto Conventions paragraph (lines 12-19) to match, and add a test that setting the same document twice leaves a single version. Leave the other labelled 'ignored' fields unchanged.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed: the proto comment lists 'approvals' and 'not_allowed', which are never produced. Blocker::from_unmet (types.rs:41-45) uses the serde tag of Unmet, and integrate.rs:691 adds 'lease'. The real stable table is in docs/guides/policy.md:104-118 (linked from agwp-v1.md), the web UI (blockers.ts) and the Go client use those codes, and the generated SDK docs carry the wrong list. The serde-tag coupling itself is explicit (`rename_all = snake_case`) and documented, so a new Unmet::code() is not needed.
verdicts.refined_fix: Replace the Blocker.code comment with the actual set: missing_validation, failed_validation, insufficient_approvals, changes_requested, missing_provenance, actor_not_allowed, author_not_allowed, too_many_changed_files, lease (see docs/guides/policy.md#outcome-codes). Regenerate the schemas. Add a unit test in ag-policy that pins the serde tag of every Unmet variant to that list, so a rename breaks a test.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed in predict.rs:39,61-75: the full ancestor sets of the stream head and of each open proposal are collected with WALK_LIMIT 50_000, and ag-dag ancestors() returns LimitExceeded, which becomes AgentError::Invalid. predict therefore fails outright on any repository with more than 50k changesets of history, and the cost is proportional to total history rather than divergence. The limit is undocumented and not configurable, and it makes the API unusable rather than degraded.
verdicts.refined_fix: Add an exclusive-range walk to ag-dag (for example `only_in(g, include, exclude, limit)`) that walks both heads in generation order with merge_bases-style painting. It stops when no queued node is painted only-include, so the cost is proportional to the divergence. Use it in predict() for `mine` (proposal minus stream head) and `theirs` (stream head minus proposal). Apply the cap to the size of the divergence, not to total history, and when exceeded return a clear error naming the limit. Test with more than 50k shared changesets and a small divergence.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed at predict.rs:71: `tx.proposals_list(Some("open"), 1000)` orders newest first with SQL LIMIT 1000 across ALL streams, and only then filters by stream. Once more than 1000 proposals are open, older open proposals on the target stream are silently dropped, so overlaps are missed with no error or flag.
verdicts.refined_fix: Add a storage query `proposals_open_for_stream(stream)` (`WHERE state='open' AND stream=?1 ORDER BY created_at, id`) and use it in predict() instead of the global list plus filter. If a cap is kept, make it an explicit error (AgentError::Invalid naming the cap) rather than silently dropping rows. Test with more than 1000 open proposals on other streams plus an overlapping pair on the target stream.

verdicts.reason: The 20-path cut in clip() is a documented sample limit (the Overlap.paths doc comment says 'sorted, truncated to 20'). The overlap itself and its kind are always reported, and the module header says prediction is a conservative advisory signal. Not knowing the total number of shared paths does not mislead anyone about whether overlaps exist.

A stored lease scope can only be written through leases::acquire (the sole lease_insert caller outside tests), which first compiles the scope with the same PathMatcher::new. A later compile failure needs data corruption or a globset syntax change, and leases expire within 24 h. `let Ok(..) else continue` is therefore unreachable defensive code, not enforcement posing as real. The predict.rs:115 copy is advisory only.

The prefix-based overlap test is deliberate, deterministic and documented: docs/guides/agents.md:58 says it 'is conservative (may report an overlap that is not real, never misses one)', and the scopes_may_overlap doc says the same. For an exclusive-lease refusal, a false positive fails safe, and the unit test overlap_is_conservative_but_sound pins the behaviour. Disjoint globs sharing a prefix can use distinct directories or soft leases.

MAX_TTL_MS is a named limit, and the error text states the allowed range ('ttl must be between 1 ms and 86400000 ms'). Leases are renewable through extend(), so a 24 h cap per grant does not constrain a long-running holder. The CLI supplies its own default (--ttl default 1h, cli.md:1375), and rejecting ttl_ms=0 with a clear message does not mislead anyone.

The premise is wrong: .github/workflows/ci.yml has a test matrix of only ubuntu-latest and macos-latest, so Windows is not currently a built or tested target (Windows support is separate in-progress work). ag_crypto::KeyPair::save/load document the 0600 behaviour as Unix-only ('on Unix'), and the KeyStore code is explicitly cfg(unix). Windows ACL handling belongs to that Windows work, not to this finding.

prompt_digest is an agent-supplied, self-signed claim, and provenance.rs:5-12 states claims are not verified ('an agent can lie about its model or rationale'). A well-formed 64-hex string would prove nothing more, so no operator is misled by the missing format check. Unused hex/sha2 dependencies are housekeeping, not a defect in this contract.

The finding's main claims are largely refuted. The canonical form is specified in agwp-v1.md:163-166 (compact JSON, keys sorted at every level, absent optionals as null), and independent vectors do exist: sdk/testdata/gen_signing_vectors.py produces sdk/testdata/signing-vectors.json, which the Python and TypeScript SDK conformance tests check. A residual gap remains. Rust never checks those vectors, and canonical_bytes() relies on serde_json's default sorted map; the workspace does not enable serde_json/preserve_order today. agents_flow.rs signs with the same canonical_bytes, so it cannot catch a regression. docs/architecture/object-format.md:10 still says provenance is covered by 'Rust tests only', which is now stale.
verdicts.refined_fix: Do not write a new canonicalizer or adopt RFC 8785. Add a Rust test in crates/ag-agent (or ag-server) that loads sdk/testdata/signing-vectors.json, builds each ProvenanceRecord, and asserts canonical_bytes() equals case.canonical_json and that the case signature verifies under signing_message. Add a golden-string assertion for key order. Update docs/architecture/object-format.md:10 to name the sdk/testdata provenance vectors.

verdicts.reason: The doc on evaluate() says matcher compilation failures are treated as 'nothing matches', but eval.rs:184-196 calls .expect("validated policy") on every matcher, so an invalid policy panics. The only production caller, verdict_in_tx (integrate.rs:648-655), always obtains the policy through Policy::parse and maps parse errors to MetaError::Invalid, so the panic is unreachable in practice. What remains is a wrong public-API contract.
verdicts.refined_fix: Fix the contract, not the architecture. Replace the doc sentence with: `# Panics` if `policy` did not pass `Policy::validate` (obtain it via `Policy::parse`). A ValidatedPolicy newtype or a Result return is unnecessary because the single caller already validates.

verdicts.reason: Facts.stream is only a documented input-context field (Facts is built by integrate.rs:675 and the tests); evaluate() is a pure function of a per-stream policy, so the stream name does not change the verdict. It is an internal Rust struct, not a wire field, and no operator or client is misled by it.

MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_MS is a named constant, and docs/guides/policy.md:69-70 documents it ('attestations dated more than five minutes in the future are ignored'). It is a fixed security bound, and the finding itself calls it borderline. Per-policy tuning is a feature request, not a defect.

The behaviour is documented and fail-closed. docs/guides/policy.md:88-98 says the envelope requires `max_files > 0` and 'With max_files left at 0 nothing is ever inside the envelope'. A policy with max_files=0 never grants autonomy, which is the restrictive outcome. The 0=unlimited meaning of max_changed_files is a different field with its own documented semantics (document.rs:192).

Only the doc comment is defective. Policy::default() (document.rs:184-186) is described as 'no requirements beyond agents do not integrate themselves', but ApprovalRules::default() sets min_for_agents: 1, so agent-authored changes need a human approval; policy.md:20-22 states this correctly. The 'deployment baseline policy' request is a feature, not a defect: the permissive no-policy default is documented design (policy.md 'Default (no policy stored)', 'Solo project: no policy').
verdicts.refined_fix: Correct the Default impl doc comment to: the built-in policy for a stream with no stored policy (version 0): any non-agent may integrate, with no validations, no path rules and no human approvals for human-authored changes; agents cannot integrate themselves and agent-authored changes need one human approval (approvals.min_for_agents = 1). Do not add a server-level default_document option in this fix.

verdicts.reason: The central claim is wrong. Negotiate's max_object_bytes and max_request_bytes come from the configurable cfg.limits (session.rs:40-41, config.rs:176-195), and ag_protocol::limits is documented as 'Default protocol limits'. MAX_BATCH, MAX_PAGE_SIZE and CHUNK_BYTES are protocol constants. The two remaining literals (100_000 ops, 10_000 changesets per publication) equal ag_types::Limits::default(), which the engine always uses (repo.rs:140), so advertised equals enforced today. Only a hypothetical drift risk remains.

from_status (error.rs:261-282) first decodes ErrorInfo from the status details, then the ag-error-code metadata, and uses the code-based fallback only for non-AGWP peers. It is documented as 'best effort', and the finding concedes this. Genuine AGWP servers always attach the detail, so real errors never reach the lossy path.

build.rs:9-19 is an explicit mapping table, and the finding itself states that all five `_json` fields and both `bytes` fields in the proto are covered (checked against agwp.proto lines 185, 588, 732, 1135, 1227, 1396, 1445). This is a maintainer convention for a repo-owned proto, with no runtime or operator impact, and the openapi.json sync test would show a missing mapping as a diff.

These are named, clamped server limits, not misleading behaviour. Several are already documented in the proto: heartbeat_ms '0 = 15000' and ttl_secs 'capped by server policy'. The MintCredential cap is configurable (cfg.auth.max_ttl_secs / max_agent_ttl_secs) and the error message states the maximum. Long-poll ceilings (30 s, 1 h claim lease) only shorten a wait. The one gap, that DiffRequest.context cannot be 0, is a minor API nit and does not mislead operators.

client_name and client_version are informational self-identification, like a User-Agent. The NegotiateRequest message makes no promise to track them, and ag-client sends them at lib.rs:207. Ignoring them in negotiate() does not affect correctness, security or any documented behaviour.

For the documented repo-pattern syntax (`*` wildcards, authz.rs:239), replacing '*' with 'x' yields a string the pattern always matches, so the repo test is a tautology and whoami effectively evaluates the subject match, which is the intended result. The heuristic would only misreport for undocumented glob metacharacters (`[`, `{`, `?`) in a repo pattern. That is a code-quality nit in how the effective-roles list is computed, not a protocol defect.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed: the proto (agwp.proto:927) and openapi.json:3852 say "stale", but reap_stale_runs writes "abandoned" (ag-agent/src/registry.rs:202), as do ag-storage meta/agents.rs:38 and the web RunsTable.vue:56. verdicts.reason: Core claim confirmed, though overstated on the "looks like a feature" part. The Conventions text (agwp.proto:12-20) lists SetPolicy as naturally idempotent, but set_policy (ag-integrate/src/admin.rs:278-293) always calls policy_put, which appends MAX(version)+1 (ag-storage records.rs:367-385). Attestations are bound to the exact policy_version (ag-policy/src/eval.rs:337), so a retry after a lost response silently invalidates validations. All 19 `idempotency_key` fields are in fact annotated "Accepted and ignored" in the proto (count verified), and the Conventions paragraph says to ask for the outcome rather than retry, so only the SetPolicy claim is factually wrong. The other repeat hazards (workspace modify, review, enqueue, provenance) are documented as non-deduplicating.

Update the proto comment for SetPolicyRequest.idempotency_key from "ignored" to honored. 2) Remove SetPolicy from the "naturally idempotent" list in the Conventions block (SetPolicy appends a version each time), and move it to the honored list. 3) Add duplicate-request tests over HTTP and gRPC asserting a single policy version for a repeated key, and `idempotency_key_reused` for a different document. Honoring the key on the other ignored operations is optional and separate.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed on a production path. predict() (ag-agent/src/predict.rs:59-80) calls `ancestors(..., WALK_LIMIT=50_000)` for the stream head and for every open proposal head, and `ancestors` returns DagError::LimitExceeded once the limit is passed (ag-dag/src/lib.rs:118-128). That error is mapped to MetaError::Invalid, so predict fails for any repository with more than 50k ancestors. It is reached from the server (api/agents.rs:338-343, gRPC grpc.rs:473) and the CLI `ag predict` (cmds/agents.rs:469). The cost is also O(total history) per proposal, although only the divergence matters.
verdicts.refined_fix: Add a divergence primitive to ag-dag and use it in predict. In crates/ag-dag/src/lib.rs add `pub fn divergence<G: Graph + ?Sized>(g: &G, a: &ChangesetId, b: &ChangesetId, limit: usize) -> Result<(Vec<ChangesetId>, Vec<ChangesetId>), DagError>`, returning (only_a, only_b). Use the same generation-ordered heap and P1/P2/STALE flags as merge_bases (lib.rs:185-217): pop in descending generation; a node popped with flags exactly P1 goes to only_a, exactly P2 goes to only_b, and P1|P2 becomes STALE and propagates; stop when every queued node is STALE. This is correct because a node is popped only after all of its children (strictly higher generation) have propagated their flags. Return LimitExceeded only if |only_a|+|only_b| > limit (a divergence cap, e.g. 50_000). In predict.rs drop head_ancestors and the per-proposal full walks, and compute `(mine, theirs) = divergence(tx as &dyn Graph, &p.head, &head, CAP)` per proposal, so cost is proportional to the divergence. Add a test with more than 50k shared changesets and a small divergence that asserts success (ag-dag test plus the ag-agent predict test).

verdicts.reason: Confirmed: predict.rs:71-72 calls `tx.proposals_list(Some("open"), 1000)` (records.rs:227-233: `ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 1000`) and only then filters `p.stream == stream` in Rust. In a repository with more than 1000 open proposals across streams, the oldest open proposals of the target stream are silently dropped, so overlaps are missed with no error or flag. It is reachable via the server predict handler and the CLI.
verdicts.refined_fix: In crates/ag-storage/src/meta/records.rs add `pub fn proposals_for_stream(&self, state: &str, stream: &str, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<ProposalRow>, MetaError>` implemented with `self.proposals_where("state = ?1 AND stream = ?2 ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT ?3", &params![state, stream, limit as i64])`. In predict.rs use `tx.proposals_for_stream("open", stream, MAX_PREDICT_PROPOSALS)` with a named constant (for example 5000) and a `truncated: bool` in Prediction when the result length equals the cap. Expose the flag as `PredictResponse.truncated` (additive proto field). Add a test with more than 1000 open proposals on other streams plus an overlapping pair on the target stream, asserting the overlap is found.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed: clip() (predict.rs:50-52) takes the first 20 paths, the struct doc admits "truncated to 20" (line 28), and the wire Overlap message (agwp.proto:1111-1115) has only a,b,kind,paths. The server copies paths unchanged (api/agents.rs:342-349), so a client cannot tell that paths were dropped or how many exist. It is on the production predict path.
verdicts.refined_fix: Name the constant (`const MAX_OVERLAP_PATHS: usize = 20;`) and make clip return `(Vec<String>, usize)` (the clipped paths and the total count). Add `total_paths: usize` to ag_agent::predict::Overlap and `uint32 total_paths = 5;` to the proto Overlap (additive; documented as "number of shared paths before truncation; > paths.len() means truncated"). Map it in api/agents.rs:342 and print `(+N more)` in the CLI predict output. Regenerate the schemas. Add a test with 25 shared paths asserting paths.len()==20 and total_paths==25. Making the cap request-controlled is optional.

verdicts.reason: The `else { continue }` branch (leases.rs:176) is unreachable from any production input. lease_insert has exactly one non-test caller, acquire (leases.rs:96), which first validates the scope with the identical `PathMatcher::new` (leases.rs:66). A stored scope therefore compiles unless the DB row is hand-corrupted or the glob crate retroactively rejects syntax it accepted before. The finding itself concedes the scopes are validated at acquire. It is a hypothetical defense-in-depth gap, not a reachable defect.

Confirmed on a production path. acquire() (leases.rs:74-81) refuses an exclusive lease when scopes_may_overlap(&l.scope, scope) is true for another holder's exclusive lease. That function (leases.rs:46-49) compares literal prefixes only, so `src/**/*.md` and `src/**/*.rs` (both prefix `src/`) or `src/lib.rs` against `src/**/*.md` are reported as overlapping and the second exclusive lease is refused with lease_conflict (AcquireLease in api/agents.rs:242). It is documented as conservative and is safe, but it wrongly blocks legitimate leases.
verdicts.refined_fix: Keep the conservative contract but sharpen it with sound disjointness proofs in crates/ag-agent/src/leases.rs. (a) If one side has no glob metacharacters (none of `*?[]{}\`), the overlap is exactly `PathMatcher::new(std::slice::from_ref(other)).map(|m| m.is_match(literal)).unwrap_or(true)`. (b) For glob-vs-glob add a literal-suffix test: `fn literal_suffix(g:&str)->&str` returns the text after the last of `*?[]{}\` (empty if none or the glob ends in a metacharacter). If both suffixes are non-empty and neither `sa.ends_with(sb)` nor `sb.ends_with(sa)`, return false, because both suffixes must be suffixes of the same path. Then fall back to the existing prefix test. Add unit tests: `src/**/*.md` vs `src/**/*.rs` is false, `src/lib.rs` vs `src/**/*.md` is false, `src/**` vs `src/lib.rs` is true, `**/*.rs` vs `src/lib.rs` is true, and `**/*.rs` vs `src/**/*.rs` is true. Add a proptest against brute-force matching over generated paths (never false when a common path exists).

verdicts.reason: MAX_TTL_MS (leases.rs:27) is a named public protocol bound whose value is stated in the rejection message (`ttl must be between 1 ms and 86400000 ms`), not a placeholder or fake value; the same 24 h scale appears elsewhere in the project (e.g. orchestrator lease_ttl validation). It is enforced consistently in acquire and extend. Not being operator-tunable and missing from the proto comment is a minor doc preference, not a hardcode-posing-as-real defect.

verdicts.reason: Narrowed to a doc-versus-code mismatch. Confirmed: App::negotiate (ag-server/src/api/session.rs:13-49) reads only supported_versions and features. client_name and client_version are never read, logged or counted anywhere in ag-server (grep finds them only in ag-client/src/lib.rs:207-208, which sends them), and the proto fields have no comment. They are accepted and ignored on a production endpoint.
verdicts.refined_fix: In App::negotiate emit a bounded, sanitized log line: `tracing::debug!(client_name = %clip(&req.client_name, 64), client_version = %clip(&req.client_version, 32), "negotiate")`, where clip truncates and strips control characters. Do not make client_name a metric label, because Negotiate needs no credentials and a client-controlled label is a cardinality attack. Document in the proto that these fields are informational and logged. Add a test using tracing-test (or a captured subscriber) asserting that the fields are logged and truncated; alternatively remove the two fields from the proto and clients.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed: Whoami (ag-server/src/api/session.rs:56-60) checks each binding by calling `Authorizer::roles(p, [b], &b.repo.replace('*', "x"))`, which then runs glob_match(&b.repo, sample_repo) (authz.rs:342-346). It is correct only for patterns whose sole metacharacter is `*`. grant_role (api/admin.rs:328-344, control.rs:269) stores any string and glob_match uses full globset syntax, so a binding such as `{acme,beta}/web` or `[ab]*` is effective in Authorizer::check but is replaced by a sample that it does not match, and whoami omits it from Principal.roles. The result is an inaccurate informational field (production route and used by the web WhoamiCard).
verdicts.refined_fix: In crates/ag-server/src/authz.rs extract the subject test from Authorizer::roles into `pub fn binding_applies(principal:&Principal, b:&Binding)->bool { let ident=principal.identity.as_str(); let base=principal.identity.principal(); glob_match(&b.subject, ident) || glob_match(&b.subject, base.as_str()) || principal.groups.iter().any(|g| b.subject == format!("group:{g}")) }`, and use it inside roles(). In session.rs whoami replace the sample-repo call with `if Authorizer::binding_applies(p, b) { roles.push(format!("{}:{}", b.repo, b.role.as_str())); }`. Keep the group_roles and bootstrap handling as is. Add tests for exact, prefix `acme/*`, `*`, `{a,b}/x`, `[ab]*` and group-subject bindings.
